questions.stem: Grandfather thanked his son politely for the smartphone and put it in a drawer. This shows that he
options: was saving the phone for a grandchild
was courteous but preferred his old radio
was angry with his son for wasting money
did not know how to open the box
questions.explanation: He thanked his son "politely", so he was not rude, but by putting the phone away and patting the wooden box he showed which he valued more.

whyNot.D: Nothing suggests he could not use or open it.
whyNot.C: "Politely" rules out open anger.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.context:

questions.stem: Why did the writer's father bring the radio home even though it could not be repaired?
options: He wanted to sell it as an antique
He hoped to find the parts later
The repairer refused to keep it
questions.explanation: The radio no longer worked, so its value was sentimental: it had been Grandfather's companion every evening, and returning it to its shelf keeps his memory alive.

whyNot.B: The repairer said the parts had not been made for forty years, so this hope is not suggested.
whyNot.A: He put it back on its shelf; nothing suggests selling it.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.context:

questions.stem: The passage ends: "where it still sits, silent, every evening at seven." What is the effect of this ending?
options: It recalls Grandfather's habit and creates a sense of loss
It shows that the family no longer listens to the news
It explains why the uncle's gift was useless
It suggests that the radio might work again one day
questions.explanation: Seven o'clock was when Grandfather turned on the news. The radio now sits "silent" at that hour, which reminds the reader of the old man's routine and of his absence.

whyNot.B: The ending is about the radio and Grandfather, not the family's news habits.
whyNot.D: The repairer said it could not be fixed; "silent" stresses this.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The manager gave a VAGUE answer to the workers' questions.
questions.explanation: A vague answer is one that is not clear or definite. The nearest meaning is "unclear".

whyNot.C: A vague answer may be honest or not; "vague" is about clarity.
whyNot.A: Speed has nothing to do with vagueness.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The commissioner's visit was meant to PACIFY the angry youths.
questions.explanation: To pacify is to make angry or upset people calm. The nearest meaning is "calm".

whyNot.D: "Provoke" means to make angrier, nearly the opposite.
whyNot.A: He may address them, but "pacify" names the aim: calming them.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: Despite the warnings, the driver remained OBSTINATE.
questions.explanation: "Obstinate" means refusing to change one's opinion or behaviour despite warnings. The nearest meaning is "stubborn".

whyNot.A: A careful driver would heed the warnings.
whyNot.B: "Silent" says nothing about refusing to change.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The businessman was known for his GENEROSITY.
questions.explanation: Generosity is readiness to give freely. Its opposite is meanness: unwillingness to give or share.

whyNot.C: "Kindness" is close in meaning to generosity.
whyNot.B: Wealth is having money, not an attitude to giving it.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The editor rejected the article because it was BIASED.
questions.explanation: "Biased" means unfairly favouring one side. The opposite is "objective": based on facts and not influenced by personal feelings.

whyNot.A: "Unfair" is close in meaning to biased.
whyNot.B: "Prejudiced" is also close in meaning.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The army won a DECISIVE victory in the first battle.
questions.explanation: A decisive victory settles the matter clearly. The opposite is "inconclusive": not leading to a clear result.

whyNot.D: "Final" is close in meaning to decisive here.
whyNot.A: "Quick" is about speed; a decisive victory can be slow.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Either the students or the teacher ___ to blame for the broken window.
questions.explanation: With "either … or", the verb agrees with the nearer subject. The nearer subject is "the teacher" (singular), so the verb is "is".

whyNot.A: "Are" agrees with "students", but that is the farther subject.
whyNot.B: "Have to blame" changes the meaning and is plural.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The police ___ arrested the suspects in connection with the robbery.
questions.explanation: "Police" is a plural noun in English (like "cattle"), so it takes a plural verb: "The police have arrested…".

whyNot.C: "Has" treats "police" as singular, a common error.
whyNot.A: "Was arrested" would make the police the ones arrested.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: We ___ in this house in Owerri since 2015.
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and continues to now, marked by "since", takes the present perfect: "We have lived here since 2015."

whyNot.B: The simple present cannot be used with "since 2015".
whyNot.C: The simple past suggests the living has ended, which clashes with "in this house" and "since".

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Chidi is very fond ___ his grandmother.
questions.explanation: The adjective "fond" is always followed by the preposition "of": "fond of someone or something".

whyNot.D: "Fond with" is a common error.
whyNot.A: "Fond for" is not standard English.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: The football match was CALLED OFF because of the heavy rain. This means that the match was
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb "call off" means to cancel something that was planned.

whyNot.A: A shortened match still took place; "called off" means it did not.
whyNot.C: "Called" here does not mean announced.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Halima TAKES AFTER her mother. This means that Halima
options: was born after her mother left
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb "take after" means to resemble an older family member in looks or character.

whyNot.C: "Looks after" means to care for someone.
whyNot.A: The phrasal verb has nothing to do with following.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Some people describe the new tax law as A DOUBLE-EDGED SWORD. This means that the law
options: has both good and bad effects
punishes people twice for the same offence
was passed twice by the assembly
is too harsh to be obeyed
questions.explanation: A double-edged sword cuts both ways. The idiom describes something that brings both advantages and disadvantages.

whyNot.B: The idiom is not about double punishment.
whyNot.D: "Sword" does not suggest harshness here; the point is the two edges.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Nobody came to the party, ___?
questions.explanation: "Nobody" makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive. Indefinite pronouns like nobody and everybody are picked up by "they" in tags: "Nobody came, did they?"

whyNot.B: A negative tag after a negative statement is wrong.
whyNot.C: "Wasn't it?" does not match the verb "came" or the subject; it is a common error.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Which of the following is the passive form of "The farmers harvested the maize"?
options: The farmers were harvested by the maize.
The maize is harvesting by the farmers.
The maize has harvested the farmers.
The maize was harvested by the farmers.
questions.explanation: In the passive, the object (the maize) becomes the subject, the verb becomes "be" + past participle in the same tense (was harvested), and the doer follows "by".

whyNot.C: This makes the maize the doer and is not passive.
whyNot.A: This reverses who did what.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Unless you hurry, you ___ the last bus to Onitsha.
questions.explanation: "Unless" means "if not". This is an open condition about a real future possibility, so it takes the present tense in the "unless" clause and "will" in the main clause.

whyNot.B: "Would miss" goes with an unreal condition in the past tense ("Unless you hurried…").
whyNot.D: "Would have missed" refers to the past.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the correctly spelt word to complete the sentence: The match will ___ start at four o'clock.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is d-e-f-i-n-i-t-e-l-y: it is built from "definite" + "-ly", so it keeps "finite" in the middle.

whyNot.A: "Definately" is the most common error; there is no "a".
whyNot.C: "Definitly" drops the "e" of "definite".

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Which of the following words has the same vowel sound as "law"?
questions.explanation: "Daughter" is /ˈdɔːtə/: the "augh" gives /ɔː/, the same long vowel as in "law" /lɔː/.

whyNot.A: "Doubt" has /aʊ/.
whyNot.D: "Dot" has the short /ɒ/.
whyNot.B: "Dough" has /əʊ/.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the word that contains the short vowel /ʌ/ heard in "love" and "son".
questions.explanation: "Oven" is /ˈʌvn/: the "o" is pronounced /ʌ/, as in "love", "son" and "cup".

whyNot.D: "Over" is /ˈəʊvə/.
whyNot.A: "Often" has /ɒ/.
whyNot.B: "Own" is /əʊn/.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Which of the following words has the same vowel sound as "car"?
questions.explanation: "Calm" is /kɑːm/: the "l" is silent and the vowel is /ɑː/, as in "car" /kɑː/.

whyNot.A: "Cold" has /əʊ/.
whyNot.B: "Come" has /ʌ/.
whyNot.C: "Call" has /ɔː/.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Which of the following words contains the long vowel /uː/, as in "food"?
questions.explanation: "Fruit" is /fruːt/, with the long vowel /uː/.

whyNot.B: "Foot" has the short /ʊ/.
whyNot.C: "Full" has /ʊ/.
whyNot.D: "Fun" has /ʌ/.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Which of the following words contains the diphthong /ɔɪ/, as in "boy"?
questions.explanation: "Choice" is /tʃɔɪs/: the "oi" spelling gives /ɔɪ/.

whyNot.C: "Chose" has /əʊ/.
whyNot.D: "Chase" has /eɪ/.
whyNot.A: "Cheese" has /iː/.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Which of the following words has the same vowel sound as "square"?
questions.explanation: "Scarce" is /skeəs/, with the diphthong /eə/ as in "square" /skweə/, even though it is spelt like "scar".

whyNot.A: "Scar" is /skɑː/.
whyNot.B: "Score" is /skɔː/.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: In which of the following words does "ch" represent the sound /ʃ/?
questions.explanation: "Brochure" (from French) is /ˈbrəʊʃə/: the "ch" is pronounced /ʃ/, as in "machine".

whyNot.D: "Church" has /tʃ/.
whyNot.A: "Chemist" has /k/.
whyNot.C: "Choose" has /tʃ/.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Which of the following words contains the consonant sound /dʒ/?
questions.explanation: "Soldier" is /ˈsəʊldʒə/: the "di" before a vowel is pronounced /dʒ/, as in "judge".

whyNot.B: "Goat" begins with /ɡ/.
whyNot.D: "Guess" begins with /ɡ/; the "u" is silent.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Which of the following words begins with the consonant sound /j/, as in "yes"?
questions.explanation: "University" is /ˌjuːnɪˈvɜːsəti/: it begins with /j/, which is why we say "a university", not "an university".

whyNot.B: "Umbrella" begins with the vowel /ʌ/.
whyNot.C: "Usher" begins with the vowel /ʌ/.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: In which of the following words does "gh" represent the sound /f/?
questions.explanation: "Rough" is /rʌf/: the "gh" is pronounced /f/, as in "enough" and "cough".

whyNot.B: In "though" the "gh" is silent.
whyNot.C: In "night" the "gh" is silent.
whyNot.D: In "ghost" the "gh" is /ɡ/.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: In which of the following words is the final "n" silent?
questions.explanation: "Autumn" is /ˈɔːtəm/: after "m" at the end of a word, "n" is silent, as in "column" and "hymn".

whyNot.C: "Again" ends in /n/.
whyNot.A: "Human" ends in /n/.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: In which of the following words is the letter "t" silent?
questions.explanation: "Castle" is /ˈkɑːsl/: the "t" after "s" before "-le" is silent, as in "whistle" and "wrestle".

whyNot.A: "Pattern" has /t/.
whyNot.B: "Mistake" has /t/.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: In which of the following words is the "-ed" ending pronounced /d/?
questions.explanation: After a voiced sound other than /d/, "-ed" is pronounced /d/. "Rob" ends in the voiced /b/, so "robbed" is /rɒbd/.

whyNot.B: "Jumped" ends in /t/ (after voiceless /p/).
whyNot.C: "Wanted" ends in /ɪd/ (after /t/).
whyNot.D: "Pushed" ends in /t/ (after voiceless /ʃ/).

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Choose the word that is stressed on the first syllable.
questions.explanation: "Industry" is IN-dus-try, /ˈɪndəstri/. "Indeed", "inform" and "intend" are all stressed on the second syllable.

whyNot.D: "Indeed" is in-DEED.
whyNot.A: "Inform" is in-FORM.
whyNot.B: "Intend" is in-TEND.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: Which of the following words is stressed on the third syllable: politician, political, politics or policy?
questions.explanation: "Politician" is po-li-TI-cian: words ending in -ian are stressed on the syllable just before the ending.

whyNot.D: "Political" is po-LI-ti-cal, stressed on the second.
whyNot.C: "Politics" is PO-li-tics, stressed on the first.
whyNot.B: "Policy" is PO-li-cy, stressed on the first.

questions.subject: english-language
questions.stem: "You haven't seen my keys, have you?" If the speaker says the question tag with a rising tune, the speaker
options: is certain the listener has the keys
is genuinely unsure and is asking for information
is ordering the listener to find the keys
questions.explanation: A rising tune on a question tag makes it a real question: the speaker does not know and wants an answer. A falling tune would show the speaker expects agreement.

whyNot.B: Certainty is shown by a falling tune on the tag.
whyNot.A: A rising tag invites an answer.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Evaluate 1011₂ + 111₂, giving your answer in base two.
questions.explanation: Convert to base ten: 1011₂ = 8 + 2 + 1 = 11 and 111₂ = 4 + 2 + 1 = 7. Their sum is 18. In base two, 18 = 16 + 2 = 10010₂. (Adding column by column with carries gives the same result.)

whyNot.B: 1122₂ adds the digits without carrying; the digit 2 cannot appear in base two.
whyNot.D: 10110₂ equals 22, not 18.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Evaluate (2.4 × 10⁵) × (5 × 10⁻³), giving your answer in standard form.
questions.explanation: Multiply the numbers and add the powers: 2.4 × 5 = 12 and 10⁵ × 10⁻³ = 10². So the product is 12 × 10² = 1.2 × 10 × 10² = 1.2 × 10³.

whyNot.D: 1.2 × 10² forgets that changing 12 to 1.2 adds one to the power of ten.
whyNot.A: 12 × 10² has the right value but is not in standard form, since 12 is not between 1 and 10.
whyNot.B: 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ multiplies the powers (5 × −3) instead of adding them.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the value of 17 × 8 in modulo 7.
questions.explanation: 17 × 8 = 136. Divide by 7: 7 × 19 = 133, so 136 = 133 + 3 and the remainder is 3. (Or reduce first: 17 ≡ 3 and 8 ≡ 1 (mod 7), so 17 × 8 ≡ 3 × 1 = 3.)

whyNot.B: 4 adds instead of multiplying: 17 + 8 = 25 = 21 + 4.
whyNot.C: 1 is 8 reduced modulo 7; the 17 must also be reduced and multiplied in.
whyNot.D: 6 is the last digit of 136, its remainder on dividing by 10, not by 7.

whyNot.B: 8 takes 4^(−1/2) as 2 instead of 1/2 (ignoring the negative index).
whyNot.D: 4 is only the first factor, 8^(2/3).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Given that log₁₀ 2 = 0.3010 and log₁₀ 3 = 0.4771, find log₁₀ 12.

whyNot.A: 0.7781 is log 2 + log 3 = log 6; 12 needs two factors of 2.
whyNot.D: 0.9030 is 3 log 2 = log 8.
whyNot.B: 1.2552 is log 2 + 2 log 3 = log 18.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.explanation: This is a difference of two squares: (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b². Here a² = (2√3)² = 4 × 3 = 12 and b² = (√2)² = 2. So the product is 12 − 2 = 10.

whyNot.D: 14 adds the squares (12 + 2) instead of subtracting them.
whyNot.B: 4√3 adds the two brackets instead of multiplying them.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A shop in Onitsha raised the price of a ₦5,000 shirt by 20%. A month later it reduced the new price by 20%. What is the final price?
questions.explanation: After the rise: 5,000 × 1.2 = ₦6,000. The 20% reduction is on ₦6,000: 6,000 × 0.8 = ₦4,800. The two changes do not cancel because they are percentages of different amounts.

whyNot.B: ₦5,000 assumes a 20% rise and a 20% fall cancel out; the fall is taken from the larger price.
whyNot.D: ₦4,000 takes 20% off the original ₦5,000 and ignores the rise.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: In a class of 50 students, 30 offer Physics, 25 offer Chemistry and 8 offer neither subject. How many students offer both Physics and Chemistry?
questions.explanation: Students offering at least one subject = 50 − 8 = 42. By n(P ∪ C) = n(P) + n(C) − n(P ∩ C): 42 = 30 + 25 − n(P ∩ C), so n(P ∩ C) = 55 − 42 = 13.

whyNot.A: 5 is 55 − 50: it forgets to remove the 8 students who offer neither.
whyNot.B: 17 is the number who offer Physics only (30 − 13).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A car bought for ₦4,000,000 depreciates at 10% per annum, each year's loss being 10% of its value at the start of that year. Find its value after 3 years.
questions.explanation: Each year the value is multiplied by 0.9. After 3 years: 4,000,000 × 0.9³ = 4,000,000 × 0.729 = ₦2,916,000.

whyNot.C: ₦2,800,000 takes 10% of the original price off every year (straight-line), not 10% of the current value.
whyNot.D: ₦3,240,000 is the value after only 2 years.
whyNot.B: ₦1,200,000 is the total loss under straight-line depreciation, not the value.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Express the recurring decimal 0.272727… as a fraction in its lowest terms.
questions.explanation: Let x = 0.2727… . The block '27' has two digits, so multiply by 100: 100x = 27.2727… . Subtract: 99x = 27, so x = 27/99 = 3/11.

whyNot.B: 27/100 = 0.27 exactly; it ignores the repeating digits.
whyNot.C: 27/90 subtracts 10x instead of 100x, which does not cancel a two-digit repeating block.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Solve the simultaneous equations 3x + 2y = 7 and 5x − 2y = 9.
questions.explanation: Add the equations to eliminate y: 8x = 16, so x = 2. Substitute in the first: 6 + 2y = 7, so 2y = 1 and y = 1/2. Check in the second: 10 − 1 = 9 ✓.

whyNot.D: x = 1, y = 2 satisfies 3x + 2y = 7 but gives 5 − 4 = 1, not 9, in the second equation.
whyNot.B: x = 2, y = 1 gives 6 + 2 = 8, not 7, in the first equation.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Evaluate the determinant of the matrix with rows (3, −2) and (4, 1).
questions.explanation: For a 2 × 2 matrix with rows (a, b) and (c, d), the determinant is ad − bc. Here ad − bc = (3)(1) − (−2)(4) = 3 + 8 = 11.

whyNot.B: −5 is 3 − 8: it forgets that subtracting (−2)(4) = −8 means adding 8.
whyNot.A: −11 is bc − ad, the products in the wrong order.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the sum to infinity of the geometric progression 12, 6, 3, …
questions.explanation: The first term is a = 12 and the common ratio is r = 6/12 = 1/2. Since |r| < 1, S∞ = a/(1 − r) = 12/(1/2) = 24.

whyNot.A: 21 just adds the three terms shown; the terms go on forever.
whyNot.B: 18 uses a(1 + r) instead of a/(1 − r).
whyNot.D: 36 divides by 1 − 2/3, using the wrong ratio.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: If f(x) = 3x − 2 and g(x) = x², find g(f(2)).
questions.explanation: Work from the inside out. f(2) = 3(2) − 2 = 4. Then g(4) = 4² = 16.

whyNot.A: 10 is f(g(2)) = 3(4) − 2: the functions are applied in the wrong order.
whyNot.C: 4 is only f(2); g has not yet been applied.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: If A is the matrix with rows (2, 1) and (3, 4), find the determinant of 2A.
questions.explanation: det A = (2)(4) − (1)(3) = 5. 2A has rows (4, 2) and (6, 8), so det 2A = 32 − 12 = 20. In general, for a 2 × 2 matrix, det(kA) = k² det A = 4 × 5 = 20.

whyNot.D: 10 multiplies the determinant by 2 only; each of the two rows is doubled, so the factor is 2² = 4.
whyNot.C: 5 is the determinant of A itself.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A binary operation ∗ is defined on the real numbers by a ∗ b = a + b − 2ab. Find 3 ∗ (−1).

whyNot.B: −4 treats −2ab as −2 × 3 = −6 and ignores the sign of b: 2 − 6 = −4.
whyNot.D: 4 drops the sign of b in the first part (3 + 1) and ignores −2ab.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the remainder when x³ − 2x² + 3x − 5 is divided by x − 2.
questions.explanation: By the remainder theorem, the remainder on dividing by (x − 2) is the value of the polynomial at x = 2: 8 − 8 + 6 − 5 = 1.

whyNot.A: −27 is the value at x = −2; dividing by x − 2 means substituting x = +2.
whyNot.D: −5 is just the constant term, the value at x = 0.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: If α and β are the roots of 2x² − 6x + 3 = 0, find the value of α² + β².
questions.explanation: α + β = −b/a = 6/2 = 3 and αβ = c/a = 3/2. Then α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ = 9 − 3 = 6.

whyNot.A: 12 uses (α + β)² + 2αβ, adding instead of subtracting.
whyNot.C: 9 is (α + β)², which still contains the 2αβ term.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the range of values of x for which x² − x − 6 < 0.
questions.explanation: Factorise: x² − x − 6 = (x − 3)(x + 2). The product is negative when the factors have opposite signs, which happens between the roots −2 and 3. So −2 < x < 3. (Test x = 0: −6 < 0 ✓.)

whyNot.D: x < −2 or x > 3 is where the expression is positive.
whyNot.B: −3 < x < 2 uses the roots with the wrong signs; (x + 3)(x − 2) is x² + x − 6.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: y is partly constant and partly varies as x. When x = 1, y = 7 and when x = 3, y = 13. Find y when x = 5.
questions.explanation: Write y = a + bx. Then a + b = 7 and a + 3b = 13. Subtracting: 2b = 6, so b = 3 and a = 4. When x = 5, y = 4 + 3(5) = 19.

whyNot.C: 35 treats y as varying directly with x only (y = 7x).
whyNot.B: 21 adds the 4 from b and a wrongly (4 + 3 × 5 + 2).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the midpoint of the line segment joining (−3, 5) and (7, −1).

whyNot.D: (5, −3) halves the differences, (7 − (−3))/2 and (−1 − 5)/2, instead of the sums.
whyNot.A: (4, 4) adds the coordinates but forgets to divide by 2.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the equation of the straight line with gradient 3 that passes through the point (1, 2).
questions.explanation: Use y − y₁ = m(x − x₁): y − 2 = 3(x − 1), so y = 3x − 3 + 2 = 3x − 1. Check: at x = 1, y = 2 ✓.

whyNot.C: y = 3x + 2 uses the y-coordinate of the point as the intercept; at x = 1 it gives 5, not 2.
whyNot.A: y = 3x + 1 gives y = 4 at x = 1.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: P and Q are two fixed points. What is the locus of a point that moves so that it is always equidistant from P and Q?
options: A circle with centre at the midpoint of PQ and radius PQ
A line through P parallel to PQ
questions.explanation: Every point on the perpendicular bisector of PQ is the same distance from P as from Q, and no other point is. So the locus is the perpendicular bisector of PQ.

whyNot.A: A point on the circle with diameter PQ is generally closer to one of P and Q than to the other; that circle is the locus of points where angle PXQ = 90°.
whyNot.C: Points on a line through P are at different distances from P and Q.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the gradient of a line perpendicular to the line 2x + 3y = 6.
questions.explanation: Rewrite 2x + 3y = 6 as y = −(2/3)x + 2, so its gradient is −2/3. Perpendicular gradients multiply to −1, so the required gradient is −1 ÷ (−2/3) = 3/2.

whyNot.C: −2/3 is the gradient of the given line itself (that is for a parallel line).
whyNot.A: −3/2 takes the reciprocal but forgets to change the sign.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: TA and TB are tangents from an external point T to a circle with centre O, touching it at A and B. If angle ATB = 50°, find angle AOB.
questions.explanation: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so angles OAT and OBT are each 90°. The angles of quadrilateral OATB add up to 360°: angle AOB = 360° − 90° − 90° − 50° = 130°.

whyNot.D: 50° assumes angle AOB equals angle ATB; they are supplementary, not equal.
whyNot.A: 100° doubles angle ATB, using the angle-at-centre rule where it does not apply.
whyNot.B: 65° is half of 130°, the angle at the circumference on the major arc.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Two triangles are similar. A side of the smaller triangle is 4 cm and the corresponding side of the larger is 6 cm. If the area of the smaller triangle is 32 cm², find the area of the larger.
questions.explanation: For similar figures the ratio of areas is the square of the ratio of corresponding sides: (6/4)² = 9/4. Area of larger = 32 × 9/4 = 72 cm².

whyNot.C: 48 cm² multiplies by the length ratio 6/4 instead of its square.
whyNot.A: 108 cm² uses the cube of the ratio, which is for volumes.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Solve 2 sin θ − 1 = 0 for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°.
questions.explanation: 2 sin θ = 1, so sin θ = 1/2. Sine is positive in the first and second quadrants. The basic angle is 30°, so θ = 30° or 180° − 30° = 150°.

whyNot.B: sin 210° = −1/2; the third quadrant gives negative sines.
whyNot.D: 60° and 120° solve sin θ = √3/2, not 1/2.
whyNot.C: sin 330° = −1/2; 330° solves cos θ = √3/2 with 30°.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A rectangular box measures 3 cm by 4 cm by 12 cm. Find the length of the longest straight rod that fits inside it (the diagonal from one corner to the opposite corner).
questions.explanation: The diagonal of the base is √(3² + 4²) = 5 cm. The space diagonal is then √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 cm. (Directly: √(3² + 4² + 12²) = √169.)

whyNot.C: 5 cm is only the diagonal of the 3 cm by 4 cm face.
whyNot.A: 19 cm adds the three edges, but the shortest path from corner to corner is the straight diagonal.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: The sides of a triangle are 5 cm, 7 cm and 8 cm. Find the angle opposite the 7 cm side.

whyNot.C: 120° has cosine −1/2; it comes from subtracting 25 + 64 from 49 instead of the other way round.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A surveyor walks 8 km from P to Q on a bearing of 060°. How far east of P is Q?
questions.explanation: A bearing of 060° is measured clockwise from north, so the path makes 60° with north. The eastward distance is the side opposite this angle: 8 sin 60° = 8 × √3/2 = 4√3 km (about 6.93 km).

whyNot.A: 4 km = 8 cos 60° is the distance north of P, not east.
whyNot.D: 8√3 km forgets the 1/2 in sin 60° = √3/2.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find dy/dx if y = sin x − cos x.
questions.explanation: d/dx(sin x) = cos x and d/dx(cos x) = −sin x. So dy/dx = cos x − (−sin x) = cos x + sin x.

whyNot.B: cos x − sin x forgets that the derivative of cos x is −sin x, so subtracting it gives + sin x.
whyNot.D: −cos x + sin x is just the original function rearranged: sin x − cos x.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Differentiate y = 5/x² with respect to x.
questions.explanation: Write y = 5x⁻². Using d/dx(xⁿ) = nxⁿ⁻¹: dy/dx = 5 × (−2)x⁻³ = −10x⁻³ = −10/x³.

whyNot.D: 10/x³ drops the minus sign that comes from the negative power.
whyNot.B: −10/x reduces the power by 2 instead of 1 in the wrong direction.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Evaluate the definite integral ∫₁² 2x dx.
questions.explanation: ∫2x dx = x². Evaluate between the limits: [x²]₁² = 2² − 1² = 4 − 1 = 3.

whyNot.D: 4 is only the value at the upper limit; the value at x = 1 must be subtracted.
whyNot.A: 2 integrates 2x as if it were the constant 2: 2(2 − 1) = 2.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Differentiate y = (2x + 1)³ with respect to x.
questions.explanation: Use the chain rule. Let u = 2x + 1, so y = u³. dy/du = 3u² and du/dx = 2. dy/dx = 3u² × 2 = 6(2x + 1)².

whyNot.A: 3(2x + 1)² forgets to multiply by the derivative of the inside, 2.
whyNot.B: 6(2x + 1)³ does not reduce the power by one.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the area enclosed by the curve y = x², the x-axis and the lines x = 1 and x = 3.
questions.explanation: Area = ∫₁³ x² dx = [x³/3]₁³ = 27/3 − 1/3 = 26/3 = 8⅔ square units.

whyNot.C: 9 square units is only the value of x³/3 at the upper limit; the value at x = 1 must be subtracted.
whyNot.A: 8 square units is y(3) − y(1) = 9 − 1, which uses the curve instead of integrating it.
whyNot.D: 26 square units forgets to divide by 3 when integrating x².

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the x-coordinates of the stationary points of the curve y = x³ − 3x² − 9x + 2.
questions.explanation: At a stationary point dy/dx = 0. dy/dx = 3x² − 6x − 9 = 3(x² − 2x − 3) = 3(x − 3)(x + 1). So x = 3 or x = −1.

whyNot.A: x = 1 and x = −3 come from factorising x² − 2x − 3 with the signs reversed.
whyNot.C: x = 0 and x = 3 solve x² − 3x = 0, which leaves out the −9x term.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A particle moves in a straight line so that its displacement after t seconds is s = t³ − 4t² + 5t metres. Find its velocity when t = 2 s.
questions.explanation: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement: v = ds/dt = 3t² − 8t + 5. At t = 2: v = 12 − 16 + 5 = 1 m/s.

whyNot.D: 2 m/s is the displacement at t = 2 (8 − 16 + 10), not the velocity.
whyNot.A: 4 m/s is the acceleration at t = 2 (6t − 8).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve y = x² + 1 at the point (1, 2).
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 2x, so the gradient at x = 1 is 2. The tangent passes through (1, 2): y − 2 = 2(x − 1), giving y = 2x.

whyNot.C: y = 2x + 1 has the right gradient but gives y = 3 at x = 1, so it misses the point (1, 2).
whyNot.D: y = x + 1 uses gradient 1; the gradient is found by differentiating, not from the coefficient of x².

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Differentiate y = x² sin x with respect to x.
questions.explanation: Use the product rule: if y = uv then dy/dx = u′v + uv′. With u = x² (u′ = 2x) and v = sin x (v′ = cos x): dy/dx = 2x sin x + x² cos x.

whyNot.A: 2x cos x multiplies the two derivatives together, which is not the product rule.
whyNot.C: 2x sin x − x² cos x has the wrong sign: the derivative of sin x is +cos x.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: The radius of a circular ink stain grows at 0.5 cm per second. How fast is its area increasing when the radius is 4 cm?
questions.explanation: A = πr², so dA/dr = 2πr. By the chain rule dA/dt = (dA/dr)(dr/dt) = 2π(4)(0.5) = 4π cm²/s (about 12.6 cm²/s).

whyNot.B: 8π cm²/s is dA/dr at r = 4; it forgets to multiply by dr/dt = 0.5.
whyNot.A: 16π cm²/s is the area itself when r = 4, not its rate of change.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: In how many different ways can 4 students stand in a row for a photograph?
questions.explanation: There are 4 choices for the first place, 3 for the second, 2 for the third and 1 for the last: 4! = 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24.

whyNot.A: 16 = 4 × 4 allows the same student to stand in two places.
whyNot.B: 12 = 4 × 3 fills only the first two places.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: In how many ways can a committee of 3 be chosen from 7 people?
questions.explanation: Order does not matter in a committee, so use combinations: ⁷C₃ = 7!/(3! × 4!) = (7 × 6 × 5)/(3 × 2 × 1) = 210/6 = 35.

whyNot.D: 210 = ⁷P₃ counts ordered arrangements; the same three people in a different order form the same committee.
whyNot.C: 21 = ⁷C₂ chooses 2 people, not 3.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A bag contains 4 white, 5 black and 3 red marbles. One marble is picked at random. What is the probability that it is not black?
questions.explanation: There are 4 + 5 + 3 = 12 marbles, and 4 + 3 = 7 of them are not black. P(not black) = 7/12. (Or 1 − 5/12 = 7/12.)

whyNot.C: 5/12 is the probability that it IS black.
whyNot.B: 7/5 compares non-black to black marbles; a probability cannot exceed 1.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: In a survey of 45 students in Kaduna, 18 said football was their favourite sport. What angle represents football on a pie chart of the results?
questions.explanation: The angle is the fraction of the whole times 360°: (18/45) × 360° = 0.4 × 360° = 144°.

whyNot.A: 40° is the percentage (18/45 = 40%) written as degrees.
whyNot.C: 162° uses 18 × 9, the angle for 18 out of 40, not 45.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the variance of the numbers 3, 5 and 7.

whyNot.A: 4 divides the sum of squared deviations by n − 1 = 2 instead of n = 3.
whyNot.D: 4/3 is the mean deviation, the average of the absolute deviations 2, 0 and 2, not of their squares.
whyNot.C: √(8/3) is the standard deviation, the square root of the variance.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.context:
The number of goals scored by a school team in 20 matches is shown below.
Goals: 2, 3, 4, 5
Number of matches: 4, 6, 7, 3
questions.stem: Find the mean number of goals per match.

whyNot.D: 3.5 is the average of the four goal values 2, 3, 4, 5, ignoring the frequencies.
whyNot.C: 5 is the average of the frequencies (20 ÷ 4).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Three fair coins are tossed together. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
questions.explanation: There are 2³ = 8 equally likely outcomes. Only TTT has no head. P(at least one head) = 1 − P(no head) = 1 − 1/8 = 7/8.

whyNot.D: 1/8 is the probability of no head at all (or of three heads).
whyNot.B: 3/8 is the probability of exactly one head.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: How many different arrangements can be made from all the letters of the word ABUJA?
questions.explanation: ABUJA has 5 letters with A appearing twice. Number of arrangements = 5!/2! = 120/2 = 60. Dividing by 2! removes the repeats made by swapping the two As.

whyNot.B: 120 = 5! treats the two As as different letters.
whyNot.A: 24 = 4! uses only the 4 different letters.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Events A and B are independent, with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.5. Find P(A or B), the probability that at least one of them happens.
questions.explanation: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B). For independent events P(A ∩ B) = 0.4 × 0.5 = 0.2. So P(A ∪ B) = 0.4 + 0.5 − 0.2 = 0.7.

whyNot.A: 0.9 just adds the probabilities, which is right only for mutually exclusive events; independent events can happen together.
whyNot.C: 0.2 is P(A and B), not P(A or B).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A committee of 4 is to be made up of 2 boys and 2 girls chosen from 5 boys and 4 girls. In how many ways can this be done?
questions.explanation: Choose the boys: ⁵C₂ = 10 ways. Choose the girls: ⁴C₂ = 6 ways. Each choice of boys can go with each choice of girls, so the total is 10 × 6 = 60.

whyNot.A: 126 = ⁹C₄ chooses any 4 of the 9 children, ignoring the 2 boys and 2 girls condition.
whyNot.C: 16 adds the two counts (10 + 6) instead of multiplying them.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Convert 156 (base ten) to a number in base eight.
questions.explanation: Divide by 8 repeatedly: 156 ÷ 8 = 19 r 4, 19 ÷ 8 = 2 r 3, 2 ÷ 8 = 0 r 2. Reading the remainders from the bottom up gives 234₈. Check: 2 × 64 + 3 × 8 + 4 = 128 + 24 + 4 = 156.

whyNot.C: 432₈ reads the remainders from top to bottom; it equals 282.
whyNot.B: 324₈ equals 212, not 156.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Write 0.07846 correct to 2 significant figures.
questions.explanation: Leading zeros are not significant, so the first two significant figures are 7 and 8. The next digit is 4, which is less than 5, so we round down: 0.078.

whyNot.B: 0.079 rounds up although the next digit (4) is less than 5.
whyNot.C: 0.08 is correct to 1 significant figure (or 2 decimal places).
whyNot.A: 0.0785 has 3 significant figures.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the highest common factor (HCF) of 84 and 126.
questions.explanation: 84 = 2² × 3 × 7 and 126 = 2 × 3² × 7. The HCF takes the lowest power of each common prime: 2 × 3 × 7 = 42.

whyNot.A: 21 is a common factor but not the highest; 42 also divides both numbers.
whyNot.D: 252 is the LCM, the smallest number both divide into.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Share ₦72,000 among Ade, Bisi and Chuka in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. How much does Chuka get?
questions.explanation: The total number of parts is 2 + 3 + 4 = 9. One part is 72,000 ÷ 9 = ₦8,000. Chuka has 4 parts: 4 × 8,000 = ₦32,000.

whyNot.A: ₦24,000 is Bisi's share (3 parts).
whyNot.B: ₦28,800 divides by 10 parts instead of 9.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.explanation: 2⁰ = 1 (any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1). 4^(1/2) = √4 = 2. 8^(−1/3) = 1/∛8 = 1/2. The sum is 1 + 2 + 1/2 = 3½.

whyNot.D: 2½ takes 2⁰ as 0 instead of 1.
whyNot.C: 5 takes 8^(−1/3) as 2, ignoring the negative index.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Simplify log₁₀ 24 − log₁₀ 3 + log₁₀ 125.
questions.explanation: Combine using log a − log b = log(a/b) and log a + log b = log(ab): log(24 ÷ 3 × 125) = log(8 × 125) = log₁₀ 1000 = 3, since 10³ = 1000.

whyNot.D: 146 adds and subtracts the numbers themselves (24 − 3 + 125) and drops the logarithm.
whyNot.B: log₁₀ 146 wrongly turns subtraction and addition of logs into subtraction and addition of the numbers.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A trader in Aba bought 50 tubers of yam at ₦1,200 each and sold all of them at ₦1,500 each. Find her percentage profit.
questions.explanation: Profit on each tuber = 1,500 − 1,200 = ₦300. Percentage profit = (profit ÷ cost price) × 100 = (300 ÷ 1,200) × 100 = 25%. (Using totals: 15,000 ÷ 60,000 × 100 gives the same.)

whyNot.B: 20% divides the profit by the selling price (300 ÷ 1,500) instead of the cost price.
whyNot.D: 300% treats the ₦300 profit itself as a percentage.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Expand and simplify (√3 + 1)².

whyNot.A: 4 squares each term separately (3 + 1) and leaves out the middle term 2ab.
whyNot.B: 3 + 2√3 forgets the 1² at the end.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.explanation: 0.25 = 1/4, so (1/4)^(−3/2) = 4^(3/2). The negative index turns the fraction upside down. Then 4^(3/2) = (√4)³ = 2³ = 8.

whyNot.D: 1/8 forgets that the negative index means taking the reciprocal.
whyNot.A: −8: a negative index does not make the answer negative.
whyNot.B: 4 only flips 1/4 and ignores the power 3/2.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A number is increased by 25% and the result is then decreased by 20%. The final result is 600. Find the original number.
questions.explanation: Let the number be x. After the increase: 1.25x. After the decrease: 0.8 × 1.25x = 1.0x. So the two changes cancel exactly, x = 600.

whyNot.D: 630 assumes the changes leave a net 5% change, adding 5% back to 600.
whyNot.B: 500 undoes only the 25% increase (600 ÷ 1.2), not both changes.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Factorise x² − 7x + 12.
questions.explanation: Find two numbers that multiply to +12 and add to −7: they are −3 and −4. So x² − 7x + 12 = (x − 3)(x − 4).

whyNot.A: (x + 3)(x + 4) gives +7x, not −7x.
whyNot.C: (x − 2)(x − 6) gives −8x as the middle term.
whyNot.D: (x − 3)(x + 4) gives x² + x − 12.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Expand (3x − 2)(x + 5).
questions.explanation: Multiply each term: 3x × x = 3x², 3x × 5 = 15x, −2 × x = −2x, −2 × 5 = −10. Collect: 3x² + 15x − 2x − 10 = 3x² + 13x − 10.

whyNot.A: 3x² − 13x − 10 has the wrong sign on the middle term.
whyNot.C: 3x² + 17x − 10 adds 2x instead of subtracting it.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Make t the subject of the formula v = u + at.
questions.explanation: Subtract u from both sides: v − u = at. Divide both sides by a: t = (v − u)/a.

whyNot.C: (u − v)/a has the subtraction the wrong way round, giving the negative of t.
whyNot.D: a(v − u) multiplies by a instead of dividing.
whyNot.A: v − u − a subtracts a, but a multiplies t, so we must divide by it.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Solve the equation x/3 − (x − 1)/4 = 1.
questions.explanation: Multiply every term by 12: 4x − 3(x − 1) = 12, so 4x − 3x + 3 = 12, giving x + 3 = 12 and x = 9. Check: 9/3 − 8/4 = 3 − 2 = 1 ✓.

whyNot.D: x = 15 comes from −3(x − 1) = −3x − 3, getting the sign of the 3 wrong.
whyNot.B: x = 11 forgets to multiply the −1 in the bracket by 3: 4x − 3x + 1 = 12.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Simplify 1/(x − 1) − 1/(x + 1).
questions.explanation: Use the common denominator (x − 1)(x + 1) = x² − 1: [(x + 1) − (x − 1)]/(x² − 1) = (x + 1 − x + 1)/(x² − 1) = 2/(x² − 1).

whyNot.A: −2/(x² − 1) subtracts the numerators in the wrong order.
whyNot.C: 2x/(x² − 1) is the sum of the two fractions, not the difference.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Solve x² − 4x + 1 = 0, leaving your answer in surd form.

whyNot.A: 4 ± √3 forgets to divide the whole numerator by 2a = 2.
whyNot.B: 2 ± √5 uses b² + 4ac = 20 inside the root.
whyNot.C: −2 ± √3 uses +b instead of −b.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the nth term of the arithmetic progression 5, 9, 13, 17, …
questions.explanation: Here a = 5 and d = 4. Tₙ = a + (n − 1)d = 5 + 4(n − 1) = 4n + 1. Check: n = 1 gives 5 and n = 3 gives 13 ✓.

whyNot.C: 4n + 5 gives 9 as the first term; it uses a + nd instead of a + (n − 1)d.
whyNot.D: 5n + 4 swaps the first term and the common difference.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Solve the simultaneous equations y = x + 1 and x² + y² = 25.

whyNot.D: (4, 3) and (−3, −4) lie on the circle but not on y = x + 1 (for (4, 3), x + 1 = 5, not 3).
whyNot.A: (4, 3) does not satisfy y = x + 1.
whyNot.B: (−3, −2) and (4, 5) lie on the line but not on the circle: 9 + 4 ≠ 25.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: The sum of the first n terms of the arithmetic progression 2, 5, 8, … is 155. Find n.

whyNot.A: 11 terms give S₁₁ = (11/2)(4 + 30) = 187, which is too many.
whyNot.B: 9 terms give S₉ = (9/2)(4 + 24) = 126, which is too few.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: y varies inversely as the square root of x. When x = 4, y = 6. Find x when y = 3.
questions.explanation: y = k/√x. With x = 4, y = 6: 6 = k/2, so k = 12. When y = 3: 3 = 12/√x, so √x = 4 and x = 16.

whyNot.A: 8 treats y as varying inversely as x itself (xy = 24 gives x = 8).
whyNot.B: 36 squares the old y value (6²) instead of using the constant k = 12.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: The diagonals of a rhombus are 10 cm and 16 cm long. Find its area.
questions.explanation: The area of a rhombus is half the product of its diagonals: (1/2) × 10 × 16 = 80 cm².

whyNot.C: 160 cm² forgets to halve the product of the diagonals.
whyNot.A: 40 cm² halves twice.
whyNot.D: 26 cm² adds the diagonals instead of using half their product.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 5 cm. (Take π = 22/7.)

whyNot.A: 220 cm³ = 2πrh is the curved surface area, not the volume.
whyNot.C: 1540 cm³ doubles the volume (uses the diameter in place of r once).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A rectangular plot in Abeokuta has an area of 48 m² and a length of 8 m. Find its perimeter.
questions.explanation: Width = area ÷ length = 48 ÷ 8 = 6 m. Perimeter = 2(length + width) = 2(8 + 6) = 28 m.

whyNot.C: 14 m is length + width; the perimeter goes round all four sides.
whyNot.B: 96 m doubles the area, mixing up area and perimeter.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A parallelogram has adjacent sides 12 cm and 9 cm, and the angle between them is 30°. Find its area.
questions.explanation: Area of a parallelogram = ab sin θ = 12 × 9 × sin 30° = 108 × 1/2 = 54 cm².

whyNot.A: 108 cm² multiplies the sides without the sine of the angle (correct only for a rectangle).
whyNot.D: 27 cm² uses ½ab sin θ, which is the area of a triangle, half the parallelogram.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A solid cone has base radius 7 cm and slant height 10 cm. Find its total surface area. (Take π = 22/7.)
questions.explanation: Total surface area = curved surface + base = πrl + πr² = (22/7)(7)(10) + (22/7)(7)² = 220 + 154 = 374 cm².

whyNot.B: 220 cm² is only the curved surface; a solid cone also has a circular base.
whyNot.A: 154 cm² is only the base area.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: The area of a circle is 616 cm². Find its radius. (Take π = 22/7.)

whyNot.A: 28 cm is the diameter.
whyNot.D: 196 is r², before taking the square root.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: 1,540 cm³ of water is poured into an empty cylindrical can of radius 7 cm. How deep is the water? (Take π = 22/7.)
questions.explanation: The water forms a cylinder of radius 7 cm, so its volume is πr²h. Base area = (22/7) × 49 = 154 cm². Depth h = 1,540 ÷ 154 = 10 cm.

whyNot.D: 70 cm divides by πr = 22 instead of the base area πr² = 154.
whyNot.C: 35 cm divides by the circumference 2πr = 44 instead of the base area.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A chord of a circle of radius 8 cm subtends an angle of 60° at the centre. Find the length of the chord.
questions.explanation: The two radii and the chord form a triangle with two sides of 8 cm and a 60° angle between them. Its base angles are each (180° − 60°)/2 = 60°, so it is equilateral and the chord is 8 cm. (Or chord = 2r sin(θ/2) = 16 sin 30° = 8 cm.)

whyNot.C: 4 cm is half the chord (r sin 30°).
whyNot.B: 4√3 cm is the distance from the centre to the chord, r cos 30°.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A solid metal sphere of radius 3 cm is melted down and recast into a cylinder of radius 2 cm. Find the height of the cylinder.
questions.explanation: Volume is unchanged. Sphere: (4/3)π(3)³ = 36π cm³. Cylinder: π(2)²h = 4πh. So 4πh = 36π and h = 9 cm.

whyNot.B: 4.5 cm takes the cylinder's volume as 2πr²h = 8πh instead of πr²h = 4πh.
whyNot.A: 27 cm uses πr³ = 27π for the sphere (no 4/3) and then divides by π only.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A circular flower bed of radius 7 m is surrounded by a path, so that the outer edge of the path is a circle of radius 10.5 m with the same centre. Find the area of the path. (Take π = 22/7.)
questions.explanation: Area of path = area of outer circle − area of inner circle = π(10.5² − 7²) = (22/7)(110.25 − 49) = (22/7)(61.25) = 192.5 m².

whyNot.B: 38.5 m² is π × 3.5² — the width of the path squared, which is not the area of a ring.
whyNot.A: 346.5 m² is the area of the outer circle alone.
whyNot.D: 154 m² is the area of the flower bed itself, the inner circle.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Two angles on a straight line are 3x and 2x + 30°. Find x.
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°: 3x + 2x + 30° = 180°, so 5x = 150° and x = 30°.

whyNot.A: 36° divides 180° by 5 and ignores the 30°.
whyNot.C: 42° adds the 30° to 180° instead of subtracting it (5x = 210°).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon.
questions.explanation: The sum of the interior angles of an n-sided polygon is (n − 2) × 180°. For a pentagon n = 5: 3 × 180° = 540°.

whyNot.D: 360° is the sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral (and of the exterior angles of any polygon).
whyNot.C: 720° is for a hexagon.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the value of tan 45° − sin 30°.

whyNot.A: 0 takes sin 30° as 1.
whyNot.B: 3/2 adds the two values instead of subtracting.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: AB is a diameter of a circle and C is a point on the circle. If angle CAB = 35°, find angle ABC.
questions.explanation: The angle in a semicircle is a right angle, so angle ACB = 90°. In triangle ABC: angle ABC = 180° − 90° − 35° = 55°.

whyNot.C: 35° assumes triangle ABC is isosceles with AC = BC, which is not given.
whyNot.D: 70° doubles 35°, using the angle-at-the-centre rule where it does not apply.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A ladder 10 m long leans against a vertical wall and makes an angle of 60° with the level ground. How high up the wall does it reach?
questions.explanation: The ladder is the hypotenuse and the height is opposite the 60° angle: height = 10 sin 60° = 10 × √3/2 = 5√3 m (about 8.66 m).

whyNot.A: 5 m = 10 cos 60° is the distance of the foot of the ladder from the wall.
whyNot.D: 10√3 m uses tan 60°; the ladder is the hypotenuse, not the adjacent side.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Town A is 5 km due north of town B, and town C is 5 km due east of town B. Find the bearing of C from A.
questions.explanation: From A, C is 5 km south and 5 km east, so it lies exactly south-east. Triangle ABC is right-angled and isosceles, so angle BAC = 45°. The bearing from north clockwise is 180° − 45° = 135°.

whyNot.D: 045° is north-east; C is to the south of A.
whyNot.B: 225° is south-west.
whyNot.C: 315° is the bearing of A from C, the back bearing.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: In a circle with centre O, A and B are points on the circle such that angle OAB = 25°. C is a point on the major arc AB. Find angle ACB.
questions.explanation: OA = OB (radii), so triangle OAB is isosceles and angle OBA = 25°. Then angle AOB = 180° − 25° − 25° = 130°. The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre: angle ACB = 130° ÷ 2 = 65°.

whyNot.A: 130° is the angle at the centre, AOB, not at the circumference.
whyNot.B: 50° is the sum of the two base angles.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: From a point P on level ground, the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is 30°. From a point Q, 20 m nearer the tower in a straight line, the angle of elevation is 60°. Find the height of the tower.
questions.explanation: Let the height be h and the distance from Q to the foot be x. Then h = x tan 60° = x√3 and h = (x + 20) tan 30° = (x + 20)/√3. So 3x = x + 20, giving x = 10 m and h = 10√3 m (about 17.3 m).

whyNot.C: 20√3 m uses the 20 m gap as the distance from Q to the tower.
whyNot.A: 10 m is the distance from Q to the foot of the tower, not the height.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is one-fifth of each interior angle. How many sides has the polygon?
questions.explanation: Let the exterior angle be e; then the interior angle is 5e. They add up to 180°, so 6e = 180° and e = 30°. Number of sides = 360° ÷ 30° = 12.

whyNot.A: 10 sides gives an exterior angle of 36°, which is a quarter of the interior angle (144°).
whyNot.D: 5 is the ratio given, not the number of sides.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: PT is a tangent at T to a circle with centre O and radius 5 cm. If PT = 12 cm, find the distance OP.
questions.explanation: The radius OT is perpendicular to the tangent at T, so triangle OTP has a right angle at T. By Pythagoras: OP = √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 cm.

whyNot.A: 17 cm adds the two lengths, but OP is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle.
whyNot.B: √119 cm subtracts the squares, treating PT as the hypotenuse.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.context:
The shoe sizes of 35 pupils in a class in Ilorin are shown below.
Shoe size: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9
Number of pupils: 4, 9, 12, 7, 3
questions.stem: What is the modal shoe size?
questions.explanation: The mode is the value that occurs most often. Size 7 has the highest frequency (12 pupils), so the modal shoe size is 7.

whyNot.D: 12 is the highest frequency, not the shoe size that has it.
whyNot.A: 9 is the largest shoe size, not the most common.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A letter is chosen at random from the word ABEOKUTA. What is the probability that it is a vowel?
questions.explanation: ABEOKUTA has 8 letters: A, B, E, O, K, U, T, A. The vowels are A, E, O, U and A — 5 letters. P(vowel) = 5/8.

whyNot.C: 1/2 = 4/8 counts the letter A only once.
whyNot.D: 3/8 is the probability of a consonant (B, K, T).
whyNot.B: 5/7 divides by 7, counting A only once in the total.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the median of 14, 9, 21, 17, 9, 12, 19 and 25.
questions.explanation: Arrange in order: 9, 9, 12, 14, 17, 19, 21, 25. There are 8 numbers, so the median is the mean of the 4th and 5th: (14 + 17)/2 = 15.5.

whyNot.A: 17 is the 5th number alone; with an even count we average the two middle numbers.
whyNot.C: 14 is the 4th number alone.
whyNot.D: 9 is the mode.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the variance of 1, 3, 4, 6 and 6.
questions.explanation: Mean = 20/5 = 4. Squared deviations: (1 − 4)² = 9, (3 − 4)² = 1, 0, 4, 4. Their sum is 18. Variance = 18/5 = 3.6.

whyNot.B: 4 is the mean, not the variance.
whyNot.D: 18 is the sum of squared deviations before dividing by 5.
whyNot.C: 1.9 is roughly the standard deviation (√3.6), not the variance.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.context:
A student's monthly spending:
Food: ₦12,000
Transport: ₦6,000
Books: ₦4,000
Others: ₦2,000
questions.stem: If the spending is shown on a pie chart, what angle represents transport?

whyNot.D: 60° is the angle for books (4,000/24,000 × 360°).
whyNot.B: 180° is the angle for food.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Two fair dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the product of the two numbers is 6?
questions.explanation: There are 36 equally likely outcomes. A product of 6 comes from (1, 6), (6, 1), (2, 3) and (3, 2): 4 outcomes. Probability = 4/36 = 1/9.

whyNot.C: 1/18 = 2/36 counts (1, 6) and (6, 1) as one outcome, and (2, 3) and (3, 2) as one.
whyNot.D: 1/6 is the probability that one die alone shows a 6.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.context:
The masses, in kg, of 10 bags of beans are grouped below.
Mass (kg): 1–5, 6–10, 11–15
Frequency: 3, 5, 2
questions.stem: Using the class mid-values, estimate the mean mass of the bags.

whyNot.C: 8 kg is the mid-value of the modal class, not the mean.
whyNot.B: 25 kg is Σfx divided by 3 classes instead of 10 bags.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A fair die is thrown twice. What is the probability of getting at least one six?
questions.explanation: P(no six in one throw) = 5/6, so P(no six in two throws) = (5/6)² = 25/36. P(at least one six) = 1 − 25/36 = 11/36.

whyNot.B: 1/3 = 1/6 + 1/6 counts the outcome (6, 6) twice.
whyNot.D: 1/36 is the probability of two sixes.
whyNot.C: 25/36 is the probability of no six.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A box contains 3 red and 2 white balls. A ball is drawn, its colour noted and it is put back; then a second ball is drawn. What is the probability that both balls are the same colour?
questions.explanation: With replacement the draws are independent. P(both red) = (3/5)² = 9/25 and P(both white) = (2/5)² = 4/25. P(same colour) = 9/25 + 4/25 = 13/25.

whyNot.D: 9/25 counts only the case where both are red.
whyNot.B: 2/5 is the without-replacement answer (3/5 × 2/4 + 2/5 × 1/4 = 8/20).
whyNot.C: 12/25 is the probability that the colours are different.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: The mean of 10 numbers is 12. When two of the numbers are removed, the mean of the remaining 8 numbers is 11. Find the mean of the two numbers removed.
questions.explanation: Sum of the 10 numbers = 10 × 12 = 120. Sum of the remaining 8 = 8 × 11 = 88. The two removed numbers add up to 120 − 88 = 32, so their mean is 32 ÷ 2 = 16.

whyNot.A: 32 is the sum of the two numbers, not their mean.
whyNot.D: 1 is just the drop in the mean (12 − 11).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Convert 47 (base ten) to a number in base three.
questions.explanation: Divide by 3 repeatedly: 47 ÷ 3 = 15 r 2, 15 ÷ 3 = 5 r 0, 5 ÷ 3 = 1 r 2, 1 ÷ 3 = 0 r 1. Reading upwards gives 1202₃. Check: 27 + 2 × 9 + 0 + 2 = 47.

whyNot.A: 2021₃ reads the remainders from top to bottom; it equals 61.
whyNot.D: 1220₃ equals 51, not 47.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 12, 18 and 30.
questions.explanation: 12 = 2² × 3, 18 = 2 × 3² and 30 = 2 × 3 × 5. The LCM takes the highest power of each prime: 2² × 3² × 5 = 4 × 9 × 5 = 180.

whyNot.D: 6 is the HCF, the largest number that divides all three.
whyNot.C: 360 is a common multiple but not the lowest.
whyNot.B: 90 is not a multiple of 12.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Write 3.5 × 10⁻³ as an ordinary decimal number.
questions.explanation: Multiplying by 10⁻³ means dividing by 1,000, which moves the decimal point 3 places to the left: 3.5 → 0.0035.

whyNot.D: 0.035 moves the point only 2 places.
whyNot.C: 3500 moves the point to the right, which is for 10³.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.explanation: First the bracket: 1/2 + 1/3 = 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6. Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal: 5/6 × 12/5 = 60/30 = 2.

whyNot.C: 25/72 multiplies by 5/12 instead of dividing.
whyNot.A: 1/2 divides the other way round (5/12 ÷ 5/6).
whyNot.D: 5/6 is only the value of the bracket.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Simplify 2√12 + 3√27.

whyNot.B: 5√39 adds the numbers outside and inside the roots, which is not allowed for surds.
whyNot.C: 11√3 takes 2√12 as 2√3, forgetting to simplify √12 first.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Evaluate log₄ 64 + log₂ 0.5.
questions.explanation: 64 = 4³, so log₄ 64 = 3. 0.5 = 2⁻¹, so log₂ 0.5 = −1. The sum is 3 + (−1) = 2.

whyNot.D: 4 takes log₂ 0.5 as +1; 0.5 is less than 1, so its logarithm is negative.
whyNot.C: 3 is only log₄ 64.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A radio marked ₦45,000 is sold at a discount of 15%. What is the selling price?

whyNot.D: ₦6,750 is the discount, not the selling price.
whyNot.B: ₦51,750 adds 15% instead of taking it off.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Six workers can build a fence in 10 days. Working at the same rate, how long would 4 workers take?
questions.explanation: The job takes 6 × 10 = 60 worker-days. Fewer workers take longer (inverse proportion): 60 ÷ 4 = 15 days.

whyNot.C: 6⅔ days treats it as direct proportion (fewer workers, less time).
whyNot.B: 12 days adds 2 days for the 2 workers removed.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.explanation: Write everything as a power of 2: 4^(x − 1) = 2^(2x − 2) and 32 = 2⁵. So 2^(x + 2x − 2) = 2⁵, giving 3x − 2 = 5, 3x = 7 and x = 7/3.

whyNot.B: x = 2 gives 2² × 4¹ = 16, not 32.
whyNot.C: x = 5/3 forgets the −2 from 4^(−1) = 2^(−2).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Evaluate (0.00042 × 3000) ÷ 0.0021, giving your answer in standard form.

whyNot.A: 6 × 10³ adds an extra power of ten when moving the decimal point.
whyNot.D: 6 × 10⁻² subtracts the indices the wrong way round.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Factorise completely 4x² − 25.
questions.explanation: 4x² − 25 is a difference of two squares: (2x)² − 5². Using a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) gives (2x − 5)(2x + 5).

whyNot.C: (2x − 5)² = 4x² − 20x + 25, which has a middle term.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Solve the equation 7 − 2x = 3x − 8.
questions.explanation: Collect x terms on one side and numbers on the other: 7 + 8 = 3x + 2x, so 15 = 5x and x = 3. Check: 7 − 6 = 1 and 9 − 8 = 1 ✓.

whyNot.A: x = −3 makes a sign error when moving −8 across.
whyNot.C: 15 is 5x; it still has to be divided by 5.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: If y = 3x² − 2, find the value of y when x = −3.
questions.explanation: Square first: (−3)² = 9. Then y = 3 × 9 − 2 = 27 − 2 = 25.

whyNot.D: −29 takes −3² as −9 instead of (−3)² = 9.
whyNot.A: 79 squares 3x as a whole: (3 × −3)² − 2 = 81 − 2.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Simplify (2x + 6)/(x² + 3x).
questions.explanation: Factorise top and bottom: 2x + 6 = 2(x + 3) and x² + 3x = x(x + 3). Cancel the common factor (x + 3): 2(x + 3)/[x(x + 3)] = 2/x.

whyNot.A: 2 cancels x(x + 3) completely, leaving out the x in the denominator.
whyNot.D: 6/(3x) cancels terms (2x with x²), not factors.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Solve the simultaneous equations 4x − y = 5 and 2x + 3y = 13.
questions.explanation: From the first equation y = 4x − 5. Substitute: 2x + 3(4x − 5) = 13, so 14x − 15 = 13, 14x = 28 and x = 2. Then y = 8 − 5 = 3.

whyNot.D: x = 1, y = −1 satisfies the first equation only: 2 − 3 = −1, not 13.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: The first term of a geometric progression is 3 and the common ratio is −2. Find the 4th term.

whyNot.A: 24 forgets that an odd power of a negative number is negative.
whyNot.B: 48 = 3 × (−2)⁴ is the 5th term.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Solve the inequality 3(x − 2) ≥ 5x + 4.
questions.explanation: Expand: 3x − 6 ≥ 5x + 4. Subtract 3x and 4 from both sides: −10 ≥ 2x, so x ≤ −5. (Check x = −6: −24 ≥ −26 ✓.)

whyNot.D: x ≥ −5 reverses the sign: when −10 ≥ 2x is rewritten with x on the left, the inequality must point the other way.
whyNot.A: x ≤ 5 loses the minus sign of −10.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the quadratic equation whose roots are 2/3 and −1.
questions.explanation: If x = 2/3 then 3x − 2 = 0; if x = −1 then x + 1 = 0. The equation is (3x − 2)(x + 1) = 0, which expands to 3x² + 3x − 2x − 2 = 3x² + x − 2 = 0.

whyNot.C: 3x² − x − 2 = (3x + 2)(x − 1) has roots −2/3 and 1, the signs reversed.
whyNot.A: x² + x − 2 = (x + 2)(x − 1) has roots −2 and 1.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: F varies jointly as m and n, and inversely as the square of d. F = 12 when m = 2, n = 3 and d = 1. Find F when m = 4, n = 5 and d = 2.

whyNot.A: 20 divides by d = 2 instead of d² = 4.
whyNot.C: 40 forgets to divide by d² at all.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: The 4th term of an arithmetic progression is 10 and the sum of its first 6 terms is 57. Find the first term.
questions.explanation: a + 3d = 10 and S₆ = (6/2)(2a + 5d) = 57, so 2a + 5d = 19. From the first, a = 10 − 3d; substitute: 20 − 6d + 5d = 19, so d = 1 and a = 7. Check: 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 add up to 57 ✓.

whyNot.D: 1 is the common difference, not the first term.
whyNot.A: 10 is the 4th term.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A square has a perimeter of 36 cm. Find its area.
questions.explanation: Each side = perimeter ÷ 4 = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm. Area = side² = 9² = 81 cm².

whyNot.D: 36 cm² takes the perimeter as the area.
whyNot.A: 324 cm² = 36 × 9 multiplies the perimeter by the side.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A prism has a triangular cross-section with base 6 cm and height 4 cm. The prism is 10 cm long. Find its volume.
questions.explanation: Volume of a prism = area of cross-section × length. Area of the triangle = (1/2) × 6 × 4 = 12 cm². Volume = 12 × 10 = 120 cm³.

whyNot.B: 240 cm³ forgets the 1/2 in the area of a triangle.
whyNot.A: 20 cm³ adds the dimensions instead of multiplying.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the perimeter of a semicircle of radius 7 cm, including its straight edge. (Take π = 22/7.)
questions.explanation: The curved part is half the circumference: πr = (22/7) × 7 = 22 cm. The straight edge is the diameter, 14 cm. Perimeter = 22 + 14 = 36 cm.

whyNot.B: 22 cm is only the curved edge.
whyNot.D: 44 cm is the circumference of the full circle.
whyNot.C: 29 cm adds the radius instead of the diameter.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the curved surface area of a hemisphere of radius 7 cm. (Take π = 22/7.)
questions.explanation: The curved surface of a hemisphere is half that of a sphere: (1/2) × 4πr² = 2πr² = 2 × (22/7) × 49 = 308 cm².

whyNot.C: 616 cm² is the surface area of a whole sphere.
whyNot.B: 154 cm² is the area of the flat circular face.
whyNot.A: 462 cm² is the total surface area (curved + flat face).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A cone has base radius 5 cm and slant height 13 cm. Find its volume, leaving your answer in terms of π.
questions.explanation: First find the vertical height: h = √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12 cm. Volume = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)π × 25 × 12 = 100π cm³.

whyNot.D: 325π/3 uses the slant height 13 cm in place of the vertical height.
whyNot.B: 300π cm³ forgets the 1/3.
whyNot.C: 65π is the curved surface area πrl (in cm²), not the volume.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the area of an equilateral triangle of side 6 cm.

whyNot.C: 18 cm² = (1/2) × 6 × 6 treats the triangle as right-angled.
whyNot.A: 18√3 cm² forgets the 1/2.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A closed rectangular box measures 8 cm by 5 cm by 3 cm. Find its total surface area.
questions.explanation: There are three pairs of equal faces: 8 × 5 = 40, 8 × 3 = 24 and 5 × 3 = 15. Total surface area = 2(40 + 24 + 15) = 2 × 79 = 158 cm².

whyNot.A: 120 cm³ is the volume (8 × 5 × 3), not a surface area.
whyNot.D: 79 cm² counts each pair of faces only once.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: An arc of length 11 cm is part of a circle of radius 7 cm. Find the angle the arc subtends at the centre. (Take π = 22/7.)
questions.explanation: Arc length = (θ/360°) × 2πr. The circumference is 2 × (22/7) × 7 = 44 cm. So θ/360° = 11/44 = 1/4 and θ = 90°.

whyNot.C: 45° uses πr = 22 cm as the whole circumference.
whyNot.A: 180° would need an arc of 22 cm, half the circumference of 44 cm.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A cylindrical water tank in a school in Maiduguri has radius 1.4 m and height 2 m. How many litres does it hold when full? (Take π = 22/7 and 1 m³ = 1,000 litres.)

whyNot.A: 8,800 litres uses 2πrh = 17.6 m² halved, mixing the curved surface area with volume.
whyNot.C: 17,600 litres uses the curved surface area 2πrh = 17.6 as if it were a volume.
whyNot.B: 1,232 litres multiplies by 100 instead of 1,000.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: The surface area of a sphere is 616 cm². Find its volume. (Take π = 22/7.)

whyNot.A: 4312 cm³ forgets to divide by 3.
whyNot.B: 2874⅔ cm³ uses r = 7 but doubles the volume (8/3 instead of 4/3).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: The supplement of an angle is three times the angle. Find the angle.
questions.explanation: Let the angle be x. Its supplement is 180° − x. So 180° − x = 3x, giving 4x = 180° and x = 45°.

whyNot.D: 60° comes from 180° ÷ 3, forgetting that the angle itself is also part of the 180°.
whyNot.A: 22.5° uses complements (90°) instead of supplements.
whyNot.B: 135° is the supplement, not the angle.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: The interior angles of a polygon add up to 1080°. How many sides has the polygon?
questions.explanation: (n − 2) × 180° = 1080°, so n − 2 = 6 and n = 8. The polygon is an octagon.

whyNot.C: 6 is n − 2; two must be added back.
whyNot.B: 12 divides 1080° by 90°.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the value of sin 60° × cos 30°.

whyNot.A: 1/4 uses 1/2 for both values (those are sin 30° and cos 60°).
whyNot.B: √3/4 uses 1/2 for one of the values.
whyNot.D: 1 assumes sin 60° × cos 30° = sin² + cos² of the same angle.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A transversal cuts two parallel lines. Two co-interior (allied) angles formed are (2x + 10)° and (3x − 30)°. Find x.
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles between parallel lines add up to 180°: 2x + 10 + 3x − 30 = 180, so 5x − 20 = 180, 5x = 200 and x = 40.

whyNot.B: 28 adds the constants (10 + 30) instead of combining +10 and −30: 5x + 40 = 180.
whyNot.C: 36 ignores the constants: 5x = 180.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the equation of the straight line passing through (2, −1) and (4, 5).

whyNot.D: y = 3x − 1 has the right gradient but does not pass through either point.
whyNot.C: y = (1/3)x − 5/3 uses change in x over change in y for the gradient.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A boat leaves a jetty and sails 30 km on a bearing of 090°, then 40 km on a bearing of 180°. How far is it from the jetty?
questions.explanation: 090° is due east and 180° is due south, so the two legs are at right angles. Distance = √(30² + 40²) = √2500 = 50 km.

whyNot.C: 70 km is the total distance sailed, not the straight-line distance from the jetty.
whyNot.D: 10 km subtracts the two legs.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: If cos θ = −√3/2 and θ is an obtuse angle, find θ.
questions.explanation: The basic angle with cosine √3/2 is 30°. Cosine is negative in the second quadrant, where θ = 180° − 30° = 150°.

whyNot.B: 210° also has cosine −√3/2 but it is a reflex angle, not obtuse.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A boy whose eyes are 1.5 m above the ground stands 20 m from the foot of a vertical flagpole on level ground. The angle of elevation of the top of the pole from his eyes is 30°. Find the height of the flagpole, correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.explanation: Height above eye level = 20 tan 30° = 20 × 0.5774 = 11.547 m. Add the eye height: 11.547 + 1.5 = 13.047 ≈ 13.05 m.

whyNot.A: 11.55 m forgets to add the boy's eye height of 1.5 m.
whyNot.D: 36.14 m uses tan 60° instead of tan 30°.
whyNot.C: 10.00 m uses sin 30° instead of tan 30° and leaves out the eye height.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: AB and CD are parallel chords of a circle of radius 5 cm, on opposite sides of the centre. AB = 6 cm and CD = 8 cm. Find the distance between the chords.
questions.explanation: The perpendicular from the centre bisects a chord. For AB: distance = √(5² − 3²) = 4 cm. For CD: √(5² − 4²) = 3 cm. On opposite sides of the centre the distances add: 4 + 3 = 7 cm.

whyNot.D: 1 cm subtracts the distances, which is correct only when both chords are on the same side of the centre.
whyNot.A: 2 cm is the difference in the lengths of the chords halved.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: In triangle ABC, D is on AB and E is on AC such that DE is parallel to BC. AD = 4 cm, DB = 6 cm and DE = 5 cm. Find BC.
questions.explanation: Triangles ADE and ABC are similar because DE ∥ BC. AB = 4 + 6 = 10 cm. So BC/DE = AB/AD = 10/4, and BC = 5 × 10/4 = 12.5 cm.

whyNot.B: 7.5 cm uses DB/AD = 6/4 instead of AB/AD.
whyNot.A: 10 cm is the length of AB, not BC.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: A day of the week is chosen at random. What is the probability that its name begins with the letter T?
questions.explanation: There are 7 days, and two of them (Tuesday and Thursday) begin with T. Probability = 2/7.

whyNot.A: 1/7 counts only one of Tuesday and Thursday.
whyNot.C: 5/7 is the probability that the name does NOT begin with T.
whyNot.B: 2/5 counts only the five weekdays.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the mean of 8, 12, 7, 15 and 13.
questions.explanation: Mean = sum ÷ number of values = (8 + 12 + 7 + 15 + 13) ÷ 5 = 55 ÷ 5 = 11.

whyNot.D: 12 is the median (the middle value of 7, 8, 12, 13, 15), not the mean.
whyNot.C: 55 is the sum; it must be divided by 5.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.context:
Marks scored by 20 students in a test:
Marks: 0–9, 10–19, 20–29, 30–39
Number of students: 3, 7, 8, 2
questions.stem: How many students scored 20 marks or more?
questions.explanation: Scores of 20 or more are in the classes 20–29 and 30–39. Number of students = 8 + 2 = 10.

whyNot.A: 8 counts only the 20–29 class.
whyNot.B: 18 adds the 10–19 and 20–29 classes.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.context:
A survey of 20 families in a village recorded the number of children in each family.
Number of children: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4
Number of families: 2, 5, 8, 4, 1
questions.stem: Find the mean number of children per family.

whyNot.A: 2 is the mode (and the median), not the mean.
whyNot.B: 2.5 is (0 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 4) ÷ 4, ignoring the frequencies.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Three fair coins are tossed together. What is the probability of getting exactly two heads?
questions.explanation: The 8 equally likely outcomes are HHH, HHT, HTH, THH, HTT, THT, TTH, TTT. Exactly two heads: HHT, HTH, THH — 3 outcomes. Probability = 3/8.

whyNot.A: 1/4 counts only 2 of the 3 arrangements of two heads.
whyNot.C: 1/2 is the probability of at least two heads (including HHH).
whyNot.B: 2/3 treats the answer as 'two out of three coins'.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the mean deviation of 2, 4, 6 and 8.

whyNot.D: 5 is the mean itself.
whyNot.A: 0 adds the deviations with their signs; they always cancel, which is why absolute values are used.
whyNot.C: 8 is the sum of the absolute deviations; it must be divided by 4.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: On a pie chart showing how 72 students travel to school, the sector for students who walk has an angle of 50°. How many students walk to school?
questions.explanation: Number = (sector angle ÷ 360°) × total = (50/360) × 72 = 3600/360 = 10 students.

whyNot.A: 50 is the angle, not the number of students.
whyNot.C: 26 is 360 ÷ 14, which mixes up the numbers.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: The probability that Musa hits a target is 1/3 and the probability that Tunde hits it is 1/4. They shoot independently. What is the probability that at least one of them hits the target?
questions.explanation: P(Musa misses) = 2/3 and P(Tunde misses) = 3/4. P(both miss) = 2/3 × 3/4 = 1/2. P(at least one hits) = 1 − 1/2 = 1/2.

whyNot.A: 7/12 = 1/3 + 1/4 counts the case where both hit twice.
whyNot.B: 1/12 is the probability that both hit.
whyNot.C: 1/4 = (1/3)(3/4) is the probability that only Musa hits; Tunde hitting must be counted too.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Find the standard deviation of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7.
questions.explanation: Mean = 28/7 = 4. Squared deviations: 9, 4, 1, 0, 1, 4, 9; their sum is 28. Variance = 28/7 = 4. Standard deviation = √4 = 2.

whyNot.B: 4 is the variance (and also the mean); the standard deviation is its square root.
whyNot.A: 28 is the sum of squared deviations before dividing by 7.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Two fair dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the sum of the two numbers is a prime number?
questions.explanation: The prime sums possible are 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11. Ways: 2 → 1, 3 → 2, 5 → 4, 7 → 6, 11 → 2, a total of 15 out of 36. Probability = 15/36 = 5/12.

whyNot.B: 1/2 assumes half the sums are prime.
whyNot.A: 1/3 = 12/36 leaves out the sums 2 and 3 (or 11).
whyNot.C: 7/18 = 14/36 misses one of the outcomes, for example counting the sum 2 as not prime.

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: The least count of a vernier caliper is 0.01 cm. When it is used to measure the diameter of a test tube, the main scale reads 2.3 cm just before the vernier zero, and the 7th vernier division lines up exactly with a main-scale mark. What is the diameter of the test tube?
questions.explanation: Reading = main-scale reading + (coinciding vernier division × least count). Vernier part = 7 × 0.01 cm = 0.07 cm. Diameter = 2.3 cm + 0.07 cm = 2.37 cm.

whyNot.A: 2.307 cm uses 0.001 cm for each vernier division; the least count given is 0.01 cm.
whyNot.D: 2.30 cm leaves out the vernier reading altogether.
whyNot.C: 3.00 cm adds 7 × 0.1 cm; each vernier division is worth only 0.01 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: A football is kicked from level ground with a speed of 40 m s⁻¹ at an angle of 30° above the horizontal. How long is the ball in the air before it lands? (g = 10 m s⁻², ignore air resistance)
questions.explanation: Time of flight T = 2u sin θ ÷ g. The vertical part of the velocity is u sin 30° = 40 × 0.5 = 20 m s⁻¹. T = 2 × 20 ÷ 10 = 4.0 s.

whyNot.D: 2.0 s is only the time to reach the highest point; the ball takes the same time again to come down.
whyNot.A: 6.9 s uses cos 30° instead of sin 30°; the time in the air depends on the vertical component.
whyNot.B: 8.0 s uses the full 40 m s⁻¹ as if the ball were kicked straight up.

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: A car of mass 1000 kg goes round a flat circular bend of radius 50 m at a steady speed of 10 m s⁻¹. What is the centripetal force acting on the car?
questions.explanation: Centripetal force F = mv² ÷ r = 1000 × 10² ÷ 50 = 100 000 ÷ 50 = 2000 N. This force, provided by friction between the tyres and the road, is directed towards the centre of the bend.

whyNot.B: 200 N is mv ÷ r; the speed must be squared.
whyNot.D: 1000 N is ½mv² ÷ r; there is no ½ in the formula for centripetal force.
whyNot.C: 100 000 N is mv² without dividing by the radius.

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: A block of mass 4 kg is released from rest on a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. What is its acceleration down the plane? (g = 10 m s⁻²)
questions.explanation: Only the component of the weight along the plane, mg sin θ, accelerates the block (the plane is smooth, so there is no friction). a = mg sin θ ÷ m = g sin 30° = 10 × 0.5 = 5.0 m s⁻². The mass cancels out.

whyNot.C: 8.7 m s⁻² uses g cos 30°, which is the component of g perpendicular to the plane.
whyNot.A: 10 m s⁻² is the acceleration of free fall; on a slope only part of the weight acts along the plane.
whyNot.D: 20 m s⁻² is mg sin θ (the force, 20 N) taken as the acceleration without dividing by the mass.

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: Pressure is defined as force per unit area. What are the dimensions of pressure?
questions.explanation: Force has dimensions MLT⁻² (mass × acceleration) and area has dimensions L². Pressure = force ÷ area = MLT⁻² ÷ L² = ML⁻¹T⁻².

whyNot.A: MLT⁻² is the dimension of force; it has not been divided by area.
whyNot.D: ML²T⁻² is the dimension of energy (force × distance), not pressure.

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: A particle performs simple harmonic motion with an amplitude of 0.1 m and a frequency of 5 Hz. What is its maximum speed? (π = 3.14)
questions.explanation: Maximum speed v = ωA, where ω = 2πf. ω = 2 × 3.14 × 5 = 31.4 rad s⁻¹. v = 31.4 × 0.1 = 3.14 m s⁻¹. The particle has this speed as it passes through the centre of its motion.

whyNot.C: 0.50 m s⁻¹ is fA; the angular frequency ω = 2πf must be used.
whyNot.B: 31.4 is ω alone; it has not been multiplied by the amplitude.
whyNot.A: 98.6 is ω²A, which gives the maximum acceleration (in m s⁻²), not the maximum speed.

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: A trader drags a sack of garri 10 m along the ground with a rope. The tension in the rope is 50 N and the rope makes an angle of 60° with the horizontal. How much work does the tension do on the sack?
