whyNot.C: 300 crates divides the fixed cost by the variable cost per crate (₦600,000 ÷ ₦2,000).
whyNot.A: 171 crates divides the fixed cost by the price alone (₦600,000 ÷ ₦3,500), ignoring variable costs.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: The demand for staple foods such as garri is price-inelastic. When there is a bumper harvest of cassava, farmers' total revenue is likely to
options: stay the same, because demand does not change
rise, because price increases with output
fall, because price drops by a larger proportion than quantity sold rises
rise, because they sell a larger quantity
questions.explanation: With inelastic demand, buyers will take extra quantity only at a much lower price. The percentage fall in price is greater than the percentage rise in quantity sold, so price × quantity (total revenue) falls.

whyNot.D: Selling more does not raise revenue when the price falls proportionately more.
whyNot.B: A bigger harvest lowers price; it does not raise it.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: Which hand tool is most commonly used to cut down grass and small shrubs when clearing land for farming?
questions.explanation: The cutlass (machete) has a long sharp blade used for slashing grass, cutting shrubs and clearing bush. It is the most common clearing tool on Nigerian farms.

whyNot.B: A rake gathers trash and levels soil.
whyNot.D: A hand trowel is used for transplanting seedlings.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: On hard, stony land with many tree roots, a disc plough is preferred to a mouldboard plough mainly because
options: its discs roll over obstacles instead of being caught and broken
it needs no tractor to pull it
it turns the furrow slice over more completely
it also sows the seed while ploughing
questions.explanation: Disc plough bodies are rotating concave discs. When they hit a stone or root they roll over it, so they are less likely to break than the fixed share of a mouldboard plough. They also work better in hard and sticky soils.

whyNot.C: The mouldboard plough generally inverts the soil and buries trash more completely.
whyNot.D: Ploughs do not sow seed; a planter does that.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: Which tractor-drawn implement places seeds in the soil at a uniform depth and spacing?
questions.explanation: A planter opens a furrow, drops seeds at set intervals and depths, and covers them. This gives an even plant population and saves labour.

whyNot.B: A harrow breaks clods after ploughing.
whyNot.D: A ridger forms ridges.
whyNot.A: A slasher cuts grass and weeds.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: The main reason for greasing the moving parts of farm machines regularly is to
options: increase the fuel used by the engine
prevent the tyres from going flat
reduce friction and wear between the parts
questions.explanation: Grease forms a film between moving metal surfaces. This reduces friction, heat and wear, so parts last longer and the machine runs smoothly.

whyNot.A: Reducing friction lowers, not raises, the power and fuel needed.
whyNot.B: Tyre pressure has nothing to do with greasing.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: In a two-stroke petrol engine such as that of a small knapsack mist-blower, how often does a power stroke occur?
options: Once in every two revolutions of the crankshaft
Twice in every revolution of the crankshaft
Once in every four revolutions of the crankshaft
Once in every revolution of the crankshaft
questions.explanation: A two-stroke engine completes its cycle in two strokes of the piston (one up, one down), which is one revolution of the crankshaft. So there is a power stroke in every revolution. A four-stroke engine has one power stroke in every two revolutions.

whyNot.A: One power stroke in two revolutions describes a four-stroke engine.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: A tractor hiring service in Niger State charges ₦45,000 per hectare for ploughing. How much will a farmer pay to plough 3.5 ha?

whyNot.B: ₦135,000 is the cost for only 3 ha.
whyNot.C: ₦180,000 is the cost for 4 ha.
whyNot.D: ₦12,857 divides the rate by the area instead of multiplying.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: A farmer irrigates a 2 ha vegetable farm with water to a depth of 25 mm. What volume of water is applied? (1 ha = 10,000 m²)

whyNot.C: 5,000 m³ uses 0.25 m (250 mm) as the depth.
whyNot.D: 50 m³ uses 0.0025 m as the depth; 25 mm is 0.025 m.
whyNot.B: 50,000 m³ uses 2.5 m as the depth instead of 0.025 m.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: A disadvantage of using work animals such as oxen for ploughing is that they
options: can work for 24 hours without rest
are too costly for any farmer to buy spare parts for
must be fed and cared for even when there is no farm work
need petrol or diesel to work
questions.explanation: Work animals need feed, water, housing and veterinary care all year, even in seasons when they are not working. They also tire quickly and can be attacked by disease.

whyNot.D: Animals run on feed, not fuel; needing fuel is a feature of tractors.
whyNot.A: Animals tire and need rest; working without rest would be an advantage, and it is not true.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: Which machine is used to separate maize grains from the cobs after harvest?
questions.explanation: A maize sheller (hand-operated or motorised) strips the dry grains from the cob much faster than shelling by hand.

whyNot.A: A cassava grater shreds peeled cassava tubers into a mash.
whyNot.C: A rice huller removes the husk from paddy rice.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: In farm surveying, ranging poles are used mainly to
options: mark points so that straight survey lines can be set out
record the area of the farm in hectares
measure the height of trees on the farm
measure the angle between two survey lines
questions.explanation: Ranging poles are long, brightly painted poles placed at survey stations. Sighting along them lets the surveyor mark out straight lines between points.

whyNot.D: Angles and bearings are measured with a prismatic compass or theodolite.
whyNot.B: Area is calculated from the measurements; poles do not record it.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: The branch of agriculture that deals with the growing of fruits, vegetables and ornamental plants is called
questions.explanation: Horticulture is the cultivation of garden crops: fruits such as citrus and mango, vegetables such as tomato and pepper, and ornamental flowers and shrubs.

whyNot.B: Silviculture is the growing and care of forest trees.
whyNot.A: Pisciculture is fish farming.
whyNot.D: Apiculture is bee keeping.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: A youth in Ogun State keeps giant African land snails in pens and sells them for meat. This branch of animal production is called
questions.explanation: Heliciculture is snail farming. Giant African land snails are a popular, protein-rich meat in southern Nigeria and need little space or capital to rear.

whyNot.D: Sericulture is the rearing of silkworms for silk.
whyNot.A: Aquaculture is the farming of fish and other water organisms.
whyNot.C: Apiculture is bee keeping.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: Light intensity affects crop growth mainly through its effect on the rate of
questions.explanation: Plants use light energy to make food by photosynthesis. Up to a limit, brighter light means faster photosynthesis and more growth; heavily shaded crops grow tall and weak and yield poorly.

whyNot.D: Leaching is caused by water moving through the soil.
whyNot.C: Soil erosion is caused by water and wind.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: The keeping of honey bees in hives for honey and beeswax is called
questions.explanation: Apiculture (bee keeping) produces honey and beeswax. Bees also pollinate crops, so hives near farms can improve fruit and seed set.

whyNot.B: Heliciculture is snail farming.
whyNot.C: Floriculture is the growing of flowers.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: Most smallholder farmers in Nigeria still use hoes and cutlasses rather than tractors. The main reason is that
options: tractors cannot be used on any Nigerian soil
hand tools give higher yields than tractors
they have low incomes and cannot afford machines
the government has banned tractors on small farms
questions.explanation: Small farmers have low incomes and little access to credit, and their plots are small and scattered. Buying or hiring tractors is too costly for them, so they rely on cheap hand tools.

whyNot.B: Hand tools do not give higher yields; they limit the area a farmer can cultivate.
whyNot.A: Tractors are used on many Nigerian farms; soil alone is not the reason.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: The Fadama development projects in Nigeria were designed to improve farming mainly on
options: low-lying flood plains along rivers that can be farmed in the dry season
forest reserves in the rainforest belt
sand dunes in the far north
steep hillsides in the eastern highlands
questions.explanation: Fadama is a Hausa word for low-lying land along rivers and streams that floods in the rainy season. Such land keeps moisture into the dry season and can be irrigated with small pumps, so Fadama projects helped farmers grow crops all year.

whyNot.D: Hillsides are prone to erosion and are not the focus of Fadama projects.
whyNot.B: Forest reserves are protected for timber, not opened for Fadama farming.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: The state Agricultural Development Projects (ADPs), first set up in Nigeria in the 1970s with World Bank support, are best known for
options: exporting cocoa and groundnut on behalf of farmers
building fertiliser factories in each state
providing extension advice and inputs to small-scale farmers through a training and visit system
running large state-owned plantations of rubber and oil palm
questions.explanation: The ADPs aimed to raise the output and income of small-scale farmers. They supplied improved inputs, built rural roads and, above all, delivered extension services through the training and visit (T&V) system, in which agents were trained regularly and then visited farmers on a fixed schedule.

whyNot.D: ADPs worked with small farmers, not by running state plantations.
whyNot.A: Marketing of export crops was the job of the former commodity boards, not the ADPs.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: A disadvantage of communal ownership of land is that
options: every member of the community is denied access to land
the land can be sold freely by any member
an individual cannot use the land as security to obtain a bank loan
land becomes very cheap to buy
questions.explanation: Under communal tenure the land belongs to the community or family, not the individual, so a farmer has no title to pledge as collateral. He also has little incentive to make long-term improvements such as tree planting.

whyNot.A: Communal tenure usually gives every member some access to land; that is its main advantage.
whyNot.B: No single member may sell communal land without the agreement of the community.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: Gum arabic, an export product of northern Nigeria used in food and medicines, is obtained from
questions.explanation: Gum arabic is the dried sap that oozes from the bark of certain acacia trees (mainly Acacia senegal), which grow in the dry savanna of the far north. It is used as a thickener and stabiliser in foods, drinks and medicines.

whyNot.C: Shea trees give shea nuts, from which shea butter is made.
whyNot.B: Locust bean trees give seeds fermented to make iru (dawadawa).

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: In Yobe and Borno States, the advance of desert conditions into once-productive land is made worse mainly by
options: overgrazing and the cutting of trees for firewood
the use of improved crop varieties
questions.explanation: Desertification is caused by low rainfall together with human activities that remove vegetation, such as overgrazing, felling trees for fuelwood and bush burning. Bare soil is then blown away by wind.

whyNot.B: Shelterbelts of trees help to check desertification.
whyNot.C: These states have low, not heavy, rainfall; low rainfall is part of the problem.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: Removing extra seedlings from a stand so that only the required number of healthy plants remains is called
questions.explanation: Thinning reduces the number of plants per stand to the recommended level. The remaining plants then get enough light, water and nutrients to grow well.

whyNot.A: Supplying is replanting stands where seeds failed to germinate.
whyNot.D: Pruning is cutting off unwanted branches.
whyNot.B: Earthing up is heaping soil around the base of plants.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: Which of these crops is normally raised in a nursery before being transplanted to the field?
questions.explanation: Tomato seeds are tiny and the seedlings are delicate, so they are raised in a nursery where they can be watered, shaded and protected, and then transplanted.

whyNot.C: Maize is sown directly in the field.
whyNot.A: Yam is planted directly from setts or seed yams.
whyNot.B: Groundnut is sown directly in the field.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: The way in which sand, silt and clay particles are grouped together into crumbs or clods in a soil is called the soil's
questions.explanation: Soil structure is the arrangement of soil particles into aggregates (crumbs, blocks, plates). A crumb structure allows good aeration, drainage and root growth.

whyNot.A: Soil texture is the relative proportion of sand, silt and clay, not how they are grouped.
whyNot.C: A soil profile is the vertical section of soil showing its horizons.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: In a dry area where land has been irrigated for many years without good drainage, a white crust forms on the soil surface and crop yields fall. The cause is
options: salts left behind at the surface as water evaporates
leaching of nutrients by heavy rainfall
an increase in soil organic matter
too many earthworms in the soil
questions.explanation: Irrigation water contains dissolved salts. In hot, dry areas the water evaporates from the surface and the salts stay behind. Without drainage to wash them away they build up (salinisation), damaging crops.

whyNot.B: Leaching removes salts; the problem here is the build-up of salts in a dry area.
whyNot.C: Organic matter does not form a white salty crust.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: The recommended seed rate for a maize variety is 25 kg per hectare. How much seed does a farmer need for 3.2 ha?
questions.explanation: Seed needed = seed rate × area = 25 kg/ha × 3.2 ha = 80 kg.

whyNot.B: 28.2 kg adds the seed rate and the area instead of multiplying.
whyNot.D: 7.8 kg divides the seed rate by the area.
whyNot.A: 75 kg is the seed for only 3 ha.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: A 50 g soil sample is found to contain 30 g of sand, 12 g of silt and 8 g of clay. What is the percentage of clay in the sample?
questions.explanation: Percentage clay = mass of clay ÷ total mass × 100 = 8 ÷ 50 × 100 = 16%.

whyNot.D: 8 is the mass of clay in grams, not its percentage.
whyNot.B: 24% is the percentage of silt (12 ÷ 50 × 100).
whyNot.C: 60% is the percentage of sand (30 ÷ 50 × 100).

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: The variegated grasshopper (Zonocerus variegatus) damages cassava in the dry season by
options: biting and chewing the leaves and bark
questions.explanation: Zonocerus has biting and chewing mouthparts. Swarms eat the leaves and strip the green bark of cassava stems, which weakens the plants and reduces tuber yield.

whyNot.A: Grasshoppers chew; sap-sucking insects include aphids and whiteflies.
whyNot.D: Cassava mosaic virus is spread by whiteflies, not grasshoppers.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: Pepper seedlings in a nursery suddenly collapse at soil level and die. This damping-off disease is most likely to be made worse by
options: exposing the nursery to full sunlight
overwatering and overcrowding of the seedlings
questions.explanation: Damping-off is caused by soil-borne fungi such as Pythium. They thrive in wet, poorly drained, crowded and shaded nurseries. Moderate watering, good drainage, sterilised soil and proper spacing help prevent it.

whyNot.A: Well-drained sterilised soil reduces damping-off.
whyNot.D: Wide spacing improves air flow and reduces the disease.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: Which of the following plant nutrients is a micronutrient (trace element)?
questions.explanation: Micronutrients are needed in very small amounts; they include zinc, iron, copper, manganese, boron and molybdenum. Nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium, magnesium and sulphur are macronutrients.

whyNot.A: Nitrogen is a major macronutrient.
whyNot.D: Potassium is a major macronutrient.
whyNot.B: Calcium is a secondary macronutrient, needed in fairly large amounts.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: After harvest, cocoa beans in Ondo State are heaped and covered with plantain leaves for about six days before drying. This fermentation is done mainly to
options: make the beans heavier for sale
develop the chocolate flavour and kill the beans so they cannot germinate
soften the pods so they can be opened
kill the black pod fungus in the field
questions.explanation: During fermentation the sweet pulp is broken down, heat and acids kill the embryo, and chemical changes inside the bean produce the substances that give chocolate its flavour and colour. Unfermented beans are of poor quality.

whyNot.A: Fermentation removes pulp and water; it does not make beans heavier.
whyNot.C: The pods are broken open before the beans are fermented.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: A male cattle that has been castrated and is raised for beef is called a
questions.explanation: A steer (or bullock) is a castrated male. Castration makes the animal calmer and easier to manage and fatten for beef.

whyNot.D: A heifer is a young female that has not yet calved.
whyNot.A: A bull is an uncastrated male used for breeding.
whyNot.B: A calf is a young cattle of either sex.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: Piglets kept on concrete floors are given an iron injection within a few days of birth mainly to prevent
questions.explanation: Sow's milk contains very little iron, and piglets on concrete cannot get iron from soil. Without extra iron they cannot make enough haemoglobin and develop anaemia, becoming weak and pale.

whyNot.B: Rickets is caused by lack of vitamin D, calcium or phosphorus.
whyNot.A: Swine fever is a viral disease; iron does not prevent it.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: Which of these farm animals is a monogastric (simple-stomached) animal?
questions.explanation: A pig has a single, simple stomach like a human. Cattle, sheep and goats are ruminants with a four-compartment stomach (rumen, reticulum, omasum and abomasum).

whyNot.B: The cow is a ruminant.
whyNot.A: The sheep is a ruminant.
whyNot.D: The goat is a ruminant.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: The act of giving birth in rabbits is called
questions.explanation: A doe rabbit kindles (gives birth) about 31 days after mating, usually in a nest she lines with fur.

whyNot.A: Kidding is giving birth in goats.
whyNot.D: Farrowing is giving birth in pigs.
whyNot.C: Lambing is giving birth in sheep.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: Gumboro disease (infectious bursal disease) is especially serious in young chicks because it
options: is caused by worms in the intestine
destroys the bursa of Fabricius and weakens the birds' immunity
only affects birds older than one year
blocks the crop with undigested feed
questions.explanation: Gumboro is a viral disease that attacks the bursa of Fabricius, an organ that produces immune cells in young chicks. Affected birds may die, and survivors respond poorly to other vaccines and infections. It is prevented by vaccination.

whyNot.A: Gumboro is caused by a virus, not worms.
whyNot.C: It mainly affects young chicks, usually from about three to six weeks of age.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: A farmer in Oyo State has 250 laying hens which produce 200 eggs in one day. What is the hen-day egg production for that day?
questions.explanation: Hen-day production = eggs laid ÷ hens present × 100 = 200 ÷ 250 × 100 = 80%.

whyNot.D: 20% is the percentage of hens that did not lay (50 ÷ 250).
whyNot.A: 125% divides the hens by the eggs (250 ÷ 200), the wrong way round.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: A ranch in Plateau State has 120 ha of pasture. Its carrying capacity is one head of cattle per 2.5 ha. How many cattle can it support without overgrazing?
questions.explanation: Number of cattle = total pasture ÷ area needed per animal = 120 ÷ 2.5 = 48 head.

whyNot.A: 300 multiplies 120 by 2.5 instead of dividing.
whyNot.C: 4.8 divides 120 by 25 instead of 2.5.
whyNot.D: 30 divides 120 by 4 instead of 2.5.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: A fish farmer applies poultry manure to his earthen pond before stocking it with tilapia. The main purpose is to
options: kill predatory fish in the pond
reduce the amount of oxygen in the water
encourage the growth of plankton as natural fish food
questions.explanation: Manure releases nutrients that make tiny plants and animals (plankton) multiply in the water. Plankton is natural food for tilapia and fry, so fertilising the pond reduces feed costs.

whyNot.A: Farmers add lime to correct acidity; making the water acidic would harm the fish.
whyNot.C: Too much manure can lower oxygen, but that is a danger to avoid, not the purpose.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: A major advantage of artificial insemination (AI) in cattle breeding is that
options: semen from one superior bull can be used to breed very many cows
it prevents all diseases of the reproductive tract
it removes the need to detect when cows are on heat
questions.explanation: In AI, semen collected from a proven bull is diluted, stored and placed in many cows, even far away. This spreads good genes quickly and saves farmers the cost of keeping their own bull.

whyNot.D: Heat detection is still essential so that insemination is done at the right time.
whyNot.A: AI does not cause twins.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: To feed his cattle in the dry season, a farmer packs freshly cut green grass tightly into a pit, covers it to keep out air, and leaves it to ferment. The product is called
questions.explanation: Silage is green fodder preserved by fermentation in the absence of air. Bacteria convert sugars to acids, mainly lactic acid, which stop spoilage. It is stored in a pit or silo until needed.

whyNot.C: Hay is grass preserved by drying, not by fermenting it without air.
whyNot.B: Browse is leaves and twigs of shrubs and trees eaten directly.
whyNot.A: Concentrates are feeds rich in energy or protein, such as grains and oilseed cakes.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: The farm record that shows what a farm owns (assets) and what it owes (liabilities) on a particular date is the
questions.explanation: A balance sheet sets out the assets and liabilities of the business at a given date. The difference between them is the owner's net worth (capital).

whyNot.D: A farm diary records daily activities on the farm.
whyNot.B: A sales record lists produce sold, quantities and prices.
whyNot.C: A production record shows output such as yields or eggs laid.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: Mrs Bello decides to plant her only plot with cassava. If she had planted maize instead, she could have earned ₦400,000. The ₦400,000 she gave up is the
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative given up when a choice is made. By choosing cassava, she forgoes the ₦400,000 she would have earned from maize.

whyNot.B: A fixed cost is a cost that does not change with output, such as rent.
whyNot.A: Gross margin is revenue minus variable costs of the crop she actually grew.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: A farmer lists his needs in order of importance (first fertiliser, then a sprayer, then a new motorcycle) before deciding how to spend his money. This list is called a
questions.explanation: A scale of preference is a list of wants arranged in order of their importance. Because money is limited, the farmer satisfies the most important wants first.

whyNot.B: A farm budget estimates expected costs and returns of farm plans.
whyNot.D: A farm inventory is a list of all items owned on the farm and their values.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: A poultry farm spent a total of ₦1,800,000 to produce 600 crates of eggs. What is the average cost of producing one crate?
questions.explanation: Average cost = total cost ÷ quantity produced = ₦1,800,000 ÷ 600 = ₦3,000 per crate.

whyNot.D: ₦300 drops a zero in the division.
whyNot.C: ₦30,000 adds a zero in the division.
whyNot.B: ₦600 is the number of crates, not a cost.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: A yam farmer spent ₦2,000,000 on production and sold his harvest for ₦2,500,000. What was his profit as a percentage of cost?

whyNot.C: 20% is profit as a percentage of the selling price (500,000 ÷ 2,500,000).
whyNot.A: 80% is cost as a percentage of revenue.
whyNot.B: 125% is revenue as a percentage of cost.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: When the price of a bag of maize rises from ₦20,000 to ₦25,000, the quantity farmers supply to a market rises from 100 bags to 140 bags. What is the price elasticity of supply?
questions.explanation: Percentage change in quantity = (140 − 100) ÷ 100 × 100 = 40%. Percentage change in price = (25,000 − 20,000) ÷ 20,000 × 100 = 25%. Elasticity of supply = 40 ÷ 25 = 1.6, so supply is elastic.

whyNot.B: 0.625 divides the percentage change in price by the percentage change in quantity, the wrong way round.
whyNot.A: 0.4 is only the proportional change in quantity.
whyNot.C: 0.25 is only the proportional change in price.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: Commercial banks are often unwilling to lend to small-scale farmers mainly because the farmers
options: do not need money for their farms
are not allowed by law to borrow money
always repay loans before they are due
lack acceptable collateral and their farming is risky
questions.explanation: Small farmers often have no land title or other assets to pledge, and farming is exposed to risks such as drought, pests and price falls. Banks therefore see such loans as likely to fail.

whyNot.A: Small farmers greatly need credit for inputs and labour.
whyNot.B: No law stops farmers from borrowing.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: A trader buys rice cheaply at harvest, keeps it in a good store, and sells it months later when it is scarce. By storing it, the trader adds
questions.explanation: Storage makes produce available at a time when consumers want it and it is scarce, which is time utility. Buyers are willing to pay more for it then.

whyNot.D: Place utility is added by transporting produce to where it is needed.
whyNot.A: Form utility is added by processing, such as milling paddy into rice.
whyNot.C: Possession utility is added by transferring ownership to the buyer.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: A farmer who has heard about a new cassava variety plants it on a small part of his farm to see how it performs before deciding whether to grow it widely. He is at which stage of the adoption process?
questions.explanation: The stages of adoption are awareness, interest, evaluation, trial and adoption. In the trial stage the farmer tests the innovation on a small scale. If the results are good, he adopts it on a larger scale.

whyNot.D: At awareness, the farmer has only just heard of the idea.
whyNot.B: At interest, he seeks more information but has not yet tried it.
whyNot.C: Adoption is the full, continued use of the innovation on a large scale.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: In a farmers' marketing cooperative, part of the surplus at the end of the year is shared among members according to
options: the order in which members joined
the size of each member's family
the amount of business each member did with the cooperative
questions.explanation: Cooperatives share surplus as a patronage dividend: members who sold or bought more through the society receive more. This rewards use of the cooperative rather than capital or status.

whyNot.A: Age is not a basis for sharing cooperative surplus.
whyNot.B: Seniority of membership does not determine the share of the surplus.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: Which hand tool is used to gather grass and debris and to level the soil surface of a seedbed?
questions.explanation: A garden rake has a row of teeth on a long handle. It collects trash and breaks and levels the surface soil, leaving a smooth seedbed.

whyNot.C: A cutlass is for slashing and cutting.
whyNot.B: A pickaxe breaks hard ground.
whyNot.D: A sickle cuts grass and harvests cereals.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: Which tractor-powered implement uses rotating blades driven by the power take-off shaft to cut, break and mix the soil into a fine tilth in one operation?
questions.explanation: A rotavator (rotary tiller) has L-shaped blades on a shaft turned by the PTO. In one pass it cuts and pulverises the soil, doing the work of ploughing and harrowing together.

whyNot.A: A disc harrow's discs are pulled through the soil, not driven by the PTO, and it usually follows ploughing.
whyNot.C: A mouldboard plough turns the soil but leaves large clods.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: The radiator of a tractor engine helps to
options: filter dust from the air entering the engine
cool the engine by losing heat from the circulating water
questions.explanation: In a water-cooled engine, water picks up heat from the engine block and flows through the radiator, where air blown by the fan removes the heat. This prevents overheating.

whyNot.D: Fuel is stored in the fuel tank.
whyNot.A: The battery is charged by the alternator or dynamo.
whyNot.B: Dust is removed by the air cleaner.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: When the electrolyte level in a tractor's lead-acid battery falls below the plates, it should be topped up with
questions.explanation: Water in the electrolyte evaporates during charging. It is replaced with distilled water, which contains no dissolved minerals that could damage the plates.

whyNot.B: Oil would damage the battery and stop it working.
whyNot.C: Salt water contains impurities that damage the plates.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: A tractor uses 8 litres of diesel per hour and ploughs 0.5 ha per hour. If diesel costs ₦1,000 per litre, what is the fuel cost of ploughing 6 ha?
questions.explanation: Time needed = 6 ÷ 0.5 = 12 hours. Fuel used = 12 × 8 = 96 litres. Cost = 96 × ₦1,000 = ₦96,000.

whyNot.A: ₦24,000 multiplies 6 ha by 0.5 ha/h to get 3 hours instead of dividing.
whyNot.B: ₦48,000 uses 6 hours, as if the tractor ploughed 1 ha per hour.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: A triangular piece of farmland has a base of 120 m and a perpendicular height of 50 m. What is its area in hectares? (1 ha = 10,000 m²)
questions.explanation: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height = ½ × 120 × 50 = 3,000 m². In hectares: 3,000 ÷ 10,000 = 0.3 ha.

whyNot.A: 0.6 ha forgets the ½ in the formula for a triangle.
whyNot.C: 3 ha divides by 1,000 instead of 10,000.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: Which method of irrigation sprays water into the air through rotating nozzles so that it falls on the crops like rain?
questions.explanation: In sprinkler irrigation, water under pressure is pumped through pipes to nozzles that spray it over the crop, like rainfall. It suits uneven land and sandy soils.

whyNot.D: In furrow irrigation, water flows along channels between ridges.
whyNot.B: Basin irrigation floods level plots surrounded by low banks.
whyNot.C: Drip irrigation releases water slowly at the base of each plant.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: Driving heavy tractors repeatedly over wet farmland can harm the soil mainly by
options: increasing the number of earthworms in it
adding too much organic matter to it
compacting it so that water and roots cannot pass through easily
questions.explanation: The weight of heavy machines presses soil particles together, especially when the soil is wet. Compacted soil has fewer pore spaces, so drainage, aeration and root growth are poor.

whyNot.B: Tractor traffic does not add organic matter.
whyNot.C: Compaction affects soil structure, not its pH.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: In garri processing, which machine is used to squeeze water out of bagged, grated cassava mash?
questions.explanation: The grated mash is put in sacks and pressed with a hydraulic or screw press to remove water (dewatering). The pressed cake is then sieved and fried to make garri.

whyNot.A: The grater turns peeled tubers into mash before pressing.
whyNot.C: The fryer roasts the sieved mash after pressing.
whyNot.D: A hammer mill grinds dry materials such as grains.

questions.subject: agricultural-science
questions.stem: A tractor is stuck in mud with one rear wheel spinning while the other stays still. The driver should engage the
questions.explanation: The differential normally lets the rear wheels turn at different speeds when cornering, but it also sends power to the wheel with least grip. The differential lock makes both rear wheels turn together, so the wheel with grip can pull the tractor out.

whyNot.A: The PTO drives implements, not the wheels.
whyNot.C: The hydraulic lift raises and lowers implements.
whyNot.D: The hand throttle sets engine speed; more speed only spins the slipping wheel faster.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following best defines a citizen?
options: Any person who happens to be living in a country at a given time
A person who holds a public office in government
A legal member of a state who enjoys its rights and performs the duties it requires
A foreign visitor who has a valid entry visa
questions.explanation: A citizen is a full legal member of a state. He or she enjoys the rights the state guarantees (such as voting) and owes it duties (such as obeying its laws and paying taxes). Simply living in a country does not make a person a citizen.

whyNot.A: Foreigners (aliens) can live in a country without being its citizens.
whyNot.B: Most citizens hold no public office; office-holding is not what makes a person a citizen.
whyNot.D: A visa only allows a foreigner to enter; it does not confer membership of the state.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Ngozi arrives at school before assembly every day, wears the correct uniform and keeps to the school rules even when no teacher is watching. Which value does she show?
questions.explanation: Discipline is the habit of controlling one's behaviour and keeping to rules, time and order. Ngozi is punctual, properly dressed and obeys rules on her own, which is self-discipline.

whyNot.B: Contentment is being satisfied with what one has.
whyNot.A: Tolerance is accepting people whose views or beliefs differ from yours.
whyNot.D: Courage is facing danger or difficulty bravely.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: What is the main aim of teaching Civic Education in Nigerian schools?
options: To produce informed and responsible citizens who know their rights and duties
To train students to become professional politicians
To teach students the history of other countries
To prepare students only for careers in the civil service
questions.explanation: Civic Education teaches young people about their rights, duties and national values, and how government works, so that they grow into informed, responsible and patriotic citizens who take part usefully in national life.

whyNot.B: It is for every citizen, not only those who want to enter politics.
whyNot.D: It prepares students for life as citizens, whatever career they choose.
whyNot.C: The history of other countries belongs to History, not Civic Education.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following is a RIGHT of a Nigerian citizen rather than a duty?
options: Obeying the laws of the country
Owning property in any part of Nigeria
questions.explanation: A right is something the citizen is entitled to enjoy; a duty is something the citizen is expected to do for the state. Section 43 gives every citizen the right to acquire and own immovable property anywhere in Nigeria. Paying taxes, obeying laws and respecting the flag are duties.

whyNot.D: Paying taxes is a duty listed in section 24.
whyNot.A: Obeying the law is a basic duty of every citizen.
whyNot.B: Respecting national symbols is a duty listed in section 24.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: What do the yellow flowers (Costus spectabilis) at the base of Nigeria's coat of arms represent?
options: The two great rivers of Nigeria
The fertile soil of the land
questions.explanation: The green-and-yellow Costus spectabilis flowers on which the coat of arms stands represent the beauty of Nigeria. The eagle stands for strength, the black shield for fertile soil, and the white wavy Y for the Rivers Niger and Benue.

whyNot.B: Strength is shown by the red eagle at the top.
whyNot.C: The rivers are shown by the white wavy Y on the shield.
whyNot.D: The fertile soil is shown by the black shield.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Ifeoma was born in London. Both her parents are Nigerian citizens by birth. According to the 1999 Constitution, how is Ifeoma a Nigerian citizen?
options: By birth, because a person born outside Nigeria to a Nigerian parent is a citizen by birth
By registration, because she was born outside Nigeria
By naturalisation, after living in Nigeria for fifteen years
She cannot be a Nigerian citizen, because she was not born in Nigeria
questions.explanation: Section 25(1)(c) makes every person born outside Nigeria, either of whose parents is a citizen of Nigeria, a citizen by birth. Ifeoma's parents are Nigerian, so she is a Nigerian citizen by birth even though she was born in London.

whyNot.B: Registration is for others, such as foreign wives of Nigerians or adults born abroad whose grandparent (not parent) is Nigerian.
whyNot.C: Naturalisation is for foreigners with no Nigerian parent; Ifeoma already qualifies by birth.
whyNot.D: Place of birth is not the only route; descent from a Nigerian parent is enough.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Residents of a street in Enugu contribute money and labour every month to clear the blocked drains along their road. Which civic value are they showing?
questions.explanation: Cooperation means people working together for a common good. The residents pool their money and effort to solve a shared problem (blocked drains), which is cooperation and community spirit.

whyNot.C: Contentment is being satisfied with what one has, not joint action.
whyNot.D: Obedience is following orders or rules; nobody ordered them to do this.
whyNot.A: Courtesy is politeness and good manners towards others.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Why was the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) scheme established in 1973?
options: To train young graduates as electoral officers
To promote national unity by making young graduates serve in parts of Nigeria other than their own
To give young graduates loans to start businesses
To recruit young graduates into the Nigerian Army
questions.explanation: The NYSC was set up in 1973, shortly after the civil war, to rebuild national unity. Graduates spend a service year, usually in a state other than their own, where they learn other cultures and serve the host community.

whyNot.D: The NYSC is not military recruitment, although camp includes some drills.
whyNot.C: Giving loans is not the purpose of the scheme.
whyNot.A: Some corps members help INEC at elections, but that is not why the scheme was created.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Mr Oke, a Nigerian citizen aged 40, wishes to give up his Nigerian citizenship voluntarily. According to section 29 of the 1999 Constitution, how is this done?
options: He makes a declaration of renunciation, and he ceases to be a citizen when the President causes it to be registered
He simply leaves Nigeria and stops paying taxes
He applies to a High Court for an order cancelling his citizenship
He writes to the Senate, which votes on whether to accept his request
questions.explanation: Section 29 allows a citizen of full age (18 and above) to renounce Nigerian citizenship by making a declaration in the prescribed manner. The President causes the declaration to be registered, and on registration the person ceases to be a citizen. (The President may withhold registration while Nigeria is at war.)

whyNot.D: The Senate has no role in renunciation.
whyNot.B: Leaving the country or failing to pay tax does not end citizenship.
whyNot.C: Renunciation is by declaration and registration, not by a court order.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Section 23 of the 1999 Constitution lists Nigeria's national ethics. Which of the following is one of them?
questions.explanation: Section 23 states that the national ethics shall be Discipline, Integrity, Dignity of Labour, Social Justice, Religious Tolerance, Self-reliance and Patriotism. Dignity of labour is one of them.

whyNot.D: Putting one's ethnic group first works against national unity; it is not a national ethic.
whyNot.A: Gathering wealth is not listed; the Constitution stresses social justice instead.
whyNot.B: Party loyalty is not one of the national ethics.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: A state government sets up roadblocks to stop Nigerians from other states from entering it to live and work. Which fundamental right does this violate?
options: Right to private and family life
questions.explanation: Section 41 gives every citizen the right to move freely throughout Nigeria and to live in any part of it. Blocking citizens from other states from entering to live and work violates this right.

whyNot.D: Fair hearing concerns how courts and tribunals decide cases.
whyNot.C: Private and family life protects homes, correspondence and phone calls.
whyNot.B: Nobody is being killed; the right affected is movement.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Rights such as the right to vote, to contest elections and to join a political party are best described as
questions.explanation: Political rights allow citizens to take part in government: voting, being voted for, joining parties and holding public office.

whyNot.A: Economic rights relate to work, wages and property.
whyNot.D: Cultural rights relate to language, customs and taking part in cultural life.
whyNot.B: Social rights relate to things such as education, health and welfare.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following is an international non-governmental organisation that campaigns against human rights abuses around the world?
options: The Economic Community of West African States
The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
questions.explanation: Amnesty International, founded in London in 1961, is a non-governmental organisation that investigates and publicises human rights abuses such as torture and unlawful detention, and campaigns for victims.

whyNot.C: The IMF is an intergovernmental financial institution.
whyNot.A: ECOWAS is an intergovernmental regional body made up of states, not an NGO.
whyNot.D: OPEC is an organisation of oil-producing countries.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Bayo, a Christian student in a government school, is ordered to take part in a religious ceremony of a religion that is not his own. Which right is violated?
options: Right to dignity of the human person
Freedom of thought, conscience and religion
Freedom of expression and the press
questions.explanation: Section 38(2) states that no person attending a place of education shall be required to receive religious instruction or take part in a religious ceremony that relates to a religion other than his own. Forcing Bayo to do so violates his freedom of thought, conscience and religion.

whyNot.D: Freedom of expression concerns holding and sharing opinions and information.
whyNot.A: Dignity of the human person protects against torture, slavery and degrading treatment.
whyNot.B: Personal liberty protects against unlawful arrest and detention.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Police lock up Mr Eze for three weeks without charging him to court, because a friend complained that Mr Eze owes him money. Which right has been violated?
options: Right to acquire and own property
questions.explanation: Section 35 protects personal liberty: no one may be detained except in the cases and by the procedure the law allows, and a suspect must be taken to court within a short time. A debt is a civil matter, and holding someone for weeks without charge is unlawful detention.

whyNot.D: Freedom of movement concerns moving about and living anywhere in Nigeria; the main wrong here is the unlawful detention itself.
whyNot.A: His property has not been taken.
whyNot.C: He was not treated differently because of his ethnic group, sex, religion or origin.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Mallam Sani has been charged with an offence but cannot afford a lawyer. Which body in Nigeria can provide him with free legal representation?
options: The Nigerian Bar Association's disciplinary committee
The Legal Aid Council of Nigeria
questions.explanation: The Legal Aid Council of Nigeria provides free legal advice and representation to people who cannot afford lawyers, helping to protect their right to fair hearing.

whyNot.A: A disciplinary committee deals with misconduct by lawyers, not free representation.
whyNot.D: The National Judicial Council deals with the appointment and discipline of judges.
whyNot.B: The Code of Conduct Bureau deals with asset declarations by public officers.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which law, passed in 2003, brought the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child into Nigerian law?
questions.explanation: The Child's Rights Act 2003 domesticated the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child in Nigeria. It protects children from abuse, child labour, early marriage and neglect, and states adopt it into their own laws.

whyNot.B: The UBE Act provides for free and compulsory basic education, not the full range of child rights.
whyNot.A: The Labour Act regulates employment generally.
whyNot.D: The Electoral Act regulates elections.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Section 33 of the Constitution says a person is not regarded as deprived of life in breach of the right to life if death results from force that is reasonably necessary for one of some limited purposes. Which of these is one of those purposes?
options: Defending a person from unlawful violence
Punishing a suspect who refuses to confess
Recovering a debt that is long overdue
Breaking up a peaceful protest against the government
questions.explanation: Section 33(2) allows reasonably necessary force for the defence of any person from unlawful violence or the defence of property, to make a lawful arrest or prevent the escape of a lawfully detained person, or to suppress a riot, insurrection or mutiny.

whyNot.B: Forcing a confession is torture, which section 34 forbids.
whyNot.C: Debts are recovered through the courts, never by deadly force.
whyNot.D: A peaceful protest is not a riot; force against it is not allowed by section 33.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: In 2026 the National Assembly passes a law making a certain act a crime. Can a person be convicted under this law for doing that act in 2024?
options: Yes, if the President approves the prosecution
No, but only if the person was under 18 in 2024
No, because a person cannot be guilty of an offence for an act that was not an offence when it was done
Yes, because a new law applies to everything that happened before it
questions.explanation: Section 36(8) protects against retroactive criminal laws: no one shall be held guilty of a criminal offence for an act that did not, at the time it took place, constitute an offence. The 2024 act was lawful when done, so the person cannot be convicted.

whyNot.D: Criminal laws cannot be applied backwards to punish past acts.
whyNot.A: Presidential approval cannot override a fundamental right.
whyNot.B: The protection applies to everyone, whatever their age.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Where is the seat of the African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights, set up to enforce the African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights?
questions.explanation: The African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights sits in Arusha, Tanzania. It complements the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights in protecting the rights in the African Charter.

whyNot.A: Abuja hosts the ECOWAS Community Court of Justice, a different court.
whyNot.C: Banjul hosts the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights, not the Court.
whyNot.D: Addis Ababa is the headquarters of the African Union, not the seat of this court.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following is a key feature of democracy?
options: A ban on criticism of government
Rule by a single party that cannot be voted out
Leaders who hold office for life
questions.explanation: In a democracy the people choose and change their leaders through regular, free and fair elections. This keeps leaders accountable to the people.

whyNot.C: One-party rule with no chance of removal is a feature of authoritarian systems.
whyNot.D: Life tenure denies the people the chance to change leaders.
whyNot.B: Democracy protects the freedom to criticise government.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: The principle that no person or government is above the law, and that everyone is subject to the same law, is called
questions.explanation: The rule of law means the law is supreme: government acts only according to law, and all persons, rich or poor, ruler or ruled, are subject to the same law and the ordinary courts.

whyNot.D: Separation of powers is the sharing of government functions among three arms.
whyNot.A: Delegated legislation is law made by bodies to which the legislature has given power.
whyNot.C: Federal character is about fair spread of appointments among states.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which arm of government makes laws for Nigeria at the federal level?
questions.explanation: The legislature makes laws. At the federal level Nigeria's legislature is the National Assembly, made up of the Senate and the House of Representatives.

whyNot.B: The Federal Executive Council is part of the executive, which carries out laws.
whyNot.C: The Supreme Court is part of the judiciary, which interprets laws.
whyNot.D: The police enforce laws; they do not make them.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: The President nominates a person as a minister, but the person cannot be appointed until the Senate confirms the nomination. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Checks and balances means each arm of government can limit the others to prevent abuse of power. Section 147 makes the appointment of ministers subject to Senate confirmation, so the legislature checks the executive.

whyNot.A: Delegated legislation is law-making by bodies authorised by the legislature.
whyNot.B: Judicial review is the courts' power to declare laws or actions unconstitutional.
whyNot.C: Fusion of powers is the combining of executive and legislative roles, as in a parliamentary system.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: What is universal adult suffrage?
options: The right of only educated adults to vote
The right of only taxpayers and property owners to vote
The right of every person living in a country, including foreigners, to vote
The right of all qualified adult citizens to vote, regardless of sex, wealth, religion or education
questions.explanation: Universal adult suffrage gives the vote to all citizens who have reached the voting age (18 in Nigeria) and are otherwise qualified, without restrictions based on sex, wealth, religion, ethnic group or education.

whyNot.A: Limiting the vote to the educated is a restricted franchise.
whyNot.C: Foreigners do not vote in national elections; suffrage is for citizens.
whyNot.B: A property or tax qualification is a restricted franchise, not universal suffrage.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following is a main function of political parties in a democracy?
options: Sponsoring candidates for elections and offering policy choices to voters
Appointing judges of the High Court
questions.explanation: Political parties bring together people with similar ideas, sponsor candidates for elections, present programmes to voters, form the government when they win, and act as opposition when they lose.

whyNot.D: Interpreting the Constitution is the work of the courts.
whyNot.A: Elections are conducted by electoral commissions such as INEC, not by parties.
whyNot.C: Judges are appointed through the judicial service commissions and the executive, not by parties.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which body has the power under the 1999 Constitution to register political parties in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Third Schedule of the Constitution gives INEC the power to register political parties, monitor their organisation and operations, and examine their finances, in addition to organising federal and state elections.

whyNot.A: The National Assembly makes laws; it does not register parties.
whyNot.B: The Ministry of Justice handles legal matters for government.
whyNot.C: The Corporate Affairs Commission registers companies and business names, not political parties.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: A foreign ambassador in Abuja commits a traffic offence but cannot be tried in a Nigerian court. Which limitation on the rule of law does this show?
questions.explanation: Under international law, diplomats enjoy immunity from the courts of the country where they serve. This means they are not equal before the local law, which is a limitation on the rule of law.

whyNot.C: Delegated legislation is law made by subordinate bodies.
whyNot.B: Judicial precedent is courts following earlier decisions.
whyNot.D: Federal character concerns fair representation of states in appointments.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: The President appoints the Chief Justice of Nigeria on the recommendation of the National Judicial Council. Whose confirmation is also required?
questions.explanation: Section 231(1) provides that the Chief Justice of Nigeria is appointed by the President on the recommendation of the National Judicial Council, subject to confirmation by the Senate. This lets the legislature check appointments to the judiciary.

whyNot.A: The House of Representatives does not confirm judicial appointments.
whyNot.D: The Council of State is an advisory body; it does not confirm the appointment.
whyNot.C: The Federal Executive Council is part of the executive, which already makes the appointment.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: A candidate wants to challenge the result of a presidential election in Nigeria. In which court must the petition first be filed?
options: The High Court of the Federal Capital Territory
questions.explanation: Section 239(1) gives the Court of Appeal exclusive original jurisdiction to hear petitions on whether a person has been validly elected as President or Vice-President. Appeals from its decision then go to the Supreme Court.

whyNot.C: The Federal High Court does not hear presidential election petitions.
whyNot.D: The Supreme Court hears such cases only on appeal from the Court of Appeal.
whyNot.A: The FCT High Court has no jurisdiction over presidential election petitions.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: During a WASSCE paper, a candidate is caught with written notes on the subject hidden in his pocket. What is this offence called?
questions.explanation: Examination malpractice is any dishonest act meant to gain an unfair advantage in an examination, such as bringing in unauthorised notes, copying or leaking questions.

whyNot.A: Impersonation is when one person writes an examination for another.
whyNot.B: Plagiarism is presenting someone else's written work as your own, as in essays and projects.
whyNot.D: Truancy is staying away from school without permission.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following is a harmful effect of drug abuse on the user?
options: Damage to organs such as the brain and liver
questions.explanation: Drug abuse can damage the brain, liver, lungs and heart, cause mental illness, weaken the body's defences and lead to addiction, poor school work and broken family relationships.

whyNot.A: Drug abuse usually reduces concentration and leads to poor academic performance.
whyNot.B: Many drugs weaken the body, and sharing needles spreads infections such as HIV.
whyNot.C: Drug abuse commonly causes conflict and breakdown in family relationships.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: In HIV prevention education, what does "ABC" stand for?
questions.explanation: The ABC approach to preventing sexual transmission of HIV is: Abstain from sex, Be faithful to one uninfected partner, and use Condoms correctly and consistently if not abstaining.

whyNot.D: There is no cure for HIV; treatment controls the virus.
whyNot.A: Antibiotics treat bacteria and do not prevent HIV, which is a virus.
whyNot.B: Body cleanliness does not prevent HIV transmission.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following drugs is a depressant, slowing down the activity of the central nervous system?
questions.explanation: Depressants slow down the brain and nervous system, causing drowsiness, slow reactions and poor judgement. Alcohol is a depressant, which is why drinking and driving is dangerous.

whyNot.B: Amphetamine is a stimulant; it speeds up the nervous system.
whyNot.D: Caffeine (in coffee and kola nut) is a mild stimulant.
whyNot.C: Cocaine is a strong stimulant.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Drugs such as LSD, which make the user see or hear things that are not real, belong to which group?
questions.explanation: Hallucinogens distort the user's perception, causing them to see, hear or feel things that are not there. LSD is a well-known hallucinogen.

whyNot.C: Depressants slow down body activity but do not mainly cause hallucinations.
whyNot.B: Stimulants speed up the nervous system and make the user feel alert.
whyNot.D: Antibiotics are medicines that fight bacterial infections.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following is the most effective step a school can take to reduce cultism among its students?
options: Allowing cult groups to register openly as clubs
Ignoring cult activity so as not to provoke the members
Closing the school whenever a cult clash occurs
Running orientation and counselling programmes and firmly punishing proven cult activity
questions.explanation: Cultism is best reduced by educating students on its dangers, providing counselling and healthy clubs and sports, and applying the school rules firmly to anyone proven to be involved.

whyNot.A: Registering cults gives them legitimacy and helps them recruit.
whyNot.B: Ignoring cult activity allows it to grow and become more violent.
whyNot.C: Closing the school punishes all students and does not deal with the cause.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Soon after a person is infected with HIV, a test may still show a negative result because the body has not yet produced enough antibodies. What is this period called?
questions.explanation: The window period is the time between HIV infection and when a test can detect it. A person can test negative during this time yet still pass on the virus, so a repeat test is advised.

whyNot.D: The time from HIV infection to AIDS is usually several years, not the short testing gap.
whyNot.A: There is no recovery from HIV; it can be controlled but not cured.
whyNot.C: HIV weakens immunity; there is no 'immunity period'.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following is a PULL factor (something that attracts victims) rather than a PUSH factor in human trafficking?
options: Promises of well-paid jobs and a better life abroad
Conflict and insecurity in the victim's area
questions.explanation: Push factors are conditions at home that drive people to leave, such as poverty, unemployment and conflict. Pull factors are attractions elsewhere, such as the promise of good jobs, education or wealth abroad, which traffickers use as bait.

whyNot.A: Poverty at home pushes people out; it does not pull them anywhere.
whyNot.D: Unemployment at home is a push factor.
whyNot.C: Conflict and insecurity drive people away, so they are push factors.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: After months of taking a drug, Kunle finds that he needs larger and larger doses to get the same effect he once got from a small dose. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Tolerance develops when the body adapts to a drug, so the user needs more of it to get the same effect. It is a warning sign of developing dependence (addiction).

whyNot.B: Withdrawal is the set of unpleasant symptoms when a dependent person stops the drug.
whyNot.A: An overdose is taking a dangerous amount that poisons the body.
whyNot.C: Relapse is going back to drug use after a period of stopping.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Why is HIV not transmitted from person to person by mosquito bites?
options: Mosquitoes carry only the malaria parasite and no other organism
HIV is killed by the heat of the human body
Mosquitoes bite only people who are already infected
HIV cannot multiply in the mosquito, and the mosquito does not inject the previous person's blood when it bites
questions.explanation: When a mosquito bites, it injects saliva through a separate channel, not blood from its last meal. HIV also cannot survive and multiply inside the mosquito, so mosquitoes do not spread HIV, unlike malaria parasites that do develop inside them.

whyNot.C: Mosquitoes bite anyone, infected or not.
whyNot.B: HIV lives and multiplies at normal body temperature.
whyNot.A: Mosquitoes carry other organisms too, such as the viruses of yellow fever and dengue.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following persons is a civil servant?
options: A manager in a private commercial bank
A clerk in the Federal Ministry of Education
A member of the House of Representatives
questions.explanation: Civil servants are career officials employed in government ministries and departments to carry out government policies. A clerk in a federal ministry is a civil servant.

whyNot.D: Legislators are elected political office holders, not civil servants.
whyNot.A: Commissioners are political appointees who head ministries for a time.
whyNot.B: A private bank manager works in the private sector.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Members of an association carry placards and march peacefully through the streets of Lagos to draw public attention to their demands. Which method of pressure group activity is this?
questions.explanation: A demonstration (protest march) is a public gathering or procession to show support for or opposition to something and attract the attention of government and the public.

whyNot.B: Lobbying is private persuasion of lawmakers or officials.
whyNot.A: Litigation is going to court.
whyNot.C: A boycott is refusing to buy, use or take part in something.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: A clerk in a government office refuses to release a citizen's approved file unless the citizen pays him money. Which problem of the civil service does this show?
questions.explanation: Demanding money before performing an official duty is bribery, a form of corruption. It makes public services costly and unfair, and it is an offence that agencies like the ICPC investigate.

whyNot.A: Anonymity is a principle of the civil service, not a problem.
whyNot.D: Political neutrality is a principle of the civil service, not a problem.
whyNot.C: Permanence is a feature of the civil service, not a problem.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of the Federal Civil Service Commission?
options: Settling disputes between states in court
Making laws for the federal civil service
Appointing, promoting and disciplining federal civil servants
questions.explanation: The Federal Civil Service Commission, set up under the Constitution, has power to appoint persons to offices in the federal civil service and to promote, discipline and dismiss them. This keeps such decisions out of the hands of politicians.

whyNot.C: Laws are made by the National Assembly.
whyNot.B: Federal elections are conducted by INEC.
whyNot.A: Disputes between states are settled by the Supreme Court.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: An association campaigns against the cutting down of forests in Cross River State, although its members gain no personal benefit from the cause. What type of pressure group is it?
questions.explanation: A promotional or cause group works for a cause it believes benefits society as a whole, such as protecting the environment or human rights, rather than the private interests of its own members.

whyNot.D: An interest group, such as a trade union, protects the interests of its own members.
whyNot.B: An anomic group is a spontaneous, unorganised outburst such as a riot.
whyNot.C: A political party seeks to win elections and form the government.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: How does civil society differ from government?
options: It consists only of the armed forces and police
It is made up of the three arms of government
It consists of companies owned by the federal government
It is made up of voluntary, non-state organisations that people form on their own
questions.explanation: Civil society is the space of voluntary organisations outside the state, such as NGOs, religious bodies, trade unions, professional associations and community groups. Citizens form them freely to pursue shared interests and to hold government accountable.

whyNot.B: The arms of government are the state itself, not civil society.
whyNot.A: The armed forces and police are state institutions.
whyNot.C: Government-owned companies are part of the public sector.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Mrs Adeyemi has just been sworn in as a public officer. To which body must she declare her assets, as required by the Code of Conduct for public officers?
questions.explanation: Under the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution, public officers must declare their assets and liabilities to the Code of Conduct Bureau on taking office and at set intervals. This helps to detect and prevent corruption.

whyNot.A: INEC conducts elections and registers parties.
whyNot.C: The Public Complaints Commission investigates complaints of administrative injustice.
whyNot.B: The NHRC deals with human rights abuses.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: In a ministry, officers are arranged in grades and ranks, and each officer reports to a superior above him or her. Which feature of the civil service is this?
questions.explanation: Hierarchy means a chain of command in which officers are arranged from the highest (such as the Permanent Secretary) to the lowest, and instructions flow downward while reports flow upward.

whyNot.C: Anonymity means civil servants are not publicly credited or blamed for policies.
whyNot.B: Neutrality means civil servants do not take sides in party politics.
whyNot.A: Impartiality means treating all citizens fairly and equally.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: A public officer is accused of making a false declaration of his assets. Which body has the power to try him for this breach of the Code of Conduct?
questions.explanation: The Code of Conduct Bureau receives and checks declarations and refers breaches, but trials are conducted by the Code of Conduct Tribunal, which can punish a guilty officer, for example by removal from office or disqualification.

whyNot.D: The Bureau receives declarations and investigates; it does not try cases.
whyNot.B: The National Judicial Council deals with judges, not public officers generally.
whyNot.C: The Civil Service Commission handles discipline of civil servants but not Code of Conduct trials.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Angry residents suddenly pour into the streets and set up bonfires after a fatal accident, without any leaders or organisation. In the classification of pressure groups, this is an example of
questions.explanation: Anomic groups are spontaneous, unorganised and often short-lived outbursts, such as riots and sudden protests, with no formal leadership or membership. They arise from strong feelings about an event.

whyNot.D: Institutional groups operate within government institutions, such as groups within the army or civil service.
whyNot.A: Associational groups are formally organised bodies, such as trade unions and professional associations.
whyNot.C: Promotional groups are organised bodies that pursue a cause.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: A Ghanaian trader who lives and works in Onitsha but has not become a Nigerian citizen is best described as
questions.explanation: An alien is a person living in a country of which he or she is not a citizen. Since the trader has not acquired Nigerian citizenship, he is an alien in Nigeria.

whyNot.B: Registration would make him a citizen, but he has not acquired citizenship.
whyNot.A: Naturalisation would also make him a citizen, which he is not.
whyNot.D: A dual citizen holds the citizenship of two countries; he holds only Ghanaian citizenship.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Kemi's parents cannot afford an expensive phone for her. She is satisfied with what she has and does not envy or steal from her classmates. Which value does she show?
questions.explanation: Contentment is being satisfied with what one has and not desiring other people's property by dishonest means. It helps people avoid greed, theft and corruption.

whyNot.A: Courage is facing danger or difficulty bravely.
whyNot.B: Diligence is working hard and carefully.
whyNot.D: Patriotism is love and loyalty to one's country.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: After secondary school, Emeka learns tailoring and opens his own shop instead of waiting for a government job. Which value does he show?
questions.explanation: Self-reliance is depending on one's own skills and effort to meet one's needs. Emeka used his skill to create his own job, which is self-reliance, one of the national ethics in section 23.

whyNot.D: Tolerance is accepting people with different views or beliefs.
whyNot.B: Obedience is following rules or orders.
whyNot.C: Contentment is being satisfied with what one has, not creating new opportunities.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following is a requirement for a foreigner applying for Nigerian citizenship by naturalisation under section 27 of the 1999 Constitution?
options: Having at least one Nigerian grandparent
Being a registered member of a political party
Being married to a Nigerian man
Being acceptable to the local community in which he intends to live permanently
questions.explanation: Section 27(2) requires, among other things, that the applicant be of full age and good character, intend to live in Nigeria, be acceptable to the local community where he is to live (in the Governor's opinion), be able to contribute usefully, take the Oath of Allegiance and have lived in Nigeria for the required period.

whyNot.A: A Nigerian grandparent is a ground for registration, not naturalisation.
whyNot.C: Marriage to a Nigerian man is a ground for registration.
whyNot.B: Party membership has nothing to do with citizenship.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following can a Nigerian citizen do that a foreigner living lawfully in Nigeria cannot?
options: Go to court to seek justice
Enjoy protection of his or her life by the police
questions.explanation: Political rights such as voting and contesting elections belong only to citizens. Rights such as life, fair hearing and freedom of religion protect every person in Nigeria, including foreigners.

whyNot.A: Access to the courts and fair hearing is available to every person.
whyNot.B: Freedom of religion protects every person in Nigeria.
whyNot.D: The police must protect the lives of everyone in Nigeria, citizen or not.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: A cashier in a government office refuses a large bribe offered to her to approve a fake payment voucher. Which value does she show?
questions.explanation: Integrity means holding firmly to moral principles and doing what is right even when one could profit from doing wrong. Refusing a bribe to approve a fraud shows integrity.

whyNot.A: Tolerance is accepting people who are different from you.
whyNot.B: Courtesy is politeness and good manners.
whyNot.D: Self-reliance is depending on one's own effort to meet one's needs.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Musa, a university graduate, works happily as a vulcaniser while looking for another job, saying that no honest work is shameful. Which value does Musa hold?
questions.explanation: Dignity of labour is the belief that all honest work deserves respect, whether it is done with the hands or in an office. It is one of the national ethics in section 23.

whyNot.D: Social justice is fairness in sharing wealth and opportunities in society.
whyNot.B: Religious tolerance is respecting people of other faiths.
whyNot.C: Musa is not accepting poverty; he is working and still seeking better opportunities.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: In what way does the NYSC scheme help to promote national unity?
options: Corps members are given land in the states where they serve
Corps members are usually posted to serve in states other than their own
Corps members are posted only to their own home states
Corps members are trained to become soldiers
questions.explanation: Corps members usually serve in states other than their own. Living and working among people of other ethnic groups helps them understand other cultures, break down prejudice and build friendships across the country.

whyNot.C: Posting people only to their home states would defeat the aim of mixing Nigerians.
whyNot.D: Orientation camp includes drills, but corps members are not trained as soldiers.
whyNot.A: The scheme does not give land to corps members.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Under section 30 of the 1999 Constitution, the President may deprive a naturalised citizen of citizenship if, within a certain period after naturalisation, the person is sentenced to imprisonment for at least three years. What is that period?
questions.explanation: Section 30(1) allows the President to deprive a person who is not a citizen by birth or by registration (that is, a naturalised citizen) of citizenship if, within seven years after becoming naturalised, the person has been sentenced to imprisonment for a term of not less than three years.

whyNot.A: Two years is not the period stated in section 30.
whyNot.B: Fifteen years is the residence period for naturalisation under section 27, not this period.
whyNot.D: Twenty-five years is not stated anywhere in this section.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Kofi, aged 30, was born in Accra. Neither of his parents is Nigerian, but his grandmother is a Nigerian citizen. By which means does the 1999 Constitution allow him to become a Nigerian citizen?
options: By naturalisation only, after fifteen years in Nigeria
By an honorary award from the President
questions.explanation: Section 26(2)(b) allows a person of full age and capacity born outside Nigeria, any of whose grandparents is a Nigerian citizen, to be registered as a citizen. Citizenship by birth outside Nigeria (section 25(1)(c)) requires a Nigerian parent, which Kofi does not have.

whyNot.A: Being born abroad, Kofi would need a Nigerian parent to be a citizen by birth.
whyNot.B: He does not need to go through naturalisation, because registration is open to him.
whyNot.C: There is no 'honorary award' route to citizenship in the Constitution.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Teachers in a state form a trade union to press for better working conditions. Which fundamental right allows them to do this?
options: Right to private and family life
Right to peaceful assembly and association
questions.explanation: Section 40 gives every person the right to assemble freely and associate with others, and in particular to form or belong to any political party, trade union or other association to protect his or her interests.

whyNot.B: Freedom of movement is about moving and living anywhere in Nigeria.
whyNot.D: Fair hearing concerns trials and decisions by courts and tribunals.
whyNot.A: Private and family life protects homes, letters and phone calls.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following is an economic, social and cultural right rather than a civil and political right?
questions.explanation: Economic, social and cultural rights relate to people's welfare, such as education, health, work and an adequate standard of living. Civil and political rights include voting, fair hearing and freedom of expression.

whyNot.D: Voting is a political right.
whyNot.B: Fair hearing is a civil right.
whyNot.C: Freedom of expression is a civil and political right.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following most often prevents people in rural areas from enjoying their fundamental rights?
options: Too many courts in rural areas
The existence of a written constitution
Too much freedom of the press
Illiteracy and ignorance of their rights
