questions.explanation: The Sunnah has three types: what the Prophet said (qawliyyah), what he did (fi'liyyah), and what he saw or heard others do and approved by silence or agreement (taqririyyah). Here the Prophet only watched and did not object, so it is tacit approval.

whyNot.A: The Prophet said nothing, so it is not a saying.
whyNot.B: The action was the Companion's, not the Prophet's own.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Which practice did the Prophet (SAW) describe as 'half of faith' (shatr al-iman), in a hadith in Sahih Muslim?
questions.explanation: In the hadith narrated by Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, the Prophet (SAW) said: 'Purification is half of faith.' It shows how important cleanliness of body, clothing and place is in Islam.

whyNot.C: Fasting is a pillar of Islam but was not called half of faith in this hadith.
whyNot.A: Zakat is mentioned elsewhere as a proof of faith, not as half of it.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: The hadith 'Islam is built upon five: testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing salat, paying zakat, Hajj and fasting in Ramadan' was narrated by
questions.explanation: This hadith, recorded by al-Bukhari and Muslim, is narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar, son of the second caliph. It lists the five pillars on which Islam stands, like the supports of a building.

whyNot.A: Abu Hurairah narrated the most hadith, but this one is from Ibn Umar.
whyNot.B: Anas ibn Malik, the Prophet's servant, narrated other well-known hadith, not this one.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Emeka's Muslim neighbour Yusuf shares his food with him and helps him as he would want to be helped. Yusuf is acting on which hadith?
options: 'None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself'
'Whoever is not grateful to people is not grateful to Allah'
questions.explanation: The hadith narrated by Anas ibn Malik teaches that complete faith includes wanting for others the good you want for yourself. Treating others as you would like to be treated, as Yusuf does, is exactly this teaching.

whyNot.A: That hadith is about the intention behind deeds, not about loving good for others.
whyNot.D: 'Do not get angry' teaches control of anger, which is not the point of this situation.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: 'The strong man is not the one who overcomes others in wrestling; the strong man is the one who controls himself when he is angry.' What does this hadith mainly teach?
options: Muslims should not take part in sports
Self-control in anger is true strength
Physical strength is useless in Islam
An angry person should never be forgiven
questions.explanation: The hadith, recorded by al-Bukhari and Muslim from Abu Hurairah, changes the meaning of strength: real strength is the ability to hold back one's anger, not to beat others physically.

whyNot.A: The hadith uses wrestling as an example; it does not forbid sport.
whyNot.C: It does not condemn physical strength; it says self-control is the greater strength.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: A hadith reported by so many narrators at every stage of its chain that it is impossible for them all to have agreed on a lie is called
questions.explanation: A mutawatir hadith is transmitted by a large number of people at every level of the chain, so its authenticity is certain. A hadith that does not reach this level is called ahad.

whyNot.D: Ahad is the opposite: a hadith with fewer narrators than mutawatir.
whyNot.A: Mawdu' means fabricated, the weakest possible category.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: A hadith that meets the conditions of a sahih hadith, except that one of its narrators is slightly weaker in precise memory, is classified as
questions.explanation: Hadith scholars rank reports as sahih (sound), hasan (good) and da'if (weak). A hasan hadith has a connected chain of upright narrators and no hidden defect, but one narrator's precision is a little below the sahih standard. It is still accepted as evidence.

whyNot.A: A da'if hadith fails one or more conditions of acceptance, such as a broken chain or an unreliable narrator.
whyNot.D: Mawdu' is a report invented and falsely attributed to the Prophet.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Riyad as-Salihin (Gardens of the Righteous), a popular collection of hadith arranged under moral topics, was compiled by
questions.explanation: Imam Yahya ibn Sharaf an-Nawawi (died 676 AH) compiled Riyad as-Salihin, gathering hadith on manners, worship and character under chapter headings. He also compiled the famous Forty Hadith.

whyNot.B: Imam Malik compiled al-Muwatta', not Riyad as-Salihin.
whyNot.A: Abu Hanifah founded the Hanafi school of law; he did not compile this collection.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Which of these scholars compiled a Sunan that is one of the six major hadith collections (al-Kutub as-Sittah)?
questions.explanation: Abu Dawud as-Sijistani compiled the Sunan Abi Dawud, which focuses on hadith used for legal rulings. It is one of the six major collections, with the works of al-Bukhari, Muslim, at-Tirmidhi, an-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah.

whyNot.C: Ibn Ishaq wrote an early biography (sirah) of the Prophet, not one of the six hadith books.
whyNot.B: Ibn Khaldun was a historian known for his Muqaddimah.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: To which prophet was the Injil (Gospel) revealed?
questions.explanation: Muslims believe in the revealed books: the Suhuf to Ibrahim, the Tawrah to Musa, the Zabur to Dawud, the Injil to Isa and the Qur'an to Muhammad (SAW). The Injil was revealed to Isa.

whyNot.D: The Tawrah was revealed to Musa.
whyNot.A: The Zabur was revealed to Dawud.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Which angel is commonly taught to be in charge of rain and the provision of creatures?
questions.explanation: Islamic teaching names several angels with special duties. Mika'il (Michael) is responsible for rain and sustenance; Jibril brings revelation; Israfil will blow the trumpet; Malik guards Hell.

whyNot.B: Jibril's duty is to bring revelation to the prophets.
whyNot.A: Israfil is the angel who will blow the trumpet on the Last Day.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Which of the following is one of the acts of wudu named in Qur'an 5:6?
options: Wiping the back of the neck
questions.explanation: Qur'an 5:6 commands believers, when they rise for prayer, to wash their faces and their arms up to the elbows, wipe their heads, and wash their feet up to the ankles. Washing the face is one of these acts named in the verse.

whyNot.A: Wiping the neck is not mentioned in the verse.
whyNot.B: Rinsing the mouth is taught from the Prophet's practice, not named in Qur'an 5:6.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Which of the following breaks a Muslim's wudu?
questions.explanation: Wudu is broken by anything that comes out of the private parts, such as urine, stool or wind, as well as by deep sleep and loss of consciousness. Passing wind therefore breaks wudu, and the person must perform wudu again before salat.

whyNot.D: Reciting the Qur'an is an act of worship; it does not break wudu.
whyNot.C: Drinking water breaks a fast, but not wudu.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Musa forgot to sit for the first tashahhud in Zuhr prayer. What does he do to make up for this mistake?
options: Perform tayammum and repeat the prayer
Perform the prostration of forgetfulness (sujud as-sahw)
questions.explanation: Sujud as-sahw is two prostrations made to repair a mistake in salat caused by forgetfulness, such as missing the first tashahhud or adding an extra act. The schools differ on whether it is done before or after the salam, but all teach sujud as-sahw for such a mistake.

whyNot.C: Tayammum replaces wudu when there is no water; it does not repair a forgotten part of salat.
whyNot.B: Fasting as expiation is for other matters, such as a broken oath, not for forgetting in salat.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: According to Qur'an 2:184, what should a Muslim who is travelling in Ramadan and chooses not to fast do?
options: Fast double the days the next Ramadan
Pay a fine to the imam for each day
Make up the missed days later
Nothing, because the days are cancelled
questions.explanation: Qur'an 2:184 says: 'Whoever among you is sick or on a journey, then an equal number of other days.' The traveller may break the fast and must make up the same number of days after Ramadan.

whyNot.B: No fine to the imam is prescribed; the days are made up by fasting.
whyNot.D: The days are not cancelled; they must be fasted later.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: In the Maliki school, which most Nigerian Muslims follow, which of the following is required for a valid marriage contract?
options: A written certificate from the government
A wedding feast before the contract
questions.explanation: In the Maliki school (as in the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools), a marriage is not valid without the bride's wali, along with the dowry (mahr), the offer and acceptance, and witnesses or public announcement. The Hanafi school differs and lets an adult woman contract her own marriage.

whyNot.B: Registration may be required by civil law, but it is not a condition of the Islamic contract.
whyNot.D: The walimah (wedding feast) is a sunnah held after the marriage, not a condition of the contract.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Mallam Garba harvests 640 bags of maize from a farm watered only by rain. How many bags must he give as zakat on the harvest?
questions.explanation: Zakat on crops is one-tenth (10%) when the farm is watered by rain or rivers without cost, and one-twentieth (5%) when it is watered by irrigation with effort or cost. Rain-fed: 640 × 1/10 = 64 bags.

whyNot.D: 32 bags is 5%, the rate for crops watered by irrigation.
whyNot.C: 16 bags is 2.5%, the rate for money and trade goods, not crops.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: In the source of Islamic law called ijma', a ruling is based on
options: A vote by all adult Muslims in a town
The customs of the Arabs before Islam
The agreement of qualified Muslim scholars on a matter
The personal opinion of the ruler of the day
questions.explanation: Ijma' means consensus: when the qualified scholars (mujtahidun) of the Muslim community agree on a ruling after the Prophet's time, the ruling becomes binding. It is the third source of Shari'ah after the Qur'an and Sunnah.

whyNot.D: A ruler's opinion alone does not make ijma'.
whyNot.A: Ijma' is the agreement of qualified scholars, not a popular vote.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Which act is the essential pillar of Hajj, without which the Hajj is not valid?
options: Standing at Arafat on the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah
Shaving the head before entering ihram
Visiting the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Hajj is Arafah.' Standing (wuquf) at the plain of Arafat on the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah is the central pillar; a pilgrim who misses it has missed the Hajj for that year.

whyNot.D: Visiting Madinah is a recommended visit, not a part of Hajj.
whyNot.C: Shaving or cutting the hair is done at the end of the rites, not before ihram, and is not the essential pillar.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Who took care of the young Muhammad (SAW) immediately after the death of his mother, Aminah?
questions.explanation: Muhammad's father Abdullah died before he was born, and his mother Aminah died when he was about six. His grandfather Abd al-Muttalib then cared for him until his own death about two years later, after which his uncle Abu Talib took him in.

whyNot.C: Abu Lahab was an uncle who later became a bitter enemy of Islam.
whyNot.A: Halimah nursed him in early childhood among the Banu Sa'd, before he returned to his mother.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Aminah, the mother of Prophet Muhammad (SAW), died on the way back from Yathrib (Madinah) at which place?
questions.explanation: Aminah took the young Muhammad to visit her relatives in Yathrib. On the return journey she fell ill and died at al-Abwa', a place between Madinah and Makkah, when he was about six years old.

whyNot.A: Ta'if is the town where the Prophet later preached and was rejected.
whyNot.C: Badr is the site of the first major battle, in 2 AH.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: When the Quraysh rebuilt the Ka'bah, the clans quarrelled over who should put the Black Stone back. How did Muhammad (SAW) settle the dispute?
options: He told them to cast lots among the clans
He placed the stone himself and refused to let anyone help
He asked the eldest man in Makkah to choose one clan
He placed the stone on a cloth and had a leader of each clan lift it together
questions.explanation: Before prophethood, at about age 35, Muhammad (SAW) spread out a cloth, set the Black Stone on it, and asked a leader from each clan to hold an edge and lift it together. He then set the stone in place with his own hands. Every clan shared the honour, and fighting was avoided.

whyNot.B: He involved all the clans; he did not shut them out.
whyNot.A: Casting lots was not used; his fair solution let every clan share the honour.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Who is regarded as the first martyr in Islam, killed in Makkah for refusing to give up her faith?
questions.explanation: Sumayyah, the mother of Ammar ibn Yasir, was tortured by Abu Jahl and killed because she would not abandon Islam. She is remembered as the first martyr (shahidah) in Islam.

whyNot.D: Khadijah was the first person to accept Islam; she died a natural death in Makkah.
whyNot.C: Asma' bint Abi Bakr helped during the Hijrah and lived to old age.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: The First Pledge of Aqabah (about 621 CE) was made to the Prophet (SAW) by a group of people from
questions.explanation: At Aqabah near Mina, twelve men from Yathrib met the Prophet during the pilgrimage season and pledged to worship Allah alone and to avoid theft, adultery and other sins. A larger pledge the next year prepared the way for the Hijrah to Yathrib.

whyNot.D: The people of Ta'if rejected the Prophet and drove him out.
whyNot.A: Abyssinia gave refuge to Muslim emigrants; it did not make the Aqabah pledges.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: In Madinah, the Prophet (SAW) paired each emigrant from Makkah with a helper from Madinah to share their homes and wealth. This arrangement is called
questions.explanation: After the Hijrah, the Muhajirun had left their property in Makkah. The Prophet joined each of them in brotherhood (mu'akhat) with one of the Ansar, who shared homes, work and goods with them. This built unity in the new community.

whyNot.A: Hilf al-Fudul was a pact for justice in Makkah before prophethood.
whyNot.D: Bay'at ar-Ridwan was the pledge under the tree at Hudaybiyyah in 6 AH.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: In which year of the Hijrah did the Muslims capture the fortified oasis of Khaybar?
questions.explanation: Khaybar, north of Madinah, was taken in 7 AH, soon after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah (6 AH). Its people, who had supported the enemies of the Muslims, agreed to keep farming the land and give half the produce.

whyNot.C: 2 AH is the year of the Battle of Badr.
whyNot.A: 5 AH is the year of the Battle of the Trench.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: The Prophet (SAW) delivered his Farewell Sermon during his only Hajj, in which year?
questions.explanation: The Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajjat al-Wada') took place in 10 AH. At Arafat the Prophet taught the sanctity of life and property, the rights of women, the equality of believers and holding fast to the Qur'an. He died in Madinah early in 11 AH.

whyNot.A: 8 AH is the year of the conquest of Makkah.
whyNot.D: 11 AH is the year the Prophet died, not the year of his Hajj.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Abu Bakr was chosen as the first caliph after the Prophet's death at a meeting held in
questions.explanation: When the Prophet died in 11 AH, the Ansar gathered at the Saqifah of Banu Sa'idah in Madinah. Abu Bakr, Umar and Abu Ubaydah joined them, and after discussion Umar pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr, followed by the others.

whyNot.D: The Cave of Thawr is where the Prophet and Abu Bakr hid during the Hijrah.
whyNot.A: The house of al-Arqam was a secret meeting place for Muslims in early Makkah.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: According to the well-known account, Umar ibn al-Khattab accepted Islam after hearing verses of which surah at his sister's house?
questions.explanation: Umar set out to harm the Prophet, but learned that his sister Fatimah and her husband had become Muslims. At their house he read the opening of Surah Ta-Ha, was moved by it, and went to the Prophet to accept Islam.

whyNot.B: Al-Baqarah was revealed in Madinah, years after Umar became a Muslim in Makkah.
whyNot.D: Al-Anfal was revealed after the Battle of Badr in Madinah.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Islam is said to have been firmly established in Kano by Wangarawa scholars from Mali during the reign of which Sarki?
questions.explanation: The Kano Chronicle records that Wangarawa (Mandinka) Muslim scholars and traders came from Mali in the time of Sarki Ali Yaji in the 14th century. He accepted Islam, a mosque was built and Muslim officials were appointed.

whyNot.A: Muhammad Rumfa ruled in the late 15th century and strengthened Islam that was already present.
whyNot.D: Bagauda is remembered as the legendary founder of the Kano dynasty, long before Islam came.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: In Yorubaland, Islam was traditionally called by which name?
questions.explanation: Yoruba people called Islam 'Esin Imale' and Muslims 'Imale'. The name is often linked with Mali, because the religion reached Yorubaland through traders and teachers from the north.

whyNot.D: Ifa is the traditional Yoruba system of divination, not Islam.
whyNot.C: Ogboni is a traditional Yoruba society.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Which Fulani Muslim scholar's son, Abdulsalami, became the first Emir of Ilorin?
questions.explanation: Shaykh Alimi, a Fulani preacher, settled in Ilorin and won a following there. After the fall of Afonja, Alimi's son Abdulsalami became the first Emir of Ilorin, which became an emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate.

whyNot.D: Usman dan Fodio led the jihad in Hausaland; his descendants ruled Sokoto, not Ilorin.
whyNot.B: Al-Kanemi led Bornu and opposed the jihad.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Which Songhai ruler, a great conqueror, is remembered as only a nominal Muslim who treated the scholars of Timbuktu harshly?
questions.explanation: Sunni Ali (ruled about 1464–1492) built up the Songhai Empire by conquest, taking Timbuktu and Jenne. He mixed Islam with traditional practices and persecuted some Timbuktu scholars. After his death, Askia Muhammad took power and strongly supported Islamic learning.

whyNot.C: Askia Muhammad was a devout ruler who promoted Islamic scholarship.
whyNot.B: Mansa Musa was a ruler of Mali, famous for his pilgrimage and support for learning.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Which of the following books was written by Shehu Usman dan Fodio to revive the Sunnah and condemn innovations?
questions.explanation: Ihya' as-Sunnah wa Ikhmad al-Bid'ah ('Reviving the Sunnah and Extinguishing Innovation') is one of Usman dan Fodio's best-known works. It explains correct practice according to the Sunnah and the Maliki school and criticises un-Islamic customs.

whyNot.B: Infaq al-Maysur was written by his son, Muhammad Bello.
whyNot.D: Riyad as-Salihin is a hadith collection by Imam an-Nawawi.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: The first major victory of Usman dan Fodio's followers over the army of Gobir, in 1804, was at the Battle of
questions.explanation: In June 1804 the small jihad force defeated a much larger Gobir army at Tabkin Kwotto (Lake Kwotto). The victory greatly raised the morale of the jihadists. Alkalawa, the Gobir capital, fell later, in 1808.

whyNot.D: Tondibi (1591) was where Moroccan invaders defeated Songhai.
whyNot.C: Alkalawa, the Gobir capital, was captured in 1808, not in the first victory.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Infaq al-Maysur, an important history of the Sokoto jihad, was written by
questions.explanation: Muhammad Bello, son of Usman dan Fodio and second ruler of Sokoto, wrote Infaq al-Maysur, a history of the jihad and of the lands of the Western and Central Sudan.

whyNot.A: Nana Asma'u is remembered for her poems and for educating women.
whyNot.C: Al-Kanemi was the leader of Bornu who opposed the jihad in letters.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Jama'atu Nasril Islam (JNI), an umbrella Islamic organisation in northern Nigeria, was founded in 1962 under the leadership of
questions.explanation: Sir Ahmadu Bello, the Sardauna of Sokoto and Premier of Northern Nigeria, led the founding of Jama'atu Nasril Islam in 1962 to unite Muslims, promote Islamic education and spread Islam.

whyNot.C: Nnamdi Azikiwe was a nationalist leader and Nigeria's first President, not a founder of JNI.
whyNot.D: Aminu Kano was a northern politician who opposed the Sardauna's party.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Writing the Hausa or Fulfulde language in Arabic script, a practice spread by Islamic learning in West Africa, is called
questions.explanation: Ajami is the use of Arabic letters to write African languages such as Hausa and Fulfulde. Scholars such as Nana Asma'u wrote poems in Ajami, which helped spread Islamic teaching to people who did not know Arabic.

whyNot.A: Tafsir is the explanation of the Qur'an.
whyNot.C: Tajwid is the set of rules for reciting the Qur'an correctly.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: The Ansar-Ud-Deen Society, which has founded many Muslim schools in south-western Nigeria, was established in Lagos in
questions.explanation: The Ansar-Ud-Deen Society was founded in Lagos in 1923 by young Muslims who wanted to give Muslim children modern Western education without losing their faith. It built many primary and secondary schools in the South-West.

whyNot.C: 1804 is the year the Sokoto jihad began.
whyNot.D: 1995 is the year NASFAT was founded in Lagos.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: In which surah does the Qur'an command kindness to parents and say, 'Do not say to them a word of disrespect (uff), nor scold them'?
questions.explanation: Qur'an 17:23–24 in Surah al-Isra' commands worship of Allah alone and goodness to parents. When they reach old age, the child must not say even 'uff' to them, must speak to them kindly and pray: 'My Lord, have mercy on them as they raised me when I was small.'

whyNot.D: Al-Kahf tells of the People of the Cave, Musa and al-Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn.
whyNot.B: Maryam tells the stories of Maryam, Isa, Yahya and other prophets.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Qur'an 49:12 forbids believers from three things in the same verse. Which of the following is one of them?
options: Marrying from the People of the Book
questions.explanation: Surah al-Hujurat 49:12 tells believers to avoid much suspicion, not to spy on one another and not to backbite. It compares backbiting to eating the flesh of one's dead brother.

whyNot.B: Trade is allowed in Ramadan; the verse does not mention it.
whyNot.D: Marriage to chaste women of the People of the Book is discussed in Qur'an 5:5, not forbidden in 49:12.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: How many verses (ayat) does Surah al-Fatihah have?
questions.explanation: Surah al-Fatihah has seven verses. The Qur'an calls it 'the seven oft-repeated (verses)' (as-sab' al-mathani) in Qur'an 15:87, because it is recited again and again in salat.

whyNot.B: Five verses is the length of the first revelation from Surah al-'Alaq.
whyNot.A: Al-Fatihah is counted as seven verses, not six.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Which surah tells that the Qur'an was sent down on a night that is better than a thousand months?
questions.explanation: Surah al-Qadr (Surah 97) says the Qur'an was sent down on Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Decree), which is better than a thousand months. On it the angels and the Spirit descend, and there is peace until dawn.

whyNot.B: Al-Layl swears by the night and contrasts the generous with the miser.
whyNot.D: Al-Fajr swears by the dawn and the ten nights and warns of past nations.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Surah al-Masad (also called al-Lahab, Surah 111) condemns which enemy of Islam and his wife?
questions.explanation: Abu Lahab was the Prophet's own uncle, but he and his wife fiercely opposed him. Surah al-Masad declares that his wealth will not save him and that his wife, 'the carrier of firewood', will have a rope of palm fibre around her neck.

whyNot.D: Abu Jahl was a fierce enemy, but he is not the subject of this surah.
whyNot.B: Abu Sufyan opposed Islam for years but later became a Muslim; this surah is not about him.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: According to Qur'an 2:185, in which month was the Qur'an sent down as guidance for mankind?
questions.explanation: Qur'an 2:185 begins: 'The month of Ramadan is the one in which the Qur'an was sent down as guidance for mankind.' The verse then makes fasting in that month obligatory.

whyNot.B: Muharram is the first month of the Islamic year, not the month of revelation.
whyNot.C: Dhul-Hijjah is the month of Hajj.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Which surah opens by swearing by the fig and the olive, Mount Sinai and 'this secure city', and states that man was created in the best form?
questions.explanation: Surah at-Tin (Surah 95) swears by the fig, the olive, Mount Sinai and the secure city of Makkah, then says Allah created man in the best stature, but he falls to the lowest of the low unless he believes and does good.

whyNot.B: Al-Balad also swears by the city of Makkah, but not by the fig, olive or Mount Sinai.
whyNot.D: Ash-Shams swears by the sun, the moon, the day and the night.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Surah ad-Duha (Surah 93) reminds the Prophet that he was an orphan and Allah sheltered him. What does it command in return?
options: Do not oppress the orphan and do not repel the one who asks
Fight those who mock the orphan
Adopt orphans as one's own children
Give all one's wealth to orphans
questions.explanation: Ad-Duha recalls that Allah found the Prophet an orphan and sheltered him, lost and guided him, poor and enriched him. So: 'As for the orphan, do not oppress him; as for the one who asks, do not repel him; and proclaim the favours of your Lord.'

whyNot.D: The surah forbids oppressing orphans; it does not require giving away all one's wealth.
whyNot.C: Adoption is not mentioned in ad-Duha.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Which surah twice repeats the comforting message 'Surely, with hardship comes ease'?
questions.explanation: Surah ash-Sharh (Surah 94) asks: 'Did We not expand your chest for you?' and then says twice: 'Surely, with hardship comes ease.' It comforted the Prophet during the hard years in Makkah.

whyNot.D: Al-'Asr teaches that mankind is in loss except those who believe and do good.
whyNot.B: Al-Qari'ah describes the terror of the Day of Judgement and the weighing of deeds.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Qur'an 3:7 divides the verses of the Qur'an into two kinds. What are the verses whose meaning is clear and decisive called?
questions.explanation: Qur'an 3:7 says some verses are muhkamat (clear and decisive), which are the foundation of the Book, and others are mutashabihat (allegorical), whose meaning is not immediately clear. Believers follow the clear verses and do not chase the allegorical ones to cause confusion.

whyNot.D: Mutashabihat are the allegorical verses, the opposite group.
whyNot.B: Makkiyyat refers to verses revealed in Makkah, a different classification.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: The Companions learned how to perform salat by watching the Prophet (SAW) pray. His actions in prayer are an example of
questions.explanation: Sunnah fi'liyyah is the Sunnah of the Prophet's actions. The Prophet said, 'Pray as you have seen me praying', so his actions in salat became the model for all Muslims.

whyNot.A: Sunnah qawliyyah is made up of the Prophet's sayings, not actions.
whyNot.D: Sunnah taqririyyah is the Prophet's silent approval of what others did.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Ibn Majah, compiler of one of the six major hadith collections, came from which city?
questions.explanation: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Majah al-Qazwini came from Qazwin in Persia. His Sunan is the sixth of al-Kutub as-Sittah.

whyNot.B: Bukhara was the birthplace of Imam al-Bukhari.
whyNot.A: Nishapur was the home of Imam Muslim.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: The Prophet (SAW) said: 'Jibril kept advising me to be good to the neighbour until I thought he would make him an heir.' What does this hadith teach?
options: Neighbours share in a Muslim's inheritance
Jibril brought new laws of inheritance
The rights of neighbours are very great in Islam
questions.explanation: The hadith, recorded by al-Bukhari and Muslim, shows how strongly Islam stresses kindness to neighbours: Jibril repeated the advice so often that the Prophet thought neighbours would be given a share of inheritance. In fact they were not; the point is the greatness of their rights.

whyNot.A: The Prophet only thought it might happen; neighbours were not made heirs.
whyNot.D: The hadith speaks of 'the neighbour' in general, not only Muslim neighbours.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: 'The best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it.' Which activity does this hadith most directly encourage?
options: Studying the Qur'an and teaching it to others
Building large mosques in every town
questions.explanation: This hadith, narrated by Uthman ibn Affan and recorded by al-Bukhari, places learning and teaching the Qur'an among the best of deeds. It encourages Qur'anic schools and teachers.

whyNot.D: Building mosques is rewarded, but it is not what this hadith speaks of.
whyNot.A: Decorating the Qur'an is not the teaching of this hadith.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Kemi writes insulting comments about her classmates on social media. Which hadith does her behaviour go against most directly?
options: 'A Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand other Muslims are safe'
'The best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it'
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) said a true Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand others are safe. Insulting people, whether in speech or in writing online, is harm done with the tongue, so Kemi's behaviour goes against this hadith.

whyNot.D: That hadith is about cleanliness, not harmful speech.
whyNot.C: That hadith lists the five pillars of Islam.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Alhaji Musa sells a used car but hides the fact that its engine is faulty. Which teaching of the Prophet (SAW) is he going against?
options: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honour his guest
Honesty about defects brings blessing to a sale; hiding them removes it
Pray as you have seen me praying
questions.explanation: In the hadith narrated by Hakim ibn Hizam (al-Bukhari and Muslim), the Prophet taught that honesty and openness about defects bring blessing to a sale, while concealment and lies remove it. Hiding the engine fault is concealment.

whyNot.B: That hadith is about hospitality to guests.
whyNot.A: That hadith is about controlling anger, not honesty in trade.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: A Muslim who met one or more Companions of the Prophet (SAW), but did not meet the Prophet himself, and died a Muslim is called a
questions.explanation: A sahabi met the Prophet as a believer. The next generation, who met Companions but not the Prophet, are the tabi'un (Successors). Many hadith reached later collectors through tabi'un.

whyNot.A: A sahabi must have met the Prophet himself.
whyNot.D: Muhajir describes those who migrated from Makkah to Madinah, who met the Prophet.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: A hadith in which a Successor (tabi'i) reports directly from the Prophet (SAW), leaving out the Companion who was in between, is called
questions.explanation: A mursal hadith is one where the Successor says 'The Messenger of Allah said…' without naming the Companion he heard it from. Because a link in the chain is missing, scholars differ on using it; Imam Malik accepted many mursal reports.

whyNot.C: A mutawatir hadith has a full chain with very many narrators at each level.
whyNot.B: Muttasil means the chain is connected, which is the opposite of mursal.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: 'Religion is sincere advice (an-nasihah).' The Companions asked, 'To whom?' The Prophet replied: 'To Allah, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims and their common folk.' This hadith was narrated by
questions.explanation: This hadith, recorded by Muslim and included in an-Nawawi's Forty Hadith (number 7), is narrated by Tamim ad-Dari. It teaches sincerity in faith and in dealings with leaders and ordinary people.

whyNot.A: Bilal is known as the Prophet's mu'adhdhin, not as the narrator of this hadith.
whyNot.C: Mu'adh ibn Jabal narrated other famous hadith, such as on being sent to Yemen.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: A Muslim employer in Aba keeps delaying his workers' pay at the end of each month. Which teaching of the Prophet (SAW) is he going against?
options: Smiling at your brother is charity
Seek knowledge even if it is far away
Give the worker his wages before his sweat dries
questions.explanation: The hadith recorded by Ibn Majah tells employers to pay workers promptly, 'before his sweat dries'. Delaying wages that are due is an injustice to the worker.

whyNot.C: That teaching is about purification.
whyNot.A: That teaching encourages kindness in everyday dealings, not prompt payment of wages.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Believing in Allah's names and attributes as He described Himself, without denying, distorting or likening them to creation, is called
questions.explanation: Scholars explain tawhid in three parts: rububiyyah (Allah alone is Lord and Creator), uluhiyyah (He alone is worshipped) and al-asma' wa as-sifat (His names and attributes are unique and affirmed as He described them).

whyNot.C: Tawhid ar-rububiyyah is about Allah as the only Creator and Sustainer.
whyNot.B: Tawhid al-uluhiyyah is about directing all worship to Allah alone.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: According to Islamic belief, which two angels question a person in the grave?
questions.explanation: Hadith teach that after burial, two angels called Munkar and Nakir ask the dead person: Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is this man who was sent to you? The believer answers correctly.

whyNot.A: Harut and Marut are the two angels at Babylon mentioned in Qur'an 2:102.
whyNot.D: Raqib and 'Atid record a person's words and deeds during life (Qur'an 50:18).

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: To which prophet was the Tawrah (Torah) revealed?
questions.explanation: The Tawrah was revealed to Prophet Musa for the Children of Israel. Muslims believe in it as an original revelation from Allah, along with the Zabur, the Injil and the Qur'an.

whyNot.D: The Injil was revealed to Isa.
whyNot.C: Sulayman was a prophet-king, but no book is named as revealed to him.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Belief in al-Qadar, one of the articles of faith, means believing that
options: Human beings create their own destiny without Allah
Fortune-tellers can know a person's future
Only bad events come from Allah
Everything happens by Allah's knowledge, will and decree
questions.explanation: Al-Qadar (divine decree) is the belief that Allah knows all things, has written them, wills them and creates them. Muslims still act, make choices and are responsible for their deeds, while accepting what Allah has decreed.

whyNot.C: Muslims believe in the decree of both good and bad, not only bad.
whyNot.B: Islam forbids believing fortune-tellers; only Allah knows the unseen.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: The second call made just before the congregation stands to begin the obligatory salat is called
questions.explanation: The adhan announces that the time of salat has come. The iqamah is a shorter call given just before the prayer starts, telling the worshippers to stand in rows.

whyNot.B: The adhan is the first call, made when the prayer time begins.
whyNot.A: Takbirat al-ihram is the 'Allahu Akbar' that opens the prayer itself.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: When a Muslim traveller shortens his prayers (qasr), which of these prayers is NOT shortened?
questions.explanation: Qasr reduces the four-rak'ah prayers (Zuhr, Asr and Isha') to two rak'ahs each. Maghrib has three rak'ahs and is prayed in full, and Fajr stays at two.

whyNot.A: Zuhr has four rak'ahs and is shortened to two.
whyNot.C: Isha' has four rak'ahs and is shortened to two.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Hajiya Amina's shop holds trade goods worth ₦2,800,000 (above the nisab) after a full lunar year. At 2.5%, how much zakat must she pay on the goods?
questions.explanation: Zakat on trade goods is 2.5% of their value after a lunar year. 2.5% = 2.5/100. ₦2,800,000 × 2.5/100 = ₦70,000.

whyNot.B: ₦140,000 is 5%, double the correct rate.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Qur'an 9:60 names eight groups who may receive zakat. Which of these is one of them?
options: Wealthy traders who need more capital
Debtors who cannot repay their debts
The zakat payer's own servants as wages
questions.explanation: Qur'an 9:60 lists the poor, the needy, those who collect zakat, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, freeing captives, debtors (al-gharimin), in the cause of Allah, and the stranded traveller. Debtors who cannot pay are one of these groups.

whyNot.B: Zakat is for those in need; wealthy traders are not among the eight groups.
whyNot.D: Paying one's own workers' wages is a duty of the employer, not a use of zakat.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: A man dies leaving a wife and children. After debts and funeral costs, his estate is ₦2,400,000. According to Qur'an 4:12, what is the wife's share?
questions.explanation: Qur'an 4:12 gives the wife one-quarter if her husband leaves no child, and one-eighth if he leaves a child. Here there are children, so her share is 1/8: ₦2,400,000 ÷ 8 = ₦300,000.

whyNot.A: ₦600,000 is one-quarter, the share when there are no children.
whyNot.B: ₦800,000 is one-third, which is not the wife's share.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: During Hajj and 'Umrah, pilgrims walk around the Ka'bah in the rite of tawaf. How many circuits make one tawaf?
questions.explanation: One tawaf consists of seven circuits around the Ka'bah, starting at the corner of the Black Stone and keeping the Ka'bah on the pilgrim's left.

whyNot.C: Three is the number of circuits in which men walk briskly (ramal) in the first tawaf, not the whole tawaf.
whyNot.A: Five is the number of daily prayers, not the circuits of tawaf.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Prophet Muhammad (SAW) belonged to which clan of the Quraysh tribe?
questions.explanation: The Prophet's great-grandfather was Hashim, and his clan, Banu Hashim, was a respected branch of the Quraysh. His uncle Abu Talib was head of the clan when the Prophet began preaching.

whyNot.A: Banu Umayyah was another Quraysh clan, to which Uthman and Abu Sufyan belonged.
whyNot.C: Banu Sa'd was the tribe of his wet nurse Halimah, not his own clan.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: How old was Muhammad (SAW) when he married Khadijah bint Khuwaylid?
questions.explanation: Khadijah, a wealthy trader, was impressed by Muhammad's honesty when he led her caravan to Syria. She proposed marriage, and they married when he was 25. She was his only wife until her death.

whyNot.C: 40 is the age at which he received the first revelation.
whyNot.B: 35 is about the age when he settled the dispute over the Black Stone.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: On a trading journey to Syria with his uncle Abu Talib, the young Muhammad (SAW) was recognised as a future prophet by which Christian monk?
questions.explanation: The well-known account says that at Busra in Syria the monk Bahira saw signs of prophethood in the boy Muhammad and advised Abu Talib to protect him.

whyNot.D: Waraqah ibn Nawfal, Khadijah's cousin, confirmed the first revelation in Makkah years later.
whyNot.A: An-Najashi was the Christian king of Abyssinia who protected Muslim emigrants.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Before his prophethood, Muhammad (SAW) took part in Hilf al-Fudul. What was this agreement?
options: A truce between the Muslims and the Quraysh
A pact among Makkan clans to support anyone who was wronged
A trade agreement with the Romans in Syria
An oath to defend the Prophet signed at Aqabah
questions.explanation: Hilf al-Fudul (the Pact of the Virtuous) was formed by some Quraysh clans after a visiting trader was cheated. They swore to stand with any oppressed person in Makkah until justice was done. The Prophet later said he would still join such a pact in Islam.

whyNot.A: The truce with the Quraysh was the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah in 6 AH.
whyNot.D: The Aqabah pledges were made by people of Yathrib after prophethood.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: From which hill in Makkah did the Prophet (SAW) first call the Quraysh publicly to Islam?
questions.explanation: After about three years of secret preaching, the Prophet climbed Mount Safa and called the clans of Quraysh. He warned them of a punishment ahead and called them to worship Allah alone. Abu Lahab rejected him there.

whyNot.B: Uhud is a mountain near Madinah where a battle was fought in 3 AH.
whyNot.D: Arafat is the plain of the standing during Hajj.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: The Quraysh boycotted the Banu Hashim, who were confined to the valley of Abu Talib in Makkah. About how long did this boycott last?
questions.explanation: The Quraysh agreed not to trade with or marry into the Banu Hashim and hung the agreement in the Ka'bah. The Prophet and his clan suffered hunger in the valley for about three years until the boycott ended.

whyNot.C: The boycott lasted years, not months.
whyNot.A: Ten years is longer than the boycott; it ended a little before the Year of Sorrow.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: After the deaths of Khadijah and Abu Talib, the Prophet (SAW) went to preach in which town, where he was rejected and stoned?
questions.explanation: Seeking support, the Prophet travelled to Ta'if, south-east of Makkah. Its leaders rejected him and set people to throw stones at him. Even so, he prayed that their descendants would worship Allah.

whyNot.B: Yathrib later welcomed him; he was not stoned there.
whyNot.D: Khaybar was a Jewish oasis north of Madinah, taken in 7 AH.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: When the Prophet (SAW) arrived in Madinah, in whose house did he stay while his mosque and rooms were being built?
questions.explanation: Many families invited the Prophet, so he let his she-camel walk freely. It knelt near the house of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, and the Prophet stayed with him for some months until the mosque and his rooms were ready.

whyNot.A: Abu Bakr was a fellow emigrant from Makkah, not a host in Madinah.
whyNot.C: Abdullah ibn Ubayy became the leader of the hypocrites.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: In 2 AH, the direction of prayer (qiblah) was changed from Jerusalem to
questions.explanation: For about sixteen or seventeen months in Madinah, Muslims prayed towards Jerusalem. Then Qur'an 2:144 commanded: 'Turn your face towards al-Masjid al-Haram.' Since then Muslims have faced the Ka'bah in Makkah.

whyNot.A: The Prophet's Mosque is a place of prayer, not the qiblah.
whyNot.B: Quba' was the first mosque built, but it is not the qiblah.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: As he lay dying, Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab arranged for his successor to be chosen by
options: A public vote of all Muslims in Madinah
A council (shura) of six leading Companions
questions.explanation: After he was stabbed in 23 AH, Umar named six Companions, including Uthman, Ali, Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, to choose one of themselves. They chose Uthman ibn Affan as the third caliph.

whyNot.A: Umar excluded his son Abdullah from being chosen as caliph.
whyNot.C: The governor of Syria, Mu'awiyah, had no role in this choice.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Shehu Muhammad al-Kanemi built which town as the new capital of Bornu in the early 19th century?
questions.explanation: After the Fulani jihadists sacked the old capital Ngazargamu, al-Kanemi helped defend Bornu and founded Kukawa (around 1814) as his base. It became the capital of Bornu.

whyNot.D: Ngazargamu was the earlier capital, sacked during the jihad.
whyNot.A: Njimi was the old capital of Kanem, east of Lake Chad.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: The Muslim organisation known by the initials NASFAT, founded in Lagos in 1995, is best known for
options: Translating the Qur'an into Ajami in Timbuktu
Organising prayer and Islamic programmes for educated, working Muslims
questions.explanation: Nasrul-Lahi-il-Fathi Society of Nigeria (NASFAT) was founded in Lagos in 1995 by young professional Muslims. It holds prayer meetings, runs schools and welfare programmes, and helps working Muslims practise their faith.

whyNot.C: The jihad was led by Usman dan Fodio from 1804.
whyNot.D: The Sokoto Caliphate is ruled by the Sultan, not by NASFAT.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Who is the President-General of the Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA)?
questions.explanation: The Sultan of Sokoto, as the leading traditional Muslim ruler in Nigeria, is the President-General of the NSCIA, the umbrella body for Muslims across the country.

whyNot.A: The Emir of Kano is an important emir, but he is not the head of the NSCIA.
whyNot.B: The Shehu of Borno is a senior traditional ruler, but the NSCIA is headed by the Sultan.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Which Sarki of Kano (late 15th century) built the Kurmi market and Gidan Rumfa, and introduced many Islamic reforms in his government?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Rumfa ruled Kano about 1463–1499. He built Kurmi market and his palace, Gidan Rumfa, extended the city walls and introduced Islamic laws and practices, guided by scholars such as al-Maghili.

whyNot.A: Ali Yaji ruled in the 14th century, when the Wangarawa brought Islam to Kano.
whyNot.C: Abdullahi Bayero was a 20th-century Emir of Kano.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Arab writers described Kumbi Saleh, the capital of ancient Ghana, as having two towns. What was special about one of them?
options: It was a Muslim town with mosques, where traders and scholars lived
It was a fort built by Moroccan soldiers
It was a town where only the king's priests lived
It was a Christian town ruled by Portuguese settlers
questions.explanation: Al-Bakri wrote in the 11th century that the capital of Ghana had two parts: the king's town and a separate Muslim town with several mosques, inhabited by North African traders and scholars. It shows that Islam reached Ghana through trade.

whyNot.D: The Portuguese reached the West African coast centuries later.
whyNot.B: Moroccan soldiers invaded Songhai in 1591, long after Ghana.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: The Adamawa Emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate is named after which flag bearer of Usman dan Fodio?
questions.explanation: Usman dan Fodio gave flags to leaders who would spread the jihad in different areas. Modibbo Adama received a flag for the lands of Fombina in the east and founded Yola as his capital; the emirate was named Adamawa after him.

whyNot.C: Abdullahi dan Fodio ruled the western part of the caliphate from Gwandu.
whyNot.A: Shaykh Alimi is linked with Ilorin, not Adamawa.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Al-Hajj Umar Tall, who led a 19th-century jihad in the western Sudan, was a leading figure of which Sufi order?
questions.explanation: Al-Hajj Umar Tall was appointed a leader (khalifah) of the Tijaniyyah order during his pilgrimage. He spread the Tijaniyyah in West Africa and visited Sokoto on his way back from Makkah.

whyNot.A: The Qadiriyyah was the order of Usman dan Fodio, not of Umar Tall.
whyNot.D: The Naqshbandiyyah is mainly found in Asia, not linked to Umar Tall.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: In traditional Qur'anic schools in northern Nigeria, pupils learn to write verses of the Qur'an on
questions.explanation: In the traditional makarantar allo, pupils write verses with ink made from soot or charcoal on a wooden slate (allo), memorise them, and then wash the slate clean for the next lesson.

whyNot.A: Clay tablets were used in ancient Mesopotamia, not in these schools.
whyNot.B: Mats are for sitting on; writing is done on the wooden slate.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria (as amended), which section provides for a Sharia Court of Appeal for any state that requires it?
questions.explanation: Section 275 of the 1999 Constitution provides that there shall be a Sharia Court of Appeal for any state that requires it. Section 260 provides one for the Federal Capital Territory. These courts hear appeals on Islamic personal law.

whyNot.D: Section 6 deals with judicial powers in general.
whyNot.A: Section 38 guarantees freedom of thought, conscience and religion.

questions.subject: islamic-studies
questions.stem: How did Islam mainly spread into south-western Nigeria before the 19th-century jihad?
options: Through Muslim traders and itinerant teachers from the north
Through Portuguese missionaries on the coast
Through a military conquest by Mali
questions.explanation: Islam reached Yorubaland peacefully, through Hausa, Nupe and Mande traders and wandering Muslim teachers (alfa) who came from the north. They settled in towns such as Oyo and later Lagos and won converts.

whyNot.C: Portuguese missionaries brought Christianity, not Islam.
whyNot.D: Mali did not conquer Yorubaland.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the sum to infinity of the geometric progression 12, 6, 3, …
questions.explanation: The first term is a = 12 and the common ratio is r = 6/12 = 1/2. Since |r| < 1, S∞ = a/(1 − r) = 12/(1 − 1/2) = 12/(1/2) = 24.

whyNot.B: 21 is only the sum of the first three terms, 12 + 6 + 3.
whyNot.D: 48 divides by r² = 1/4 instead of by 1 − r = 1/2.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: In how many different ways can the letters of the word OSOGBO be arranged?
questions.explanation: OSOGBO has 6 letters in which O appears 3 times and S, G, B once each. Number of arrangements = 6!/3! = 720/6 = 120.

whyNot.D: 720 = 6! treats the three O's as different letters.
whyNot.B: 360 = 6!/2! divides as if O appeared only twice.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the remainder when x³ + 2x² − 5x + 1 is divided by (x + 3).
questions.explanation: By the remainder theorem, the remainder on dividing by (x + 3) is P(−3) = (−3)³ + 2(−3)² − 5(−3) + 1 = −27 + 18 + 15 + 1 = 7.

whyNot.D: 31 is P(3); dividing by (x + 3) needs x = −3, not x = 3.
whyNot.B: −5 comes from treating −5(−3) as −15.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Solve the equation 3^(2x) − 4(3^x) + 3 = 0.
questions.explanation: Let y = 3^x, so 3^(2x) = y². The equation becomes y² − 4y + 3 = 0, i.e. (y − 1)(y − 3) = 0, so y = 1 or y = 3. Then 3^x = 1 gives x = 0 and 3^x = 3 gives x = 1.

whyNot.A: 1 and 3 are the values of y = 3^x, not of x.
whyNot.B: 3^x = 1 gives x = 0, not x = −1.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: P is the matrix with rows (1, 2) and (3, 4), and Q is the matrix with rows (2, 0) and (1, −1). Find the product PQ.

whyNot.B: This is QP; matrix multiplication is not commutative, so the order matters.
whyNot.A: This multiplies matching entries only, which is not matrix multiplication.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: A binary operation ∗ is defined on the set of real numbers by a ∗ b = a + b − 3. Find the inverse of 5 under ∗.
questions.explanation: First find the identity e: a ∗ e = a + e − 3 = a, so e = 3. The inverse y of 5 satisfies 5 ∗ y = 3: 5 + y − 3 = 3, so y = 1.

whyNot.D: −5 is the inverse of 5 under ordinary addition, not under ∗.
whyNot.A: 3 is the identity element, not the inverse of 5.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the values of k for which the equation x² + kx + 9 = 0 has equal roots.
questions.explanation: Equal roots need discriminant b² − 4ac = 0: k² − 4(1)(9) = 0, so k² = 36 and k = ±6.

whyNot.D: ±3 is the square root of 9, the constant term, not of 4 × 9.
whyNot.B: ±18 comes from 2 × 9 instead of √(4 × 9).

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: The third term of a geometric progression is 12 and the sixth term is 96. Find the first term.
questions.explanation: ar² = 12 and ar⁵ = 96. Dividing, r³ = 96/12 = 8, so r = 2. Then a × 2² = 12, so a = 3.

whyNot.A: 2 is the common ratio r, not the first term.
whyNot.D: 6 is the second term, ar = 3 × 2.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the coefficient of x³ in the expansion of (x² − 1/x)⁶.
questions.explanation: The general term is ⁶Cᵣ(x²)^(6 − r)(−1/x)ʳ = (−1)ʳ ⁶Cᵣ x^(12 − 3r). For x³: 12 − 3r = 3, so r = 3. The coefficient is (−1)³ × ⁶C₃ = −20.

whyNot.B: 20 forgets that (−1/x)³ carries a negative sign.
whyNot.A: 15 is ⁶C₄, the term independent of x (r = 4), not the x³ term.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: The sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic progression is Sₙ = n² + 2n. Find the 10th term.
questions.explanation: The nth term is Tₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁. So T₁₀ = S₁₀ − S₉ = (100 + 20) − (81 + 18) = 120 − 99 = 21.

whyNot.A: 120 is S₁₀, the sum of the first ten terms, not the tenth term.
whyNot.D: 23 is the 11th term, S₁₁ − S₁₀ = 143 − 120.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the gradient of a line perpendicular to the line 2x + 3y = 6.
questions.explanation: Rewrite 2x + 3y = 6 as y = −(2/3)x + 2, so its gradient is −2/3. Perpendicular gradients multiply to −1, so the required gradient is −1 ÷ (−2/3) = 3/2.

whyNot.A: −2/3 is the gradient of the given line itself.
whyNot.B: −3/2 takes the reciprocal but forgets to change the sign.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the magnitude of the vector 5i − 12j.

whyNot.D: 17 adds the components, 5 + 12, instead of using Pythagoras.
whyNot.C: √119 subtracts the squares, 144 − 25, instead of adding them.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the equation of the circle with centre (−2, 3) and radius 4.
questions.explanation: (x + 2)² + (y − 3)² = 16. Expanding: x² + 4x + 4 + y² − 6y + 9 = 16, so x² + y² + 4x − 6y − 3 = 0.

whyNot.A: This has centre (2, −3); the signs of the centre were not reversed.
whyNot.B: −16 forgets to add the 4 + 9 from completing the squares.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Given a = 3i + 2j and b = 4i − 5j, find the scalar (dot) product a · b.
questions.explanation: Multiply matching components and add: a · b = (3)(4) + (2)(−5) = 12 − 10 = 2. The dot product is a scalar, not a vector.

whyNot.C: 12 is only the product of the i-components; (2)(−5) = −10 must be added.
whyNot.D: −10 is only the product of the j-components.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the equation of the line through (2, −1) that is parallel to the line 3x − y + 4 = 0.
questions.explanation: 3x − y + 4 = 0 gives y = 3x + 4, gradient 3. A parallel line has gradient 3: y − (−1) = 3(x − 2), so y + 1 = 3x − 6 and y = 3x − 7.

whyNot.C: y = 3x + 7 has the right gradient but does not pass through (2, −1).
whyNot.B: Gradient −1/3 gives the perpendicular line, not the parallel one.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the coordinates of the foci of the ellipse x²/169 + y²/144 = 1.
questions.explanation: Here a² = 169 and b² = 144 with a > b, so the major axis is along the x-axis. c² = a² − b² = 169 − 144 = 25, so c = 5 and the foci are (±5, 0).

whyNot.D: The major axis is along the x-axis (169 > 144), so the foci lie on the x-axis.
whyNot.B: (±13, 0) are the ends of the major axis (vertices), not the foci.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: The points (1, 2), (3, 6) and (k, 10) lie on a straight line. Find the value of k.
questions.explanation: The gradient from (1, 2) to (3, 6) is (6 − 2)/(3 − 1) = 2. The gradient from (1, 2) to (k, 10) must also be 2: (10 − 2)/(k − 1) = 2, so k − 1 = 4 and k = 5.

whyNot.B: 4 is k − 1, the step before adding 1.
whyNot.C: 6 would give gradient 8/5, not 2.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the scalar projection (resolved part) of a = 2i + 3j in the direction of b = 3i + 4j.
questions.explanation: The scalar projection of a on b is (a · b)/|b|. a · b = 6 + 12 = 18 and |b| = √(9 + 16) = 5, so the projection is 18/5 = 3.6.

whyNot.C: 18/√13 divides by |a|; that is the projection of b on a.
whyNot.A: 18 is a · b alone, before dividing by |b|.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the values of c for which the line y = x + c is a tangent to the circle x² + y² = 8.
questions.explanation: The line x − y + c = 0 is a tangent when its distance from the centre (0, 0) equals the radius √8: |c|/√(1² + 1²) = √8, so |c| = √8 × √2 = √16 = 4. Hence c = ±4.

whyNot.A: ±2√2 is the radius itself; the distance formula also divides by √2.
whyNot.D: ±8 uses r² = 8 instead of r = √8.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: A is the point (1, 3) and B is the point (5, 7). Find the point P that divides AB externally in the ratio 3 : 1.
questions.explanation: For external division in the ratio m : n, P = (mB − nA)/(m − n). With m = 3, n = 1: x = (15 − 1)/2 = 7 and y = (21 − 3)/2 = 9, so P = (7, 9). Check: AP = (6, 6) is 3 times PB = (−2, −2) in length.

whyNot.A: (4, 6) divides AB internally in the ratio 3 : 1.
whyNot.C: (−1, 1) divides AB externally in the ratio 1 : 3, the ratio reversed.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Given that y = 5x³ − 4/x, find dy/dx when x = 2.
questions.explanation: Write 4/x as 4x⁻¹. Then dy/dx = 15x² + 4x⁻² = 15x² + 4/x². At x = 2: 15 × 4 + 4/4 = 60 + 1 = 61.

whyNot.C: 59 differentiates −4x⁻¹ as −4x⁻²; the power rule gives +4x⁻².
whyNot.A: 60 forgets the derivative of the −4/x term.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Evaluate ∫₁² (6x² − 4) dx.

whyNot.B: 6 subtracts +2 instead of −2 at the lower limit.
whyNot.D: 8 is the value at the upper limit only.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Differentiate y = 3 cos 2x with respect to x.
questions.explanation: d/dx(cos u) = −sin u × du/dx. With u = 2x, du/dx = 2, so dy/dx = 3 × (−sin 2x) × 2 = −6 sin 2x.

whyNot.C: The derivative of cos is −sin, so the sign must be negative.
whyNot.B: −3 sin 2x leaves out the factor 2 from the chain rule.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the minimum value of the function y = x³ − 12x.
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 3x² − 12 = 0 gives x = ±2. d²y/dx² = 6x is positive at x = 2, so x = 2 gives the minimum. y = 8 − 24 = −16.

whyNot.A: 16 is the maximum value, at x = −2.
whyNot.C: 2 is the x-coordinate of the minimum point, not the minimum value.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Evaluate the limit of (x² − 9)/(x² − x − 6) as x tends to 3.
questions.explanation: Factorise: x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3) and x² − x − 6 = (x − 3)(x + 2). Cancelling (x − 3), the limit is (3 + 3)/(3 + 2) = 6/5.

whyNot.D: 1 cancels the x² terms, which is not allowed.
whyNot.A: 5/6 turns the fraction upside down.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: The radius of a circular ink stain is increasing at 0.5 cm s⁻¹. Find the rate at which its area is increasing when the radius is 4 cm.
questions.explanation: A = πr², so dA/dr = 2πr. By the chain rule dA/dt = 2πr × dr/dt = 2π × 4 × 0.5 = 4π cm² s⁻¹.

whyNot.B: 8π is dA/dr at r = 4; it still has to be multiplied by dr/dt = 0.5.
whyNot.A: 16π is the area itself at r = 4, not its rate of change.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: A particle moves in a straight line so that its displacement after t seconds is s = 2t³ − 9t² + 12t metres. At what times is the particle momentarily at rest?
questions.explanation: Velocity v = ds/dt = 6t² − 18t + 12 = 6(t² − 3t + 2) = 6(t − 1)(t − 2). The particle is at rest when v = 0, so t = 1 s and t = 2 s.

whyNot.C: At t = 0 the velocity is 12 m s⁻¹, not zero; the particle is at rest only when v = 0.
whyNot.D: t = 1.5 s is when the acceleration is zero, not the velocity.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: The region bounded by the line y = 2x, the x-axis and the line x = 3 is rotated completely about the x-axis. Find the volume of the solid formed.
questions.explanation: V = π∫₀³ y² dx = π∫₀³ 4x² dx = π[4x³/3]₀³ = π × 4 × 27/3 = 36π cubic units. (This is a cone of radius 6 and height 3: (1/3)π × 36 × 3 = 36π.)

whyNot.A: 108π is the cylinder πr²h with r = 6 and h = 3; the solid is a cone.
whyNot.B: 18π squares x but not the 2: y² = 4x², not 2x².
whyNot.C: 9π integrates y = 2x instead of y² = 4x².

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the equation of the normal to the curve y = x² − 3x + 2 at the point (3, 2).
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 2x − 3, which is 3 at x = 3. The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so its gradient is −1/3. y − 2 = −(1/3)(x − 3) gives 3y − 6 = −x + 3, i.e. x + 3y − 9 = 0.

whyNot.D: 3x − y − 7 = 0 is the tangent at (3, 2), not the normal.
whyNot.B: x − 3y + 3 = 0 uses gradient +1/3; the normal's gradient is the negative reciprocal.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Using the substitution u = x² + 1, find ∫2x(x² + 1)³ dx.
questions.explanation: With u = x² + 1, du = 2x dx, so the integral becomes ∫u³ du = u⁴/4 + c = (x² + 1)⁴/4 + c. Check: differentiating gives 4(x² + 1)³ × 2x/4 = 2x(x² + 1)³.

whyNot.D: (x² + 1)⁴ forgets to divide by the new power 4.
whyNot.A: Dividing by 8 counts the factor 2 from du = 2x dx twice.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.context:
Scores of 20 pupils in a short quiz:
Score (x): 1, 2, 3, 4
Frequency (f): 3, 5, 8, 4
questions.stem: Using the frequency table, find the mean score.

whyNot.D: 2.5 is the mean of the score values 1, 2, 3, 4, ignoring the frequencies.
whyNot.A: 13.25 divides Σfx by 4 (the number of score values) instead of by 20.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Two fair dice are thrown together. Find the probability that the sum of the numbers shown is 7.
questions.explanation: There are 36 equally likely outcomes. A sum of 7 comes from (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1): 6 outcomes. The probability is 6/36 = 1/6.

whyNot.B: 7/36 puts the target sum on top instead of counting outcomes.
whyNot.A: 1/12 counts only 3 outcomes, missing the reversed pairs.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: A and B are events with P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.5 and P(A ∪ B) = 0.9. Find P(A ∩ B).

whyNot.B: 0.3 = 0.6 × 0.5 assumes A and B are independent, which is not given (and is false here).
whyNot.D: 1.1 is P(A) + P(B), before subtracting P(A ∪ B).

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: X has a binomial distribution with n = 3 and p = 0.2. Find P(X ≥ 1).

whyNot.D: 0.512 is P(X = 0); it must be subtracted from 1.
whyNot.C: 0.384 is P(X = 1) only; X = 2 and X = 3 are also included.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the variance of the numbers 4, 6, 9, 11 and 15.
questions.explanation: Mean = 45/5 = 9. Deviations: −5, −3, 0, 2, 6; squares: 25, 9, 0, 4, 36, total 74. Variance = 74/5 = 14.8.

whyNot.D: 18.5 divides by 4 (n − 1) instead of by n = 5.
whyNot.B: 74 is the sum of squared deviations, before dividing by 5.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: A committee of 3 is chosen at random from 4 men and 3 women. Find the probability that it contains exactly 2 women.
questions.explanation: Total choices: ⁷C₃ = 35. Exactly 2 women and 1 man: ³C₂ × ⁴C₁ = 3 × 4 = 12. Probability = 12/35.

whyNot.B: 18/35 is the probability of exactly 1 woman (³C₁ × ⁴C₂ = 18).
whyNot.A: 3/35 counts the women only and forgets to choose the man.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: X is normally distributed with mean 50 and variance 16. Find the standardised value z corresponding to X = 58.

whyNot.A: 0.5 divides by the variance 16 instead of the standard deviation 4.
whyNot.D: 8 is X − μ before dividing by σ.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: A bag contains 3 red and 2 green balls. Two balls are drawn at random, one after the other, without replacement. Find the probability that they are of different colours.
questions.explanation: P(red then green) = 3/5 × 2/4 = 6/20 and P(green then red) = 2/5 × 3/4 = 6/20. Total = 12/20 = 3/5.

whyNot.C: 3/10 counts only one order (red then green).
whyNot.A: 12/25 treats the draws as with replacement (2 × 3/5 × 2/5).

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: A random variable X takes the values 1, 2, 3 and 4 with P(X = x) = kx, where k is a constant. Find E(X), the expected value of X.

whyNot.D: 2.5 is the plain average of 1, 2, 3, 4, ignoring the unequal probabilities.
whyNot.B: 0.1 is the constant k, not E(X).
whyNot.C: 30 is Σx² before multiplying by k.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: In a large batch of oranges, 40% are sweet. Five oranges are picked at random. Find the probability that exactly 3 of them are sweet.

whyNot.A: 0.02304 leaves out the factor ⁵C₃ = 10.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Two forces F₁ = (3i + 4j) N and F₂ = (5i − 10j) N act on a particle. Find the magnitude of their resultant.

whyNot.A: 14 N adds the sizes of the components, 8 + 6.
whyNot.B: 2 N subtracts the components, 8 − 6, instead of using Pythagoras.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: A car accelerates uniformly from 10 m s⁻¹ to 30 m s⁻¹ in 5 seconds. Find the distance it covers in this time.
questions.explanation: For uniform acceleration, s = ½(u + v)t = ½(10 + 30) × 5 = 20 × 5 = 100 m.

whyNot.A: 150 m uses the final speed 30 m s⁻¹ for the whole 5 s.
whyNot.C: 50 m uses the initial speed 10 m s⁻¹ for the whole time.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: A force of 50 N pulls a box 8 m along level ground. The force acts at 60° to the direction of motion. Find the work done by the force.
questions.explanation: Work done = F × s × cos θ = 50 × 8 × cos 60° = 400 × 0.5 = 200 J. Only the component of the force along the motion does work.

whyNot.D: 400 J ignores the angle, using the full force.
whyNot.A: 346 J uses sin 60° instead of cos 60°.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: A stone is dropped from rest from a height of 45 m. How long does it take to reach the ground? (g = 10 m s⁻²)
questions.explanation: s = ut + ½gt² with u = 0: 45 = ½ × 10 × t² = 5t², so t² = 9 and t = 3 s.

whyNot.B: 4.5 s divides 45 by 10, as if s = gt.
whyNot.C: 9 s is t², not t.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: A block rests on a rough plane. The angle of the plane is slowly increased, and the block is just about to slip when the plane makes 30° with the horizontal. Find the coefficient of friction.
questions.explanation: At limiting equilibrium on the plane: friction μR = mg sin θ and R = mg cos θ, so μ = tan θ = tan 30° = 1/√3.

whyNot.A: √3 is tan 60°, the angle measured from the wrong line.
whyNot.C: 1/2 is sin 30°; μ equals tan θ, not sin θ.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: A ball is projected from level ground at 40 m s⁻¹ at an angle of 30° to the horizontal. Find its time of flight. (g = 10 m s⁻²)
questions.explanation: Vertical component of velocity = 40 sin 30° = 20 m s⁻¹. Time of flight T = 2u sin θ/g = 2 × 20/10 = 4 s.

whyNot.A: 2 s is the time to reach the highest point, half the flight.
whyNot.D: 4√3 s uses cos 30° instead of sin 30°.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: A uniform plank AB, 8 m long and weighing 200 N, rests horizontally on supports at A and B. A man weighing 600 N stands 2 m from B. Find the reaction at A.
questions.explanation: Take moments about B. The plank's weight acts 4 m from B and the man is 2 m from B: R_A × 8 = 200 × 4 + 600 × 2 = 2000, so R_A = 250 N. (Then R_B = 800 − 250 = 550 N.)

whyNot.D: 550 N is the reaction at B, which is nearer the man.
whyNot.A: 400 N shares the total 800 N equally, ignoring where the man stands.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: A ball of mass 2 kg moving at 6 m s⁻¹ hits a ball of mass 3 kg at rest. After the collision the 2 kg ball moves on in the same direction at 1.5 m s⁻¹. Find the velocity of the 3 kg ball.
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved: 2 × 6 + 3 × 0 = 2 × 1.5 + 3v, so 12 = 3 + 3v and v = 3 m s⁻¹.

whyNot.B: 4 m s⁻¹ gives all 12 kg m s⁻¹ to the 3 kg ball, forgetting the 2 kg ball keeps moving.
whyNot.C: 2.4 m s⁻¹ is the common velocity if the balls had stuck together.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: A particle of mass 3 kg lies on a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. It is joined by a light inextensible string over a smooth pulley at the top of the plane to a particle of mass 2 kg hanging freely. Find the acceleration of the system. (g = 10 m s⁻²)
questions.explanation: The hanging weight is 2g = 20 N. The component of the 3 kg weight down the plane is 3g sin 30° = 15 N. Net force = 20 − 15 = 5 N acting on a total mass of 5 kg, so a = 5/5 = 1 m s⁻².

whyNot.B: 4 m s⁻² ignores the 15 N component of weight down the plane.
whyNot.C: 7 m s⁻² adds the 15 N component instead of subtracting it.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: A car of mass 1000 kg moves on a level road against a constant resistance of 1000 N. Its engine works at 30 kW. Find its acceleration at the instant its speed is 10 m s⁻¹.

whyNot.A: 3 m s⁻² forgets to subtract the 1000 N resistance.
whyNot.D: 1 m s⁻² divides the resistance, not the net force, by the mass.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: In how many ways can a team of 3 players be chosen from 8 players?
questions.explanation: The order of choosing does not matter, so use combinations: ⁸C₃ = 8!/(3! × 5!) = (8 × 7 × 6)/(3 × 2 × 1) = 56.

whyNot.C: 336 = ⁸P₃ counts ordered selections, but a team has no order.
whyNot.D: 24 is 8 × 3, which is not a counting rule here.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Solve the equation log₃(2x + 1) = 2.
questions.explanation: log₃(2x + 1) = 2 means 2x + 1 = 3² = 9. So 2x = 8 and x = 4.

whyNot.D: 2.5 comes from 2x + 1 = 3 × 2 = 6, multiplying instead of raising to a power.
whyNot.A: 3.5 uses 2³ = 8 instead of 3² = 9.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the sum of the first 6 terms of the geometric progression 2 + 6 + 18 + …

whyNot.B: 486 is the 6th term, 2 × 3⁵, not the sum.
whyNot.C: 364 is (3⁶ − 1)/2, leaving out the first term a = 2.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: α and β are the roots of the equation x² − 3x − 5 = 0. Find the value of 1/α + 1/β.

whyNot.B: 3/5 takes the product of the roots as +5; it is c/a = −5.
whyNot.A: −5/3 turns the fraction upside down: it is αβ/(α + β).

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Given that (x − 2) is a factor of x³ + ax² − 4x + 4, find the value of a.
questions.explanation: By the factor theorem, P(2) = 0: 8 + 4a − 8 + 4 = 0, so 4a + 4 = 0 and a = −1.

whyNot.C: 1 comes from a sign slip when solving 4a = −4.
whyNot.D: −2 treats −4x at x = 2 as −4 instead of −8.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: The matrix with rows (x, 4) and (3, x + 1) is singular. Find the possible values of x.
questions.explanation: A singular matrix has determinant 0: x(x + 1) − 4 × 3 = 0, so x² + x − 12 = 0, i.e. (x + 4)(x − 3) = 0. Hence x = 3 or x = −4.

whyNot.C: x = −3 or x = 4 reverses the signs when reading roots from (x + 4)(x − 3) = 0.
whyNot.A: These do not make x(x + 1) equal to 12.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Which statement is the negation of "All the students passed the test"?
options: Only one student failed the test
At least one student did not pass the test
questions.explanation: "All passed" is false as soon as one student fails. So its negation is "At least one student did not pass" (equivalently, "Not all the students passed").

whyNot.A: "No student passed" is much stronger than the negation; both statements could be false together.
whyNot.B: "Only one failed" is one special case; the negation allows any number of failures from one upwards.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: The function f is defined by f(x) = (2x + 1)/(x − 3), x ≠ 3. Find f⁻¹(x).

whyNot.A: This is the reciprocal 1/f(x), not the inverse function.
whyNot.C: Signs were slipped when collecting the x terms.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Use the first three terms of the binomial expansion of (1 + x)⁵ to find an approximate value of (1.02)⁵.

whyNot.B: 1.100 uses only the first two terms.
whyNot.A: 1.0104 uses x = 0.002 in the second term.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Express (x + 7)/((x − 1)(x + 2)) in partial fractions.

whyNot.A: B is −5/3, not +5/3; at x = −2 the factor (x − 1) is −3.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the midpoint of the line joining (−3, 5) and (7, −1).

whyNot.C: (5, −3) halves the differences of the coordinates instead of their sums.
whyNot.A: (4, 4) adds the coordinates but forgets to divide by 2.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the gradient of the line joining the points (2, −3) and (6, 5).

whyNot.B: 1/2 divides the change in x by the change in y — the wrong way up.
whyNot.C: −2 treats 5 − (−3) as 5 − 3 with the wrong sign.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the centre and radius of the circle x² + y² + 8x − 2y + 8 = 0.
questions.explanation: Compare with x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0: g = 4, f = −1, c = 8. The centre is (−g, −f) = (−4, 1) and the radius is √(g² + f² − c) = √(16 + 1 − 8) = √9 = 3.

whyNot.D: The centre is (−g, −f); this forgets to change the signs.
whyNot.A: 9 is r², not the radius.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Given a = 2i + 5j and b = 4i + 3j, find |a + b|.

whyNot.A: 14 adds the components 6 + 8 instead of using Pythagoras.
whyNot.D: √29 + 5 is |a| + |b|, which is not |a + b| unless a and b point the same way.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the angle between the vectors 3i + 4j and 4i − 3j.
questions.explanation: The dot product is (3)(4) + (4)(−3) = 12 − 12 = 0. Since cos θ = 0/(5 × 5) = 0, θ = 90°: the vectors are perpendicular.

whyNot.C: 0° would need the vectors to point the same way, giving a dot product of 25.
whyNot.D: 180° would need opposite directions, giving a dot product of −25.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the line joining A(1, 2) and B(5, 6).
questions.explanation: The midpoint of AB is (3, 4). The gradient of AB is (6 − 2)/(5 − 1) = 1, so the bisector has gradient −1: y − 4 = −(x − 3), giving x + y − 7 = 0.

whyNot.C: x − y + 1 = 0 is the line AB itself, not its perpendicular bisector.
whyNot.A: x + y − 3 = 0 has the right gradient but does not pass through the midpoint (3, 4).

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: The ellipse x²/a² + y²/9 = 1, where a > 3, has eccentricity 4/5. Find the value of a.
questions.explanation: For an ellipse with a > b, b² = a²(1 − e²). So 9 = a²(1 − 16/25) = a² × 9/25, giving a² = 25 and a = 5.

whyNot.D: 4 is ae, the distance from the centre to a focus.
whyNot.C: 25 is a², not a.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the equation of the tangent to the circle x² + y² − 4x − 6y + 8 = 0 at the point (1, 1).
questions.explanation: The centre is (2, 3). The radius to (1, 1) has gradient (3 − 1)/(2 − 1) = 2, so the tangent has gradient −1/2: y − 1 = −½(x − 1), giving 2y − 2 = −x + 1, i.e. x + 2y − 3 = 0.

whyNot.B: 2x − y − 1 = 0 is the normal (it passes through the centre), not the tangent.
whyNot.A: 2x + y − 3 = 0 has gradient −2 instead of −1/2.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: The position vectors of A and B are OA = i + 2j and OB = 7i + 11j. P lies on AB with AP : PB = 1 : 2. Find OP.
questions.explanation: AB = OB − OA = 6i + 9j. P is one third of the way from A to B, so OP = OA + ⅓AB = (i + 2j) + (2i + 3j) = 3i + 5j.

whyNot.B: 5i + 8j divides AB in the ratio 2 : 1, the ratio reversed.
whyNot.C: 4i + 6.5j is the midpoint of AB.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the perpendicular distance of the point (1, −2) from the line 5x − 12y + 4 = 0.

whyNot.A: 33/17 divides by 5 + 12 instead of √(5² + 12²) = 13.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Given that y = 4x³ − 5x² + 7, find dy/dx when x = −1.

whyNot.B: 2 treats −10(−1) as −10.
whyNot.C: −22 forgets that (−1)² = +1.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Evaluate ∫₀¹ (x + 1)² dx.

whyNot.A: 8/3 uses (x + 1)³/3 at the upper limit only, forgetting to subtract 1/3 at x = 0.
whyNot.C: 1/3 integrates x² only, dropping 2x + 1.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Given that y = x⁴ − 2x³, find the value of d²y/dx² when x = 2.
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 4x³ − 6x², so d²y/dx² = 12x² − 12x. At x = 2: 48 − 24 = 24.

whyNot.B: 8 is dy/dx at x = 2 (32 − 24), the first derivative.
whyNot.C: 48 is only the 12x² term; −12x was dropped.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: Find the gradient of the curve y = (3x − 2)⁴ at the point where x = 1.
questions.explanation: By the chain rule, dy/dx = 4(3x − 2)³ × 3 = 12(3x − 2)³. At x = 1: 12 × 1³ = 12.

whyNot.D: 4 forgets the chain-rule factor 3 from differentiating 3x − 2.
whyNot.B: 3 forgets the power 4 that comes down.

questions.subject: further-mathematics
questions.stem: A particle starts from rest and moves in a straight line with acceleration a = (6t − 4) m s⁻² after t seconds. Find its velocity when t = 3.
